stories.title: Kali Sarkar, who held spiritual gatherings in UP, arrested:Wore army uniform, had followers from abroad and over 1 lakh Instagram followers
stories.summary: 'Kali Sarkar', also known as Pradeep Shukla, who held divine courts in Jhansi, was arrested in Hardoi on Tuesday. Police had been looking for him in a 31-year-old case. At a press conference at 4 p.m., police said that the records list the names Natroz and Kali Pandit alongside history-sheeter Pradeep Shukla. In Jhansi, he was known as Satyanand Shukla, alias Kali Sarkar. Two cases were registered against him at Kotwali City in 1993. Another case was registered against him in 1998. He had been absconding in this case. The Hardoi police had also arrested Kali Sarkar from his ashram on 10 October. The court had released him at the time because the old records were unavailable. He was arrested again after the records were rectified. Kali Sarkar wore an army-style uniform and held divine courts. He claimed to cure every illness. People came to his divine courts not only from across the country but also from abroad. He has more than 1 lakh followers on Instagram. Take a look at two pictures... Now, read the full story... Pradeep Shukla is a resident of Chauhan Thok in Kotwali city, Hardoi. He holds court at the Kali Sarkar temple in Kuraincha village, where he lives. A non-bailable warrant (NBW) had been issued against him by the Hardoi court for failing to appear in court in a robbery case. On 31 October, the Hardoi police went to the Mauranipur police station in Jhansi. From there, they went to the Kali Sarkar temple with Sub-Inspector Pranjal Singh, but Kali Sarkar was not there. Earlier, when the Hardoi police had taken Kali Sarkar away, Kuraincha resident Shivendra had brought him back under his custody. When Kali Sarkar could not be found, the police reached Shivendra's roadside eatery. The Hardoi police were taking Shivendra in their private car to obtain information from him about Kali Sarkar. Shivendra pushed the police and jumped out of the moving car. A case was later registered against him. Now find out how Kali Baba was exposed after 22 years... History-sheeter Kali Sarkar is accused in cases of robbery and assault. After fleeing Hardoi, he began living at the Kali Sarkar temple in Kuraincha village, under the jurisdiction of Mauranipur police station. There, he changed his name to Satyanand Shukla, alias Kali Sarkar. He also began holding a divine court while posing as a holy man. Hundreds of people would visit his court. He claimed to cure people's illnesses and resolve their other problems. Mauranipur CO Ratneshwar Singh had said, "Several cases have been registered against Pradeep Shukla. In 1993, the police arrested him in a robbery case and sent him to jail. Another case of assault was registered against him in 1998." He was not appearing in court in either case. The court subsequently issued permanent warrants against him. The Hardoi police had been searching for him for around 12 years. He was living in a temple under an assumed name Some time ago, the police learnt that the baba was in Jhansi. The police investigated and also traced his whereabouts. On 10 October, a joint team of the Hardoi and Mauranipur police raided the temple and detained Kali Sarkar Baba, alias Pradeep Shukla. The Hardoi police took him to Hardoi, where he received relief from the court. He subsequently returned to Jhansi. Case registered for sexual abuse of a child A man had accused Pradeep Shukla of sexually abusing his grandson. The grandfather told the police, "My grandson is 12 years old. He used to visit the Kali Sarkar temple in the village every day to offer prayers. The temple priest is Satyanand Shukla, whose real name is Pradeep Shukla, aka Natroj. He holds a darbar. As my grandson began visiting the temple regularly, Baba increased contact with him." He went to call the child to him on the pretext of giving him money, food and new clothes. A few days earlier, his grandson had not returned home. When he called, Pradeep, aka Natroj, said it was quite late and that he would send him in the morning. He did not send him in the morning either. He took his grandson to Haridwar. After that, he took him to Delhi and Lucknow. He sexually abused him there. Pradeep kept informing them of his location over the phone. When the grandson did not return for around four days, I told him that I would file a police complaint. The accused then arrived in Jhansi with the grandson on 22 October. He threatened and intimidated the grandson, warning that he would kill him if he told anyone anything. When he came home, the grandson began crying. When asked, he revealed everything the accused had done. The police had registered a case two days earlier. More than 1 lakh followers on Instagram Baba had created a page on Instagram under the name 'Kali Sarkar' around a year ago. It has more than 1 lakh followers. He used to hold a divine court on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. He also held one on Wednesdays for local people. At these courts, he claimed to cure every illness and resolve other problems. Kalī Sarkār issued a notice on social media informing people that the court would remain closed for nine days because of Navratri. However, the police arrested him on the first day of Navratri itself.

stories.title: Yogi says, 'Rahul ka dhuan nikla':Nitin Nabin says his launching pad itself is faulty; Muslims also attended the event in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath targeted Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav during the BJP's 'Save democracy, remove chaos' rally in Gorakhpur on Wednesday. He said the two leaders look for excuses after losing elections. Sometimes they blame EVMs and sometimes the SIR process, but they never accept their own failures. Yogi also questioned how many times the Congress would launch Rahul Gandhi. He said, "Rahul's fire has gone out." Will leave from MP Inter College at 12 noon; preparations continued throughout the day Nearly 50,000 people are expected to take part in the "Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy" march being organised by the BJP on 4 November. Party workers from the Gorakhpur region have been invited to join it. National president Nitin Nabin will attend as the chief guest. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive on Wednesday morning to take part in the march. State president Pankaj Chaudhary will also join the march. The march will cover around 2 kilometres and will conclude near the statue of Sardar Patel at Golghar Kali Temple. BJP leaders will garland Sardar Patel's statue. National president Nitin Nabin will reach the venue at 11 a.m. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive at around 9 a.m., before him. All the leaders will be present on the permanent stage set up at MP Inter College. The national president, chief minister and state president will address the workers gathered there. Buses have been arranged to bring people to the venue. Preparations continued throughout the day Preparations for the march continued throughout Tuesday. Water had accumulated on the grounds of M.P. Inter College because of the rain. Soil was spread to make the area suitable for walking. Tents have been put up in front of the permanent stage. BJP office-bearers remained there throughout the day. Senior office-bearers kept arriving and leaving to review the preparations. Unprecedented crowds expected, roads to be filled with party workers BJP regional president Vinod Rai said there would be an unprecedented crowd during the march. Workers have been called from all 12 organisational districts of the Gorakhpur region. They will all reach the venue by 10 a.m. The workers are highly enthusiastic about the event. The national president, the chief minister and the state president will address a public meeting here, after which the march will begin. Tomorrow, BJP workers will be seen on all the city's roads. Whenever the national leadership visits, a core committee meeting is held. A meeting of the state core committee has also been scheduled in Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Shami's brother gets protection from arrest by High Court:Accused of establishing a relationship on the false promise of marriage and issuing threats
stories.summary: The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court has stayed the arrest of Mohammed Kaif until 4 November in a case involving allegedly having sexual relations on the false promise of marriage and issuing threats. The court directed him to co-operate with the investigation. The order was passed by a bench of Justice Rajnish Kumar and Justice Zafar Ahmed on Mohammed Kaif's criminal writ petition. Kaif is the brother of Indian cricketer Mohammed Shami. The next hearing in the case will be held on 4 November. Lawyer calls allegations fabricated The petition challenges the FIR registered at Ashiyana police station on 13 September under Sections 69 and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Kaif's lawyer told the court that the allegations in the FIR were false and fabricated. He said Kaif had not made any promise of marriage. The opposing party's lawyer said the FIR contained the elements of a cognisable offence and should not be quashed. Contradictions in statements highlighted During the hearing, the state government said there were contradictions in the statements recorded from the victim under Sections 180 and 183. The statement under Section 183 contains an allegation linked to the Hotel Hyatt in Lucknow, while this is not mentioned in the FIR or the statement under Section 180. The government said most of the incidents in the case were connected to Delhi. On this basis, the investigating officer has sent a recommendation to senior officials to transfer the FIR to Delhi. For now, the matter is pending before the Lucknow Deputy Commissioner of Police. The government lawyer sought time to inform the court of the senior officials' decision on the recommendation. The court stayed Kaif's arrest until the next hearing and directed him to co-operate with the investigation.

stories.title: Temperatures drop by 4°C in UP in 24 hours:Fog covers 10 districts, including Lucknow; rain alert for the next 48 hours
stories.summary: Cold has set in across Uttar Pradesh. Temperatures fell by around 4°C over the past 24 hours. The chill has intensified in the mornings and evenings. Fog covered more than 10 districts, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Moradabad, Bijnor and Hapur, on Wednesday morning. The Meteorological Department has forecast rain in the districts of Purvanchal over the next 48 hours. According to BHU meteorologist Manoj Srivastava in Varanasi, the new storm 'Murasu', which has formed over the Bay of Bengal, is unlikely to have a direct impact on Uttar Pradesh. However, some parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh may see partly cloudy skies and rain on 5 November. The cold may continue during the day as well because of weak sunshine. 4 cities in Uttar Pradesh with the most polluted air Protect These Crops from Cold and Fog See the temperatures in Uttar Pradesh cities in graphics CM says: Provide immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken serious note of the damage to crops caused by excessive rainfall and the Arnab storm. He has directed all district magistrates in the state to go into the field and arrange an immediate assessment of crop damage. He also instructed them to provide immediate compensation for crop losses. During a public meeting in Gorakhpur, the CM said, "We will also bring a special package for farmers." Exercise caution while sowing and irrigating rabi crops In view of the possibility of rain in November, farmers have been advised to remain vigilant in managing rabi crops. In particular, during the sowing of wheat, gram, peas and mustard in Purvanchal, they should ensure that drainage arrangements in the fields are in good order. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where there is sufficient moisture due to rain. Decide on sowing and irrigation only after considering the weather conditions and moisture in the soil. October received 14% more rain than average According to the Meteorological Department, Uttar Pradesh received 32.1 mm of rain in October, against the average estimate of 28.2 mm. As a result, rainfall was 14% above average.

stories.title: Man kills married lover in Ghaziabad:She had come to meet him at his room; the two had connected on Facebook
stories.summary: A man killed his 28-year-old married girlfriend by repeatedly hitting her on the head with a brick in Ghaziabad. The woman had gone to his room with her sister on Monday night, where the two got into an argument. During the quarrel, the accused picked up a brick lying nearby and repeatedly struck her on the head. She collapsed on the floor, bleeding heavily. Hearing her screams, her sister, who was waiting outside the room, rushed in and found blood scattered across the floor. When the sister raised an alarm, local residents rushed to the spot. They caught the accused and his friend while they were trying to flee and handed them over to the police. The incident took place in Naipura Colony, under the jurisdiction of Loni Border police station. The deceased was identified as Pinky, 28, wife of Pramod and a resident of Bulandshahr. She had met the accused on Facebook around five months ago. They met on Facebook, then grew closer Pinky was a resident of Malkapur in Bulandshahr. The accused, Pintu (33), is a resident of Sheikhpur Garhwa village in Bulandshahr. The two met on Facebook five months ago. Initially, they chatted on Facebook. They then exchanged mobile numbers and began speaking on the phone. Their friendship gradually grew, and they started meeting. Pintu lived in a rented room in Naipura Colony. On Monday evening, Pinky went to meet him with her sister. Her sister stayed outside the room while Pinky went inside. The two had an argument over something in the room. Pintu allegedly killed Pinky after this. Accused was fleeing with a bag when people caught him Tenant Prateek Tyagi said, "Pintu had come to rent and live in the room with his friend Aryan Gupta alias Bunty (22) just five days earlier. After the crime, Pintu began fleeing the room with a bag. Pinky's sister, who was standing outside, became suspicious of his actions. When she entered the room, she found Pinky lying there covered in blood. She raised the alarm, prompting people from the surrounding area to gather. They caught Pintu and his friend Aryan and handed them over to the police." ACP Indrapuri Amardeep Maurya said, “We received information about a woman being murdered at the Indrapuri police outpost. The police reached the spot and conducted an investigation. Pintu and his friend are being questioned.”

stories.title: Pradhan shoots 2 men after losing in gambling:One dead in Ghazipur; anger erupted after he was mocked; wife says ‘He should be killed in an encounter’
stories.summary: A village head allegedly shot two young men with a country-made pistol after losing Rs 25,000 in a gambling game in Uttar Pradesh's Ghazipur district. One of the victims died, while the other sustained serious injuries. The village head was gambling with four or five young men and had staked Rs 25,000. When he began losing, the men playing with him made a joking remark, which angered him. He then opened fire on two of them. The incident took place late on Monday (9 Nov) night in the Sadar Kotwali area, around 7 km from the district headquarters. The deceased has been identified as 28-year-old Ajay Pasi. The accused, 35-year-old village head Sanjay Bind, surrendered at around 11 am on Tuesday. Ajay's wife said, "The accused should be killed in the same way as my husband was killed. He should be killed in an encounter." See 3 Photos... Opened fire after losing Rs 25,000 gambling bet Many people gather to gamble in Maharajganj Mohanw village, under the jurisdiction of Kotwali police station, on the day after Diwali. At around 10.30 pm on Monday, eight to 10 people were gambling near a pond in Pasipurwa, close to the village. Sanjay Bind, the head of neighbouring Bakrabad village, arrived with two or three companions and joined the game. According to eyewitnesses, Rs 25,000 was at stake. As Sanjay was on the verge of losing the amount, the other players made jokes about him. This angered the village head and led to a minor altercation. He then pulled out a country-made pistol and opened fire on two young men. One victim shot in abdomen, another in right hand City Circle Officer Anil Kumar said Ajay Pasi, a resident of Mohanw village, was shot in the abdomen, while his companion, 35-year-old Surendra Ram, a resident of Islamabad, sustained a bullet injury to his right hand. Both were rushed to the district hospital. As their condition was serious, doctors referred them to Varanasi for further treatment. Ajay Pasi died during treatment, while Surendra Ram remains under medical care. Village head surrenders at police station holding placard The village head fled after the incident. Following a complaint lodged by Ajay's elder paternal uncle, Shriram, the police registered a case against him and formed teams to track him down. However, at around 11 am on Tuesday, Sanjay Bind surrendered at the police station. He arrived carrying a cardboard placard that read: "I, Sanjay Bind, am surrendering." Ajay was the only brother among three sisters The injured Surendra is a mason. Ajay worked as a labourer with him. Both their homes are 800 metres from the scene, while the village head's home is two kilometres away. Ajay was the only brother among three sisters. He is survived by his wife, Aparna Paswan (26), and their three-year-old daughter, Lado. Aparna said, "My husband left home saying he would return in five minutes. He had no dispute with anyone." Won the village head elections in 2015 and 2021 Sanjay Bind was elected village head of Bakrabad village for two consecutive terms. He won the panchayat elections held in 2015 and 2021. Villagers said he was friends with several people in Mohांव village. He often visited the village. City CO Anil Kumar said two cases had already been registered against the village head. His other activities are also being investigated.

stories.title: Gorakhpur Zoo prepares for winter:Tigers and lions to get a new diet; bears to be fed honey and jaggery
stories.summary: With temperatures beginning to drop in Gorakhpur, the Shaheed Ashfaqullah Khan Zoological Park has started preparations to protect its animals from the winter cold. Like humans, wild animals also need special care as the weather changes. Keeping this in mind, the zoo administration will make necessary changes to their enclosures, food and water arrangements. Additional measures will be taken when temperatures fall sharply and cold waves set in. Tarpaulin sheets, screens and green nets will be installed around enclosures to prevent cold winds from entering. Heaters and blowers will also be used wherever necessary during severe cold. Tarpaulin sheets and green nets to protect enclosures Chief Veterinary Officer Dr Yogesh Pratap Singh said the zoo makes seasonal changes to animal care arrangements, just as people change their clothing and use heaters and blowers during winter. The first priority during colder weather is to make the enclosures safe and comfortable. Tarpaulin sheets, screens and green nets will be installed to block cold winds. Heaters and blowers will be arranged in areas where temperatures fall significantly. These measures aim to protect the animals from cold winds and the effects of extremely low temperatures. Tigers and lions to receive changes in their diet The diets of animals will also be adjusted according to their seasonal requirements. The quantity of meat given to carnivores, particularly tigers and lions, will be modified as needed. Dr Singh said their feeding arrangements are managed according to the weather and individual requirements. Herbivorous animals will be given energy-rich food during winter. Their diets will be adjusted according to the needs of each species to ensure that the cold weather does not adversely affect their health. Bears to be fed honey, jaggery and gram Special attention will also be given to the diet of bears during winter. Honey, jaggery and gram will be included in their food. Some herbivorous animals will also be given sweet potatoes, sugarcane and oilseed cake, wherever required. The zoo administration will provide different food items according to the nature and nutritional requirements of each animal. Officials said all animals are not given the same diet, as their food is determined by their physical needs and prevailing weather conditions. Bonfires to be arranged safely during cold waves As temperatures drop further and cold waves intensify, additional arrangements will be made to keep the animals warm. Bonfires will also be arranged at safe locations wherever necessary. Enclosures exposed to cold winds will be covered with tarpaulin sheets and other protective materials. Heaters and blowers will also be used as required. Necessary seasonal changes will also be made to the upkeep of deer and other animals. Pond water to be refreshed for aquatic animals Special arrangements will also be made for aquatic animals living at the zoo. Particular attention will be paid to water management in the ponds housing hippopotamuses, crocodiles, gharials and turtles. Dr Singh said a drop in water temperature can cause discomfort to these animals. To manage the water conditions, fresh water is continuously added to the ponds from one side, while old water is drained from the other. This process ensures regular water replacement and helps maintain a suitable environment for aquatic animals. Care arrangements to vary according to each animal Dr Singh said the zoo focuses on two key aspects of animal care: food and enclosure management. Both are adjusted according to changing weather conditions and the requirements of individual species. Animals that need additional warmth will receive suitable arrangements in their enclosures, while energy-rich food will be added to the diets of those that require it. Aquatic animals will receive separate water-management arrangements. The zoo administration aims to ensure that all animals remain healthy and safe, without discomfort, as temperatures fall and cold waves affect the region.

stories.title: Siberian birds arrive in Varanasi from Russia:Migratory visitors attract tourists; Ganga ghats buzz with selfie and reel enthusiasts
stories.summary: Varanasi, the city of Baba Vishwanath, takes on a special charm during winter. Morning fog over the Ganga ghats, cold winds, cups of hot tea and thousands of white birds floating on the river create a picturesque scene. It almost looks as if Siberia has arrived at the ghats of Kashi. As every year, thousands of migratory birds have travelled thousands of kilometres to reach the banks of the Ganga. They began arriving in the first week of November and are expected to stay until February, attracting tourists and visitors who are keen to take selfies and make reels. Birds escape temperatures as low as -60°C These beautiful white birds, seen swimming in the Ganga and flying in large flocks across the sky, are commonly known as Siberian birds. Their white bodies, orange beaks and orange feet make them a major attraction for tourists. During winter, temperatures in Siberia can drop to between -50°C and -60°C. To escape the extreme cold, these birds fly thousands of kilometres to reach relatively warmer parts of India. Migratory birds reach Kashi via Pakistan According to Professor Chandana Haldar, the distance between India and Siberia is approximately 4,400 kilometres. The migratory birds follow different routes to reach India, travelling through several European countries as well as Afghanistan, Mongolia, China and Bhutan. Another group travels through Pakistan and Rajasthan before reaching Prayagraj and then Varanasi. During this long journey, the birds face several challenges, including changing weather conditions, food availability and natural obstacles. What does the scientist say? These migratory birds stay in Kashi for around four months. During their stay, they swim in the Ganga and also breed in the sandy areas across the river, where they lay their eggs. In March, as the winter chill begins to fade, they return to their natural habitats along with their young ones. According to Chandana Haldar, the natural environment of Kashi is suitable for their breeding, and the birds also find sufficient food here. However, their numbers are considerably lower this November compared with previous years. Climate change is believed to be one of the reasons why many migratory birds have not yet arrived in Kashi. Bread and savoury snacks offered by tourists can harm birds After reaching Kashi, the migratory birds face another challenge. Tourists visiting the ghats often feed them bread, savoury snacks and puffed rice out of affection. However, these food items can be harmful to the birds' health. Increasing pollution in the Ganga is also a threat to their survival. As a result, several birds die during their stay in Kashi, while others lose their lives during the return journey.

stories.title: Gorakhpur-Pune special trains to run on November 10 and 17:Chhath passengers to benefit; Yeshwantpur Express gets a halt at Pukhrayan
stories.summary: In view of the rising number of passengers travelling after Diwali for Chhath Puja, the Railways has announced two important measures. A special train festival will run from Gorakhpur to Hadapsar in Pune on November 10 and 17. In another move, the Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express will make a trial halt at Pukhrayan station. The decisions are expected to benefit passengers travelling to Pune and southern India. The special train will make two trips in each direction. Train to depart from Gorakhpur at 9.55 pm According to the timetable released by the Railways, train number 05093, Gorakhpur-Hadapsar Festival Special, will depart from Gorakhpur at 9.55 pm on November 10 and 17. It will reach Basti at 11.12 pm, Mankapur at 12.04 am the following day and Gonda at 12.30 am. It will then halt at Lucknow at 2.45 am and Kanpur Central at 4.35 am. The train will depart from Orai at 6 am, Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi at 8.15 am and Bina at 12.05 pm. It will reach Bhopal at 2.15 pm, Itarsi at 4.20 pm, Khandwa at 7.08 pm and Bhusaval at 9.05 pm. On the third day, it will travel via Manmad, Kopargaon, Belapur, Ahilyanagar and the Daund chord line before reaching Hadapsar at 7.30 am. Return train to leave Hadapsar at 10.05 am Train number 05094, Hadapsar-Gorakhpur Festival Special, will depart from Hadapsar at 10.05 am on November 12 and 19. It will reach the Daund chord line at 11.12 am, Ahilyanagar at 12.32 pm, Belapur at 2.30 pm and Kopargaon at 3.24 pm. The train will then depart from Manmad at 4.15 pm, Bhusaval at 7 pm and Khandwa at 9.50 pm. The following day, it will halt at Itarsi at 12.20 am, Bhopal at 2.25 am and Bina at 4.30 am. It will travel via Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi, Orai, Kanpur Central, Lucknow, Gonda, Mankapur and Basti before reaching Gorakhpur at 7 pm. Special train to have 20 coaches According to the Railways, the special train will have 20 coaches, including: Yeshvantpur Express to stop at Pukhrayan The Railways has also decided to introduce a trial halt for the Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express at Pukhrayan station under the North Central Railway. Train number 15023, Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express, will arrive at Pukhrayan at 6.58 pm from November 10 and depart at 7 pm. Similarly, train number 15024, Yeshvantpur-Gorakhpur Express, will arrive at Pukhrayan at 9.47 am from November 12 and depart at 9.49 am. The additional halt is expected to make travel between Gorakhpur and southern India more convenient for passengers from Pukhrayan and nearby areas.

stories.title: Businessman kills wife in Shahjahanpur:Tries to strangle one daughter; second daughter locks herself in a room to save her life
stories.summary: A businessman allegedly strangled his wife to death in Uttar Pradesh's Shahjahanpur district. He also tried to strangle their 11-year-old daughter. Terrified by her father's actions, their 16-year-old daughter locked herself inside a room and saved her life. The incident took place at around 1 am on Monday night (9 Nov). The elder daughter called her uncle from inside the locked room, following which he alerted the police. The mother and the younger daughter were rushed to a medical college, where the mother died during treatment. The 11-year-old girl is in critical condition and has been admitted to the ICU. Accused arrested from house, police say he did not flee The accused, identified as Kamlesh, did not flee after the incident and was still at home when the police arrived. He was arrested at the scene. The incident took place in Adarsh Nagar Colony, under the jurisdiction of Roza police station, around 10 km from the district headquarters. See two pictures Now understand the full case Kamlesh is reportedly living with his wife Seema (40) and daughters Komal, also known as Ananya (16), and Anjali (11). Kamlesh lived on the upper floor, while his family members lived downstairs. He has an electronics shop nearby. Kamlesh is reportedly under stress over his business these days. He also has a debt of lakhs of rupees. The husband and wife quarrelled over this at around 12:30 a.m. Kamlesh then began assaulting his wife and children. He knocked his wife to the floor and then strangled her to death. During this, he also strangled and tried to kill his younger daughter Anjali, who had come to save her mother. He then tried to attack his elder daughter Komal as well. However, she fled and locked herself in a room, saving her life. People living downstairs arrived after hearing the elder daughter's screams. Father says he never saw his son and daughter-in-law quarrel Accused Kamlesh's father, Ramesh Chandra Gupta, said, "We live downstairs in the house, while my son Kamlesh lives on the terrace with his family. There was no dispute between my son and daughter-in-law. If there had been any problem, he would have told me. I do not know what happened between them that Kamlesh took such a step." Brother says sister did not mention the quarrel Deceased Seema's brother Ashok said he had spoken to his sister on the phone on Monday evening, but she had not mentioned anything resembling a dispute. He said it did not seem from their conversation that she was troubled. This morning, he received a call telling him to come to the hospital quickly. He then spoke to his elder niece, who told him that her father had killed her mother. SP City Devendra Singh said, “Preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused committed the crime while under the influence of alcohol. He strangled his wife to death and also tried to kill his daughter by strangling her. The accused has been arrested and is being questioned.”

stories.title: Model Shraddha offers prayers morning and evening in jail:Has started interacting with other inmates; no family member has visited her so far
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, an accused in the murder case of Lucknow chicken trader Shiva Sharma, is spending her time in jail through yoga and spiritual activities. Prayers and yoga sessions in the morning and evening have become part of her daily routine. During the rest of the day, she talks to her sister Rashmi and other women inmates in the barrack. The change in her behaviour has been observed since her judicial custody was extended. Her custody was extended by 14 days on October 31 and is due to end on November 13. So far, no family member or acquaintance has visited her in jail. She has met her lawyer only twice. After businessman Shiva died on October 9, Shraddha allegedly fled with her sister Rashmi and driver Danish. After remaining on the run for 12 days across Nepal, Rae Bareli, Lucknow and Agra, she was arrested in Nagpur on October 22. See 3 pictures... Shraddha stays with her sister in jail According to jail sources, Shraddha has settled into a regular routine. She spends her mornings and evenings doing yoga, praying and engaging in spiritual activities. During the day, she talks to other women inmates in the barrack. Her sister Rashmi stays with her. Acting Senior Superintendent of Jail Rithvik Priyadarshi said Shraddha, Rashmi and their driver Tanveer were being treated like other inmates. All three are following the jail's prescribed routine. Both sisters initially appeared restless in jail For the first 24 hours after entering jail, Shraddha and Rashmi did not speak to anyone. However, they repeatedly asked questions of the deputy jailer assigned to monitor them. The sisters were lodged in a barrack housing 40-45 women inmates. According to jail sources, both were distressed by the sudden loss of their luxurious lifestyle. They reportedly kept walking around the barrack. However, their behaviour gradually changed. After losing hope of getting out of jail soon, they began spending time with and talking to other inmates. Shraddha's Instagram followers increase, following decreases After Shraddha's name surfaced in the Shiva Sharma murder case, her Instagram account became a major talking point. She maintained a public profile and regularly shared updates. Her follower count has also attracted attention. Following the incident, her followers increased from 1.41 lakh to 1.44 lakh. At the same time, the number of accounts she follows decreased from 421 to 404. It is being claimed that some VIP profiles were either blocked from her account or unfollowed by Shraddha after the incident. However, this claim has not been independently established. What is the Shiva Sharma murder case? On October 9, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow's Hazratganj area. He had reportedly been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the previous four months. At the time, Shiva's body was reportedly found wearing only underwear. Lipstick marks were found on his face, while several cigarette-burn marks were also noticed on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, filed a murder case against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Adil, in connection with his death. She alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. The three accused are currently lodged in Lucknow jail.

stories.title: Lawyers hold dance and poetry session inside Prayagraj police station:Stage sit-in with beds, chairs, tables and loudspeakers; demand accused person's arrest
stories.summary: Eight lawyers have been staging a sit-in protest at the Civil Lines police station in Prayagraj for the past four days, demanding the arrest of an agent accused of cheating a lawyer of ₹70,000 on the pretext of arranging vehicle finance. The lawyers have adopted an unusual style of protest. They dance to songs such as 'Naka Bandi' and 'Hum Pagal Nahi Hain Bhaiya, Hamara Dimaag Kharab Hai'. They have now started reciting ghazals and poetry over a microphone. Before reciting a verse, they announce, "Station House Officer, this one is for you." The lawyers have set up camp outside the police station, spreading mats, mattresses, bedsheets and mosquito nets. They have also arranged chairs, tables, a microphone and loudspeakers. They continued their protest at the police station even during Diwali and the following day, known as Parewa, without returning home. See 3 pictures... How did the dispute begin? Lawyer Brijesh Tiwari was allegedly cheated on the pretext of arranging vehicle finance. According to the complaint, an agent took ₹70,000 from him but fled without depositing the money with the finance company. An FIR was registered at the Civil Lines police station in connection with the incident. The lawyers allege that the police took no action against the accused despite registering the case. Angered by the alleged inaction, Brijesh Tiwari arrived at the police station with fellow lawyers on November 7, carrying mats and bedding, and began a sit-in protest. They later arranged chairs, tables, a microphone and loudspeakers. Lawyers refuse to end protest until agent is arrested The police have repeatedly tried to persuade the lawyers to call off their protest, but they have refused to budge. They say the sit-in will continue until the agent is arrested.

stories.summary: Three friends died on the spot and one was critically injured after a speeding Thar hit their motorcycle in Kannauj late on Monday night. All four men were travelling on the same bike. The man riding the motorcycle was not wearing a helmet. Eyewitnesses said the Thar was travelling at around 100-120 kmph. It hit the motorcycle head-on with such force that all four men were thrown 15-20 metres away. The motorcycle was completely wrecked. The Thar driver did not stop after the accident and sped away. Police reached the spot after receiving information, collected the bodies and sent them for post-mortem examinations. The injured man has been referred to Kanpur for treatment. The accident took place in the Indergarh police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Manish Kumar (28), Ved Prakash (40) and Vijay (35). The injured man is yet to be identified. All four were residents of Agaus village. Thar driver collided with them while driving on the wrong side Villagers who reached the spot after receiving information about the accident said, "The four youths riding the motorcycle had left home at around 11:20 p.m. They had just reached the front of Kachatipur College when the Thar driver came from the wrong side and collided with them." Hearing cries for help after the accident, local residents and passers-by reached the spot. The police were informed, but by then three of the youths had died. The police sent one of them to hospital by ambulance. This report is being continuously updated...

stories.title: Fog covers 15 UP cities, air quality worsens in Noida-Ghaziabad:AQI crosses 300; dense fog tomorrow, colder weather in 2 days
stories.summary: Fog and haze have increased across Uttar Pradesh after Diwali. Dense fog covered 15 cities, including Sambhal, Hapur, Bijnor and Shamli, on Tuesday morning. Visibility dropped to just 10-20 metres in some areas, making it difficult to see even a short distance ahead. Air pollution has also increased due to Diwali firecrackers. On Monday evening, Noida recorded an AQI of 332, followed by Bulandshahr at 331, Ghaziabad at 324 and Baghpat at 305. Meanwhile, temperatures in the state have dropped below 15°C. Hardoi recorded a minimum temperature of 14.5°C, while Kanpur recorded 14.6°C, making them the coldest places in the state. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for dense fog across Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. Severe cold is likely to increase in the state after two days. Prof. Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at BHU in Varanasi, said, "As dry north-westerly winds become stronger, minimum temperatures will fall further. This will make the cold more intense." Know the situation in the major cities- Know the temperature over the past 24 hours What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the level of pollutants present in the air. As the AQI rises, the air is considered increasingly dangerous and the health risk also increases. Understand it from the graphic below: How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone present in the air reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate issues to long-term conditions. Continuous exposure reduces lung capacity and increases the risk of chronic diseases. Understand this through the graphic below:

stories.title: Former SP leader opens fire:Celebrates family's acquittal in Gonda; claims it was a gun used to scare away monkeys
stories.summary: Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari and his family members opened fire during Diwali celebrations in Gonda. He recorded a video of the firing and posted it on his Facebook account. The video surfaced at around 3:30 pm on Monday. It shows eight people, including Tiwari, taking turns to fire a gun. Around 15 days ago, Tiwari's family members were acquitted in an old case. The firing was reportedly carried out to celebrate their acquittal. The incident took place in the Nawabganj police station area, around 40 km from the district headquarters. Check out visuals below : Read the full story below : Abhishek Tiwari (28), who lives in Lauwwa Veerpur village, is active in student politics. His parents are also part of his family. Abhishek joined the Samajwadi Party on 9 November 2024. He was later appointed district general secretary of the Samajwadi Party's Lohia Vahini. However, he was removed from the post on 25 February 2025 for making objectionable remarks against SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and engaging in anti-party activities. He was also expelled from the party. Eight people, including a girl, opened rapid fire In the viral video, six young men are seen firing guns one after another. The seventh person, a middle-aged man, and the eighth, a girl aged around 19, are also seen firing guns. He shared the video with a post on Facebook Abhishek Tiwari shared the video on Facebook and wrote, "After a long 25-year struggle and wait, justice has finally prevailed. This is the first Diwali after my family members were honourably acquitted, when all the members of the family are together." This time, lamps are being lit not only in homes but also in the hearts of those who faced darkness and suffering for many years. It is a celebration of the victory of justice, patience and the family. However, after the video went viral, Abhishek Tiwari removed the post from Facebook. Dainik Bhaskar does not verify this viral video. Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari said that he has a crow gun, which is used to drive away monkeys. There are a large number of monkeys in his area. For this reason, members of the family had fired the gun. He claimed that it was not a real gun. Former Samajwadi Party leader says-fired crow gun to drive away monkeys Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari said, "I have a crow gun. It is used to drive away monkeys." "There are a large number of monkeys in my area. For this reason, members of the family had fired the gun. It is not a real gun." Nawabganj Station House Officer Mrityunjay Singh said: “The matter is being investigated seriously. Strict legal action will be taken against the accused based on the findings of the investigation.”

stories.title: 'Ayodhya will become the global capital of Sanatan tourism':Akhilesh says temple theft row has reduced devotees affected business
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav has targeted the BJP government over the situation in Ayodhya. He claimed that the number of devotees visiting the city was falling after the controversy over the alleged theft at the Ram temple. He said this was also affecting local businesses. Akhilesh said that if the Samajwadi Party forms the government, it will restore Ayodhya's honour and bring transparency to temple management. He promised to develop world-class facilities and make Ayodhya the "global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage". Akhilesh shared his vision for Ayodhya in a detailed social media post. He raised issues related to temple management, tourism, local businesses, employment for boatmen, ration supplies for the poor and alleged land scams. He said the city's religious identity and the interests of local people would be given priority. Ram temple management to be made transparent Akhilesh said the controversy over the alleged theft at the Ram temple had hurt the feelings of devotees. He claimed that the fall in the number of pilgrims was affecting the local economy. He said an open and transparent system would be introduced for temple management to restore people's trust. He also promised world-class facilities for pilgrims visiting Ayodhya from across the country and abroad. He said the city would be developed as a major centre for religious tourism. Boatmen to get employment, Nishadraj's bond with Lord Ram to be highlighted Akhilesh promised to promote traditional boating in Ayodhya to provide employment to local boatmen. He said this would also help bring back the close bond between Lord Ram and Nishadraj. He accused the BJP of weakening this historic relationship. Akhilesh said the BJP's politics of dominance did not want people to remember the story of Lord Ram embracing members of the PDA community. Ayodhya to be freed from outside contractors The SP president also raised questions about the role of outsiders in land deals and construction work in Ayodhya. He said the land would be investigated and the city would be freed from outside contractors. Referring to an alleged scam involving circle rates, Akhilesh said BJP leaders and officials involved in corruption would not be spared. He alleged that outsiders had taken advantage of Ayodhya while ignoring the interests of local people. Oil and ghee to be included in ration for poor families Akhilesh also promised to include oil and ghee in ration supplies if the SP forms the government. He said this would help meet the nutritional needs of poor families. He spoke of building an Ayodhya where no poor woman or child would face humiliation or harassment. He also referred to an alleged incident in which a poor woman and her children were mistreated while collecting oil. AI video explains PDA government's ration plan Akhilesh also shared an AI-generated video along with his post. In the video, a child is shown collecting oil from lamps. When a woman asks him why he is doing so, the child says that his father is no longer alive and he is collecting oil for the family's ration. The woman tells him not to worry, saying that the PDA government will provide mustard oil free of cost along with ration supplies when it comes to power. She also says that his mother will receive ₹40,000 every year. Through the video, Akhilesh highlighted his proposed welfare plans for poor families, women and children. Action promised against those who hurt religious feelings Akhilesh also spoke about religious harmony and disputes related to places of worship. He said strict action would be taken against anyone who insults Lord Ram, Lord Krishna or respected figures of any other religion. He added that those who protect people involved in such acts would also face action if they were found to be part of a plan to disturb social harmony. Akhilesh targets BJP over Ayodhya issues Through his post, Akhilesh brought together issues related to religious faith, local business, employment, corruption and social justice. He tried to link the Ram temple theft controversy with the alleged fall in the number of devotees and its impact on local businesses. He presented Ayodhya not just as a religious tourism destination but also as a political issue focused on local jobs, transparent temple management, welfare of poor families and respect for local people.

stories.title: 'Dhirendra Shastri should not be invited to Kunda':Pratapgarh MP says they will oppose the event despite having faith
stories.summary: Political tensions have intensified in Kunda, Pratapgarh, over a religious discourse by Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, head of Bageshwar Dham, which is scheduled to be held there. After Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav opposed it, the party's leaders and workers have also launched a campaign against the event. Pratapgarh SP MP Prof. SP Singh said, "Such a controversial person should not be invited to deliver a religious discourse at all. Dhirendra Shastri conducts business in the name of religion and hurts the faith of Hindus through his statements." The MP made it clear that the Samajwadi Party would oppose the event, but that the opposition would be conducted entirely through democratic means. The workers would not disrupt law and order. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to MP Prof. SP Singh about the entire controversy and the SP's position. Read the key excerpts... Question: The Samajwadi Party has suddenly come out against the religious discourse by the head of Bageshwar Dham in Kunda. What is the party's stand? Answer: The Samajwadi Party will openly oppose it. If you claim to be well-wishers of Hindus and call yourselves protectors of Hinduism, why then do you make statements that hurt Hinduism and the sentiments of its followers? The head of Bageshwar Dham is known for his controversial statements. Sometimes he claims to speak to Lord Hanuman over the telephone. At other times, he makes statements that hurt religious sentiments. He had said that those who died in the stampede during the Kumbh had attained salvation. Such statements insult Hinduism. Question: Which of his conduct or statements do you object to the most? Answer: Hypocrisy and commercialisation are being carried out in the name of religion. People are being fooled by drawing slips, and this has been turned into a means of making money. At times, claims are made of speaking directly to God. Such people are known by their actions and conduct. Questions have repeatedly been raised about the activities of people such as Radhe Maa and the presiding head of Bageshwar Dham. Religion is a matter of faith and should not be turned into a business. Question: What would you say about the BJP's stand on this matter? Answer: The BJP should take action against such people. If someone else made such a statement, BJP members would create a huge uproar. But when such events are held among their own supporters, no action is taken. BJP members oppose Muslims, but it seems they are also opposed to Hinduism. These people are merely peddling hypocrisy. Question: Your national president, Akhilesh Yadav, has also made statements about Lord Krishna and Lord Ram. How do you view his statements? Answer: Our national president has made an absolutely correct statement. There are different beliefs regarding the form of Lord Krishna. We also have faith in Lord Ram. However, BJP leaders make statements suggesting that discrimination is being made between God and the gods and goddesses. It is beyond comprehension why the BJP does this. Our national president has raised the issue of the insult to Sanatan Dharma. Question: A religious discourse is going to be held in your district. Is the Samajwadi Party preparing to oppose it at the grassroots level? Will you also ask the main organiser, Raja Bhaiya, to cancel it? Answer: The Samajwadi Party will oppose it. The national president has also made his position clear. We are against such events and against inviting such controversial individuals. The sentiments of those who have faith in religion are hurt by such statements. Such a person should not be invited to deliver a religious discourse at all. My point is that Raja Bhaiya should not have invited such a controversial person. He should reconsider this event. Although Kunda does not fall in my Lok Sabha constituency, Pratapgarh district is ours. That is why I am opposing this event. Question: Is there a possibility of workers turning aggressive during the protest or the law and order situation deteriorating? Answer: No, we will not disrupt law and order. The protest will be held democratically. The workers will maintain law and order. We are Hindus too. We also feel hurt when someone insults our gods and goddesses. Protest does not mean violence or any kind of anarchy. The Chief Minister once also described Lord Hanuman as a Shudra. When senior party leaders themselves start making such statements, it amounts to playing with people's faith. This should not happen. Question: The event has already been proposed. Does opposing it serve any purpose now? Answer: The fact that the event was proposed earlier does not mean questions cannot be raised about it. We will continue our opposition. The decision to invite such a controversial person to deliver the religious discourse is not right.

stories.title: Lucknow's sky comes alive on Jamghat:Modi-Yogi picture kites in demand; people boycott Chinese manjha
stories.summary: On the second day of Diwali, people flew kites enthusiastically during Jamghat in Lucknow. The kites were special this year. Some featured pictures of Modi and Yogi, while others carried slogans. One kite read, "Fly kites, not your life." Kite traders completely boycotted Chinese manjha this year. Some kites also carried slogans related to the issue, such as, "Say No to Chinese manjha, use only cotton string." The biggest Jamghat for kite-flying was held in Chowk. Kite-flyer Wसी Haider said, "We wait throughout the year for this day. Hindus, Muslims and people of all faiths fly kites together. In Lucknow, kite-flying conveys the message of Ganga-Jamuni culture." A tradition that began in 1775 Kite flying in Lucknow is not a recent practice but a 250-year-old tradition. It flourished in Lucknow during the reign of Nawab Asif-ud-Daula in 1775. Kites were used not only for entertainment but also to protest against the British. Lovers would write messages on kites and send them to their beloveds' rooftops. Kites made in Lucknow now reach foreign countries. Kites priced from ₹5 to ₹500 There are more than a dozen varieties of kites, priced from ₹5 to ₹500. Rockets, Manjoli, Addhi, Pauna, Chand-Tara, Baaz, Kalidaar and plastic kites are in high demand. Traders and kite flyers are both opposing Chinese manjha. Lucknow kites reach Saudi Arabia Mohammad Salman, who runs a kite business in the Hussain Ganj area, said the shop is 35 years old. He learnt to make and fly kites from his grandfather. Whenever a kite-flying competition is held anywhere in Uttar Pradesh, the Tourism Department sends him to participate in it. Kites have now undergone this change. They have become smaller in size, as has the thread used to fly them. Kites made in Lucknow are considered the finest in India. Kites made by Salman reach Saudi Arabia and Dubai. He said that accidents were taking place regularly because of Chinese manjha. All traders are also opposed to Chinese manjha, so this time they are conveying the message "No Chinese manjha" from their shop, and kites are being flown on the same theme. He said that because of this Chinese manjha, Lucknow's 250-year-old kite-flying culture and passion are also being defamed. 'A kite is like a second wife' Meraj Ahmad Faridi, 52, says he is a kite lover. He has been flying kites continuously for the past 30 years. He says he cannot sleep on the night of Jamghat and simply waits for morning. It is a festival celebrated by people of every faith in Lucknow. As a child, his father would be very angry with them for flying kites. His father beat him, but he never lost his passion for kite flying Once, they beat him so badly over a kite that his head split open, but he still did not give up his passion for kite flying. He says a kite is like a second wife. Miraj said kite flying is not just a hobby but also exercise. He is completely fit at the age of 52, and he credits kite flying for this. He said flying a kite gives the hands plenty of exercise. It also exercises the eyes and the body.

stories.title: Why fatwa over Abdullah's nikah and Sara visiting Kedarnath:Maulana says she must repent; Allah will hold her accountable
stories.summary: Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi frequently makes headlines for issuing fatwas. He is the national president of the All India Muslim Jamaat based in Bareilly. Recently, he issued two more fatwas. He raised objections to a Hindu youth adopting a Muslim surname. Be it a politician, an actor, or a common man, no one has been spared. He says, “Muslims must not act against the principles of Islam, and anyone who fails to follow Sharia will have to seek forgiveness (repent).” The Maulana has issued fatwas against dozens of prominent leaders, film stars, and famous personalities. He claims, “Many people have accepted my fatwas and started living according to Islam; those who do not... will have to answer to God.” In light of this, several questions arise—what exactly is a fatwa? Who has the right to issue it? Does someone face any religious punishment if they choose not to comply with a fatwa issued against them? Read this report... 'Omar Abdullah-Nidhi Razdan's marriage is unlawful in Islam' Dainik Bhaskar asked Maulana Shahabuddin—how is the marriage of Omar Abdullah and Nidhi Razdan unlawful? He says—the first condition of marriage in Islam is that both the man and the woman must be Muslim. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah is indeed a Muslim, but Nidhi Razdan is a Kashmiri Hindu. According to the Maulana, Omar should have first had the person he was marrying embrace Islam, recite the Kalima and only then perform the Nikaah. Only then would this marriage have been valid in the light of Sharia. After that, they could have completed the legal proceedings under the Special Marriage Act. He bypassed the principles of Islam and directly adopted the Marriage Act, which is not acceptable in Islam. “Moreover, had he not been a Muslim, we would not have issued any decree either,” he said. Maulana says—Sara Ali is a sinner, she must seek forgiveness from God We asked the Maulana, ‘Is worshipping in a temple also a sin?’ He says—in Islam, visiting the place of worship of another religion to pray or offer water is not permissible. In Islam, associating anyone else with God is considered the greatest sin. Sara Ali is a sinner, and she must seek forgiveness from God. ‘A non-Muslim cannot add 'Mohammad' to their name' Regarding Mohammad Deepak Kumar from Uttarakhand, there were also discussions that a fatwa had been issued against him. However, the Maulana dismissed this, stating that a fatwa applies only to Muslims, not to non-Muslims. However, raising an objection to the name, he said, “Mohammad” is the name of the Prophet Mohammad, and it has its own dignity. No non-Muslim can be allowed to write "Mohammad" before their name. They ought to move forward with their original identity alone. Maulana says, ‘Whoever has faith will abide by the fatwa’ When the Maulana was asked whether anyone actually follows his fatwas and if there is any provision for punishment in case of non-compliance, he said—it is not within our authority to take action against anyone. We merely state the command of Sharia. Those who do wrong will have to answer before God. Giving examples, he said—a fatwa was issued when SP MLA Naseem Solanki visited a temple in Kanpur, after which she respected the fatwa and sought forgiveness. A fatwa was also issued against a famous woman from Kashmir, explaining the command of Sharia, which she accepted and sought forgiveness for. Who can issue a fatwa, and what is the correct procedure… To understand this, Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Dr Maulana Kalbe Rusaid Rizvi, President of the National Ulema Parliament. Dr Kalbe Rusaid explained that the rules for issuing a fatwa differ between Sunni and Shia communities. 'Issuing a fatwa without being asked is not right' Dr Kalbe Rushaid Rizvi, President of the National Ulema Parliament, questioned the fatwas issued by Maulana Shahabuddin. He said—according to Sharia, a fatwa is given when someone seeks one regarding their problem or question. When neither Omar Abdullah nor Sara Ali Khan asked for a fatwa, issuing one on one's own makes no sense. He stated that many Muslims work in Kedarnath and regularly travel there. In such a scenario, issuing a fatwa on every matter without any request is not a correct tradition. What does the country's law say regarding a fatwa? According to Indian law, a fatwa has no legal recognition or binding authority. The Supreme Court has also made it clear that a fatwa cannot violate an individual's fundamental rights, nor can it be forcibly enforced. It is merely a religious opinion or advice, and accepting or rejecting it rests entirely with the individual concerned.

stories.title: Why is Akhilesh not contesting elections himself?:Strategy or superstition; Mulayam to Mayawati have used the same tactic
stories.summary: ‘We become Chief Minister only when we do not contest elections…’ By stating this, Akhilesh Yadav has hinted at not contesting the 2027 UP Assembly elections. Meanwhile, he had previously challenged CM Yogi to contest elections from Ayodhya. The CM accepted the challenge and said - ‘Come, let us battle it out….’ In response, Akhilesh said that Pawan Pandey (a local leader) is enough there. Now the question is, why does Akhilesh himself not want to contest the election? Is there a strategy behind this or some superstition? We will decode this in today's UP Explainer… Question 1: What is the significance of Akhilesh Yadav himself not contesting the 2027 elections? Answer: This is part of Akhilesh's well-thought-out strategy. According to political experts and media reports in Uttar Pradesh, there are deep political meanings behind these statements, which we can understand in very simple terms… I) ‘Becoming CM without contesting elections’, a tried-and-tested method During a interaction with the media, Akhilesh Yadav remarked in a humorous manner that ‘We become Chief Minister only when we do not contest elections. Therefore, we will do the auspicious deed.’ Political analyst and senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans explains—the SP government was formed in 2012. Akhilesh became Chief Minister for the first time then. At that time, he was not a member of the Legislative Assembly, but a Member of Parliament in the Lok Sabha. Later, he chose the route of the Legislative Council. Before him, when Mulayam Singh Yadav became CM in 2003, he too had not entered the electoral battlefield at that time. So this could be a superstition of their party that if the National President does not enter the election fray, a government will be formed. II) An attempt to gain a political edge over CM Yogi On 11th October, Akhilesh taunted CM Yogi, saying—the Chief Minister's ticket is also decided from Delhi, he does not distribute tickets himself. Now, by speaking of not contesting the election himself, he wants to show that in the BJP, even the Chief Minister has to depend on the high command for his own seat. In contrast, in the SP, Akhilesh decides everything himself. The decision regarding whether he contests or not will be made by him; not by any ‘high command’. In fact, Akhilesh wants to demonstrate that there is no option of changing the CM face in the SP. It is certain that if the government is formed, Akhilesh alone will be the CM. Meanwhile, due to various speculations, the BJP has to clarify that Yogi Adityanath alone will be the face in the UP elections. In this way, Akhilesh's statement shows an attempt to gain an edge over the BJP. III) First the Ayodhya challenge, then putting Pawan Pandey forward During his visit to Ayodhya on 8th October, Akhilesh Yadav challenged CM Yogi to contest the election from there. When the CM accepted the challenge and challenged him in turn to contest from the same seat, Akhilesh said that Pawan Pandey (Tej Narayan Pandey) alone is enough there. Through this, Akhilesh wanted to show that his local leader is enough to defeat the senior leadership of the BJP in Ayodhya. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP had indeed defeated the BJP on the Faizabad seat. On the strength of this morale, Akhilesh is sending a message that even the strongholds of the BJP are no longer secure. His party workers themselves will manage the elections there. Overall, Akhilesh Yadav's statement about not contesting the election is not his weakness, but a well-considered move. He is directly presenting himself as the face of the Chief Minister's post, who will manage the party's command across the entire state without getting trapped in any single seat. At the same time, he is attempting to keep the BJP under psychological pressure. Question 2: If the party chief himself does not contest the election, what is the impact? Answer: A party's top leader or Chief Ministerial candidate not contesting the election themselves is nothing new in politics. Both types of impacts have been observed in Indian politics. Some are highly beneficial, while others can also cause harm. This can be understood as follows… Positive impacts (morale-boosting factors) Negative impacts (points of concern) Question 3: When Mulayam and Mayawati became CM without contesting elections, what was the situation then? Answer: When it comes to a leader becoming Chief Minister without contesting an election, it carries two meanings. First—a leader was not a member of either House of the state legislature (Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council) at that time and directly took the oath as CM. As happened with Akhilesh in 2012 and Yogi Adityanath in 2017. Second—the leader deliberately did not contest the Assembly elections, but chose the route of becoming CM through the back door, i.e., via the MLC route, as Akhilesh now wants to do. These two scenarios can be understood as follows… Mulayam Singh Yadav: Directly from Delhi politics to the throne of UP (2003) Mayawati: When she became Chief Minister while remaining outside both Houses (1995 and 2007) Year 1995: Following the Guest House incident, Mayawati became Chief Minister for the first time with the support of the BJP. When she took the oath on 3rd June 1995, she was a Rajya Sabha MP. In this government, she remained CM without becoming an MLA, as the government collapsed in just 4 months. Thereafter, in her second term (from March 1997 to September 1997) and third term (from May 2002 to August 2003) as CM, she assumed office after winning the Assembly elections. However, the government collapsed on both occasions. Year 2007: The BSP secured a full majority in UP. However, Mayawati herself had not contested the Assembly elections. She was holding rallies across the state solely as a star campaigner. When she took the oath as Chief Minister on 13th May 2007, she was a Rajya Sabha MP. After becoming Chief Minister, she resigned from the Rajya Sabha and became an MLC. Nitish's record in Bihar, always became CM without contesting The case of Nitish Kumar, who has been the Chief Minister of Bihar 10 times (totalling 19 years and 90 days), is highly unique. While serving as Chief Minister, he never directly faced the electorate. From 2005 to 2026, he remained Chief Minister continuously through the MLC route. 2000: Became the CM of Bihar for the first time for just 7 days. At that time, he was an MP from the Barh constituency and a Union Minister. He resigned due to a lack of majority, so the situation of becoming an MLA did not arise. 2005: When the BJP-JD(U) alliance won, Nitish was an MP from Nalanda. He took the oath as Chief Minister on 24th November 2005. Following this, he resigned from the Lok Sabha and became an MLC. Had he wished, he could have contested and won in the subsequent Assembly elections—such as 2010, 2015, or others—to become CM. However, whenever he became Chief Minister from 2005 to 2026 (by switching alliances), he always continued as CM by becoming a Member of the Legislative Council.

stories.title: Bolero runs over two-year-old on birthday, killing two children:Four injured in Moradabad; mob thrashes driver
stories.summary: A speeding Bolero ran over six children playing by the roadside in Moradabad on Tuesday. Two children died on the spot, while four others sustained serious injuries. After the accident, angry villagers caught the driver and held him hostage for nearly four hours. The crowd insisted on punishing the driver themselves. Despite repeated attempts by the police to pacify them, the villagers refused to relent. At around 8.30 pm, police used batons to push through the crowd and rescue the driver. The accident took place in the Moondhapande police station area at around 3.30 pm on Tuesday. Driver caught after running over children Children from Mudhiya Bhaypur village were playing by the roadside outside their homes when a speeding Bolero, travelling from Karanpur towards Moondhapande, ran over them. Chitra (1), daughter of Ranveer Singh, and Ansh (2), son of Indal, died on the spot. It was Ansh's birthday on Tuesday. Ichha (6), Mehak (5) and Ayush (6) sustained serious injuries. All three were taken to hospital. A man who ran a pakora stall and his mother were also injured after being hit by the Bolero. Villagers block road for four hours After the accident, villagers blocked the road. The angry crowd caught and beat up the driver before holding him hostage. Instead of handing him over to the police, the villagers insisted on punishing him themselves. Hundreds of people gathered at the spot. The police tried to pacify the villagers for nearly two hours, but they refused to listen. Finally, at around 8.30 pm, police used batons to disperse the crowd and safely escort the driver out.

stories.title: Man rapes 55-year-old neighbour in Lucknow:Enters her home drunk, flees after she raises an alarm
stories.summary: A neighbour raped a 55-year-old woman in Lucknow on Monday night. The woman alleges that the accused, who was under the influence of alcohol, entered her home on the pretext of feeding her chaat. He then forced himself on the woman. When she resisted, the accused also assaulted her. He fled the scene after the woman raised an alarm. The incident took place in the Mahigwan area. Read the full incident... Assaulted her when she resisted In her written complaint to the police, the victim said she was alone at home on Monday night at around 9:38 pm. During this time, Pramod Maurya (40), who lives opposite her house, arrived on the pretext of feeding her chaat. Pramod was allegedly heavily intoxicated. After entering the house, he raped the woman. When she resisted, the accused began assaulting her. The accused fled the house after the victim raised an alarm. Accused runs a chaat stall According to the victim, the accused, Pramod Maurya, lives directly opposite her house and supports his family by running a chaat cart. The accused has three children-two sons and a daughter. His wife is reportedly lodged in Panipat jail. Victim reaches police station, seeks protection from accused After the incident, the victim went to Mahigwan police station and submitted a written complaint against the accused. The woman sought the registration of a case against him and expressed concern for her safety. The victim said that the accused lives directly opposite her house. She is therefore afraid for her safety. According to Mahigwan station house officer Radheshyam Maurya, a case was registered on the basis of the woman's complaint, and the accused is being searched for.

stories.title: Ravi Kishan says Rahul Gandhi's political career is over:In Gorakhpur, says Yogi will return to power in 2027 and parties ruining the country will be wiped out
stories.summary: MP Ravi Kishan targeted Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav in Gorakhpur. Ravi Kishan said that the Congress and Rahul Gandhi's political careers were over. He said, "If you want to defeat Prime Minister Modi, do so by defeating him in the 2029 elections." On Akhilesh Yadav's tour of eastern Uttar Pradesh, he said that the Yogi government would be formed again in 2027. He described the BJP's proposed march as historic and claimed that more than 50,000 workers would take part. He said that the national president would receive a grand welcome on his first visit to Gorakhpur. 'They blame EVMs and allege vote theft when they lose' Ravi Kishan said, "Wherever Congress and Rahul Gandhi win elections, there is no tampering with EVMs or vote theft, but wherever they lose, they begin raising questions over these issues." He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had won the Lok Sabha elections in 2014, 2019 and 2024. In such a situation, those raising questions about SIR should first explain where this issue was in the earlier elections. Challenging Rahul Gandhi, he said that if he wanted to defeat Modi, he should contest the 2029 election and show that he could do so. There was no point in talking about a coup or regime change. Accuses Congress of working with foreign funding Ravi Kishan accused Congress of making anti-national statements and working with foreign funding. He said the people of the country knew everything and would not be misled by anyone. Taking aim at Rahul Gandhi, he said that Rahul Gandhi should contest the election and defeat Modi, asking what darkness he had been kept in. He said such politics should not be pursued. Yogi government will return to power in 2027 Ravi Kishan said Akhilesh Yadav's political career was over during the latter's tour of Purvanchal. He said Yogi Adityanath's government was set to return to power in 2027. He claimed that the opposition would forfeit its deposits in the next Assembly election and that the 2017 record would be broken. Ravi Kishan described the BJP's 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' foot march as historic. He said more than 50,000 workers would take part in it. The national president is visiting Gorakhpur for the first time. Elaborate preparations have been made for his welcome. He said Amit Shah had enthused party workers in Lucknow. Now, the national president is coming to boost the morale of workers in Purvanchal. This foot march will serve as the opening salvo ahead of the 2027 election. The entire country will be watching it. 'Parties destroying the country will be wiped out' Ravi Kishan said those who support the BJP and Sanatan deserve praise. He alleged that some parties wanted to spread terrorism and riots in the country. Parties that are ruining the country will be destroyed. With this resolve, the BJP will take out a march.

stories.title: Husband brings wife home, kills her two hours later:Shoots her in the jaw; couple had a love marriage three years ago
stories.summary: A young man shot and killed his wife in Shahjahanpur. They had married for love three years ago. Just two hours before the killing, he had brought his wife back from her parents' home. As soon as they arrived home, the couple began arguing. During the argument, the husband opened fire at his wife with a country-made pistol. The bullet hit her jaw, killing her on the spot. The young man remained inside the house even after the killing. Meanwhile, the family members reached the spot after hearing the sound of gunfire. Police who arrived at the scene arrested the husband. The incident took place at around 1 p.m. on Tuesday in the Nigohi police station area, about 25 km from the district headquarters. Here is the full story Shivam Verma (25), who lived in Trilokpuri village, married Reshma Maurya (22) for love three years ago. Reshma's home is in Chaudera village in Nigohi, around 5 km from Shivam's house. Shivam's family consists of his mother, Munni Devi, his father, Shishupal, his brother, Vipin, and his sister, Nisha. Shivam's family worked in farming, while he operated a combine harvester used for cutting paddy. Younger sister recounts the murder Reshma's younger sister Priya said that 20 days ago, her elder sister had quarrelled with her brother-in-law over dowry. After that, her sister had gone to her parents' home. Her brother-in-law Shivam came to the house today. He tried hard to persuade her, telling her to return home. Reshma then agreed to go to her marital home. The two left on a motorcycle at 11:30 a.m. Brother-in-law and in-laws used to harass her Priya said that her brother-in-law's mother, sister and brother would all harass her elder sister. Today, they also assaulted her as soon as she arrived, breaking her arm. After that, she was shot. We came here after people in the area informed us about the fight. These people then locked the door from inside. Later, when the police arrived and the door was opened, we found my elder sister's body inside. My brother-in-law had also tried to kill me Priya says that these people demanded dowry even after the love marriage. We gave them everything. Despite this, Shivam once came to my house with a country-made pistol to kill me. My family members saved me then. But he took my sister's life. We demand that Shivam be killed in an encounter. Mother said-The brute killed my daughter Reshma's family is devastated and has been crying uncontrollably since her death. Her mother, Archana, began throwing herself on the road and wailing. She kept saying, "This beast has murdered my daughter." Reshma's two brothers, Raju and Rajiv, also clung to their mother and wept. Meanwhile, on receiving information about the murder in broad daylight, Sadar Circle Officer Shubham Verma reached the spot with a police force. City Superintendent of Police Devendra Singh said: There was an ongoing domestic dispute between the husband and wife. The husband shot his wife. The accused has been taken into custody and is being questioned.
