stories.title: Yogi gives free LPG cylinders to 1.89 crore women:Says, ‘No one will ask for money; use the savings to buy sweets’
stories.summary: CM Yogi on Tuesday gave a Diwali gift to 1.89 crore women beneficiaries of the Ujjwala Yojana. Free LPG cylinders were distributed at Lok Bhawan. The CM said, "The market price of an LPG cylinder is around Rs 983.45. Of this, the Modi government already provides a subsidy of Rs 335.40. Normally, consumers have to pay Rs 648.55 from their own pockets." Yogi said, "We had promised during Diwali and Holi that we would provide free cylinders to our sisters. For Diwali, the state government has directly paid Rs 648.55 to the gas companies on your behalf. Now, you just have to take your empty cylinder to the gas agency. No one there will ask you for even a single rupee." The CM said women would now save around Rs 650, which they could happily spend on Diwali sweets for their children, earthen lamps for their homes and items required for the puja. Key highlights from Yogi's speech 'Earlier, people had to pay bribes of up to Rs 50,000; now, free connections are available' Targeting previous governments, particularly the Congress-led governments, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said, "Before 2014, getting an LPG connection in the country was like moving a mountain. People were forced to pay between Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000 in the black market for a single connection. They had to run from pillar to post, approaching politicians and officials. "On May 1, 2016, Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Ujjwala Yojana from Ballia district in Uttar Pradesh. Modi ji saw the tears caused by smoke from the traditional cooking stoves used by mothers and sisters and decided that every poor household should get a free LPG connection. Today, as a result, crores of households in Uttar Pradesh have smoke-free kitchens." 'World Bank report confirms that 460 million people have come out of poverty' Referring to a recent World Bank report, CM Yogi praised the economic policies of the Central and state governments. He said, "Before 2014, news of scams such as the Commonwealth Games scam, 2G scam and coal scam regularly made headlines. Young people were unemployed, farmers were distressed and the poor were struggling with hunger. "But after 2014, good governance was established in the country. According to the latest World Bank figures, more than 460 million people in India have moved out of poverty (BPL) and become capable of leading a normal and prosperous life." UP before and after 2017: From security to self-reliance Referring to law and order in Uttar Pradesh, the Chief Minister compared the situation before 2017 with the present: 1. Security situation: The CM said that before 2017, the arrival of festivals brought fears of unrest, riots and curfews. Women and girls were not safe, while traders lived in fear. Markets used to remain deserted. 2. The situation today: Today, Diwali markets are bustling with activity. In a warning, the CM said, "If anyone harasses a girl or woman on the road today, they know that their path will lead straight to hell. There will be no more riots or curfews." 3. Women working night shifts: Earlier, women were afraid to step out after sunset. Today, women in the state are working fearlessly in factories and industries, even during night shifts. Schemes such as 'Lakhpati Didi' and 'BC Sakhi' have helped women become financially independent. Major special packages for farmers and women to be announced soon The Chief Minister indicated two major announcements for the state's farmers and women. Package for 3 crore farmers: Referring to crop damage caused by El Niño and unseasonal rain and hailstorms, the CM said the government was providing immediate compensation for the losses. In addition, a special package is being prepared to provide relief to 3 crore farming families. Economic empowerment package for women: The government is also preparing a major package to make women financially self-reliant, in addition to ensuring their safety. The CM said that Uttar Pradesh and India could become a 'Developed India' by 2047 only when women, who make up half the population, become economically independent. 'Annapurna Bhojanalayas' to open at mandis and workers' hubs Expanding facilities for the poor and labourers, the CM announced that the government was going to launch the 'Annapurna Bhojanalaya' scheme. The scheme will initially be introduced at market committees (mandis), where farmers arriving to sell their crops will be able to get fresh, nutritious and dignified meals by paying a nominal token amount. Affordable meals will also be provided to construction workers at designated workers' hubs. The CM also pointed out that 'Atal Residential Schools' are successfully operating across the state under the BOC Board, providing free, world-class education to children of poor labourers. Honorarium hike and model shops to be developed at a faster pace The Yogi government also shared details of the increase in honorariums for employees working at the grassroots level in the state. The honorariums of Anganwadi workers, cooks, village chowkidars and PRD personnel have already been increased, while the process is underway for other categories of employees as well. Along with providing better profit margins to ration shop dealers, the government is now developing these shops into model outlets called 'Annapurna Bhawans'. At the end, CM Yogi said, Festivals can be truly enjoyed only when there is a smile on the face of even the person standing at the last rung of society. My best wishes to 1.89 crore families on Diwali. Let us all come together and share the happiness of this festival with one another.

stories.title: Effigy of Dhirendra Shastri burnt at Kashi Vidyapeeth, arrest demanded:Students' union says remarks on Lord Krishna hurt religious sentiments
stories.summary: Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha staged a protest at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith on Tuesday against remarks made by storyteller Dhirendra Krishna Shastri about Lord Krishna. Led by Chhatra Sabha national secretary Raj Singh Yadav, activists burnt an effigy of Dhirendra Shastri and demanded action against him. The protesters said that no such comment should be made from religious platforms about any god or goddess that could hurt the sentiments of devotees. They also demanded an investigation into the matter, the arrest of Dhirendra Shastri and consideration of a ban on such religious discourses. Student Sabha leaders say action should be taken against those who hurt religious sentiments Raj Singh Yadav, who led the protest, said that the remarks about Lord Krishna had hurt the sentiments of devotees. Religious platforms should be used to strengthen harmony and faith in society, not to create controversy by comparing the forms of gods and goddesses. The students' union demanded an impartial investigation into the entire matter and action against anyone found guilty. The protesters said such remarks could create a situation of hostility and tension in society. Dhirendra Shastri made the remark on 29 October In fact, Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the head priest of Bageshwar Dham, compared the forms of Lord Ram and Lord Krishna during a Ram Katha held in Karera, in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district, on 29 October. In a video that went viral on social media, Shastri was heard saying that Lord Krishna stands bent at three places. His feet are crossed over each other, his waist remains bent and he plays the flute with his neck tilted. In contrast, he described Lord Ram as standing upright. Shastri also commented while comparing the names of Ayodhya and Vrindavan. He said that playing the flute is a game, but wielding a bow is not. After the video surfaced, several saints and devotees in the Braj region objected to the comment. Apologised on 2 November after controversy escalated After the opposition grew, Dhirendra Krishna Shastri released a video on 2 November offering clarification. He said he had no intention of insulting Lord Krishna or creating a distinction between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. He himself is a devotee of Thakurji and Braj. He said he was explaining a popular verse by a saint that mentions playing the flute and wielding a bow. Shastri also said that his remarks had been viewed out of context. If his remarks had hurt anyone's sentiments, he apologised for them.

stories.title: Four-year relationship, life falls apart within a year:Praval Gupta lived separately for six months in Meerut; efforts to save marriage fail
stories.summary: Praval Gupta, a resident of Kankarkhera in Meerut, died by suicide, allegedly distressed by harassment from his in-laws. Before taking the extreme step, he recorded an eight-minute-and-six-second video. In the video, he narrated the events of his married life in detail. He alleged that his married life was marked by constant disputes with Sneha Gupta, whom he had married after being in a relationship with her for four years. Blamed wife and her relatives for his death Praval held his wife Sneha, her father Rajan Gupta, brother Sarthak Gupta and aunt Reena Gupta responsible for his death. In the video, he described the entire sequence of events, from convincing his family before the wedding to pressure to live separately after marriage, staying away from home for six months, the birth of his daughter, attempts to bring his wife back, alleged misbehaviour with his mother, pressure to transfer property in his name, an accident and mediation proceedings. According to Praval's viral video, he wanted to save his marriage and keep his parents happy as well, but the disputes continued to escalate. He levelled serious allegations against his wife and in-laws, including mental harassment, verbal abuse, physical assault and threats allegedly issued through others. Mother says they met at a wedding ceremony The family is devastated after losing their only son, Praval. His mother, Kiran Gupta, is inconsolable and seeking justice for him. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, she said Praval met Sneha Gupta at a wedding ceremony in 2021. After their first meeting, they started talking and gradually grew closer. They remained in touch for around four years. During this period, they decided to get married. Praval and Sneha's relationship initially lacked family approval According to his mother, Kiran, when Praval expressed his desire to marry Sneha, his father, Rajiv Gupta, rejected the proposal. This also led to tension within the family. However, Praval remained firm in his decision. Later, his mother Kiran and sisters Ayushi and Anushka convinced their father. Following their efforts, Rajiv Gupta agreed to the marriage. Married on November 2, 2025; tensions began soon after After receiving the family's consent, Praval and Sneha got married on November 2, 2025. Everything remained normal for the first few days, but Sneha's behaviour reportedly began to change afterwards. In the video, Praval alleged that immediately after the wedding, Sneha, her father Rajan Gupta, brother Sarthak Gupta and aunt Reena Gupta collectively started mentally harassing him. He was allegedly pressured to live separately from his parents and family. Stayed away from home for six months to save his marriage His mother, Kiran, said Praval wanted to prevent his marriage from falling apart. For this, he even decided to live separately from his family. He stayed away from his home for around six months. He hoped that this would resolve the disputes with his wife and help them lead a normal married life. However, the situation did not improve even after six months of living separately. The alleged harassment by his wife and in-laws reportedly increased instead of decreasing. Despite this, Praval continued trying to save the marriage rather than end the relationship. Tried to bring his wife home after daughter Ragini's birth In the video, Praval said that after the birth of their daughter, he tried to convince his wife to return home with him. He wanted their daughter to grow up among family members and hoped that they could start their life together again. According to Praval, when he suggested returning home, the misbehaviour towards him increased. He alleged that he was threatened and false allegations were levelled against him. Understand the reasons behind the tensions through these dates September 13: Praval returned home with his wife and daughter. September 26: A dispute broke out between the couple over uncooked rotis. September 27: Sneha's father arrived with two police constables. October 31: Mediation proceedings began at the Family Counselling Centre. November 1: Praval consumed mercury in the morning and died. Father performs last rites of his only son The police conducted a post-mortem examination of Praval's body. His family was handed over the body on Monday. As the funeral procession of the family's only son began, everyone present was overcome with grief. His father, Rajiv Gupta, mother, Kiran Gupta, and younger sister, Ayushi, broke down and wept inconsolably. The family was somehow consoled. Later, his father, Rajiv Gupta, performed his son's last rites.

stories.title: Akhilesh says he will become CM without contesting Assembly polls:Calls it auspicious, recalls taking oath after coming from Lok Sabha last time too
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav made a major announcement on the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections from Kashi on Tuesday. Responding to a question from Dainik Bhaskar, he said, "I believe the people of Kashi are deeply religious. They have a good understanding of what is an auspicious time and what is an inauspicious one. I become Chief Minister when I do not contest elections. So, I will do what is auspicious for me. "Tell me, from where did I become Chief Minister last time? From the Lok Sabha... So, this time too, I will come directly from the Lok Sabha and take the oath." Akhilesh became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh for the first time on March 15, 2012. At the time, he was a Lok Sabha MP from Kannauj. After becoming Chief Minister, he resigned from his Lok Sabha membership and became a member of the Legislative Council. Akhilesh claims BJP is set to drop 200 MLAs Akhilesh said the BJP was earlier planning to drop 100 of its MLAs, but after losing the MLC elections, it is now preparing to deny tickets to 200 MLAs. He claimed that ministers from Kashi would be the first to lose their tickets. Akhilesh visited Varanasi for the first time after the Samajwadi Party won both the Teacher and Graduate MLC seats in Kashi. He also took a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, "You could not turn Kashi into Kyoto, but at least you could have put up a picture of Kyoto. Why didn't you put up a picture of Kyoto?" Akhilesh said, "Baba Vishwanath ji made Ashutosh Sinha and Lal Bihari victorious. Baba Vishwanath has given us a double blessing." He also reiterated that the Samajwadi Party would remain opposed to EVMs even if it won all 80 Lok Sabha seats using them. Read Akhilesh's key statements... 1. 'People from the CM's own community are committing atrocities' There is not just one incident of atrocities committed by people from the Chief Minister's own community against the PDA community. No bulldozer action is being taken. The people of Dal Mandi have punished the BJP. Reservation scam, paper leaks, Manikarnika Ghat, Dal Mandi... Can anyone forget all this? 2. 'An attempt was made to erase the heritage of Manikarnika Ghat' Everyone remembers how the BJP used batons against the Pal community, from Manikarnika Ghat onwards. An attempt was made to erase the culture and heritage of this place. The BJP received a response to this in the MLC elections. 3. 'The BJP is the real source of anarchy' Commenting on the BJP's 'Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy' march, Akhilesh asked, "Where does the real anarchy exist? In the medical system. Just think, a dog mauled a newborn baby in Banda. Who can tolerate hearing such a thing? A Union minister has just visited Bareilly. Why doesn't he travel further from Bareilly and visit Shahjahanpur?" 4. 'People in Lucknow are deceiving the Central Government' The people in Lucknow are deceiving the Central Government. When the BJP is voted out, Varanasi will smile. We will work towards building the Metro under a Samajwadi Party government. 5. On Bageshwar Baba: 'People are hurt by the statements of fake Sanatanis' Akhilesh targeted the BJP over statements made by Pandit Dhirendra Shastri, head of Bageshwar Dham, about Lord Krishna and Lord Ram. He said, “These fake Sanatanis should be stopped. What are they saying about Lord Krishna? People not just in the country but across the world are hurt by this. Now, they are making all kinds of remarks about Lord Ram as well.” Akhilesh did three things... Met the family of a deceased party worker Akhilesh travelled from the airport to Sirgovardhanpur village. There, he met the family members of former district vice-president Rajesh Kumar Yadav, alias Natthu, who passed away unexpectedly, and offered his condolences. Enquired about the health of a former district president Akhilesh Yadav visited the residence of Ajay Fauji, state secretary of the Samajwadi Yuvjan Sabha. There, he enquired about the health of his father, Satish Fauji, a former SP district president who has been unwell for a long time. Held a meeting with office-bearers in Sunderpur The former Chief Minister also visited Lata Kunj, the residence of former IRS officer Rajesh Singh in Sunderpur. During a meeting with party office-bearers and workers, he discussed the MLC election results, the state of the organisation and future strategy. The meeting also included discussions on the PDA's political activities. 'SP chief could not muster the courage to visit Kashi Vishwanath temple': BJP The BJP has criticised Akhilesh Yadav over his visit to Varanasi. BJP chief spokesperson Dinesh Pratap Singh said Akhilesh, who practises appeasement politics, was now talking about Sanatan Dharma. He questioned why Akhilesh did not visit Kashi Vishwanath Dham to offer prayers. He also challenged him to clarify his stand on the Krishna Janmabhoomi issue. Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Ankush Tripathi said Akhilesh should first apologise to the people of Varanasi. He alleged that the SP government had advocated the withdrawal of cases against the accused in the Varanasi serial blasts. He also accused Akhilesh of being opposed to Sanatan Dharma. BJP leaders said religious sites such as Kashi, Mathura, Ayodhya and Vindhyachal are being developed under the Yogi government, leading to an increase in the number of tourists visiting these places.

stories.title: 25,000 cartridges recovered from two cars in Haryana, 5 arrested:STF acted on Bihar Police's tip-off; woman among those held; consignment was to be delivered in UP
stories.summary: STF Rohtak has seized 25,000 live cartridges from a Tata Harrier and a Hyundai Aura in a major operation in Haryana's Jhajjar district. The STF intercepted both vehicles near the Rohad toll plaza on the Bahadurgarh-Rohtak National Highway. The information was provided by the Bihar Police. Five youths, including a young woman, travelling in the vehicles have been arrested. All of them are residents of Badaun in Uttar Pradesh. According to DSP Shamsher Dahiya, 24,400 KF 7.65 and BMM KF-bore cartridges were recovered from the Tata Harrier, while 600 BMM KF cartridges were recovered from the Hyundai Aura. Initial investigation has revealed that the cartridges had been purchased from a gun house in Sirsa and were being transported to Uttar Pradesh. The recovery of such a large number of cartridges has raised serious questions about the supply network for arms and ammunition. The police are now investigating the entire network. First, know who the accused are and what was recovered from them… All five accused are residents of Budaun district in UP: All five arrested accused belong to Budaun district in Uttar Pradesh. They include Afifuddin alias Munna Khan (49), son of Raheesuddin, a resident of Civil Lines (Labela Chowk); Aasim Rais (33), son of Habib Ahmed, from Mohalla Nahar Khan Sarai; Sablu Khan (32), son of Sakal Khan, from Kabulpura; Arbaaz Ali (27), son of Anwar Ali, from Mohalla Nai (near the BSNL office, Sarai); and Zeenat (33), daughter of Nawab Ahmed, from Jalan Sarai (Imli Chowk). Eight mobile phones also recovered from the five accused: The STF team also recovered eight mobile phones from the spot. The police seized both cars, the cartridges and the mobile phones. The accused could not produce any valid licence for the cartridges. An FIR was registered in this connection at Asodha police station in Jhajjar district on November 3, 2026, under Sections 25(1-B)(a) and 25(8) of the Arms Act. How did the STF in Rohtak reach the accused? Know the sequence of events… 20,000 cartridges were seized in Bihar a day earlier: On November 2, 2026, the Bihar Police STF had busted a similar major racket in Bhojpur district. A man named Laltu and his associates were arrested, and around 20,000 cartridges were recovered from them. Name of Munna Khan from Budaun, UP, emerged: During the investigation, it emerged that Laltu was directly in contact with Afifuddin alias Munna Khan from Budaun and had procured the cartridges from him. As the police investigated the network, they found that Munna Khan runs 'Budaun Gun House' in the Civil Lines area of Budaun. Connection with Sirsa's 'Mehak Gun House': According to the Bihar STF, Munna Khan had personally visited Sirsa, where he purchased this large consignment of cartridges from Vijay Goyal, owner of 'Mehak Gun House'. The consignment was then being transported to UP. Bihar Police informed Rohtak STF: The Bihar STF shared this information with the Rohtak STF, following which the police team began surveillance. Acting on this information, the Rohtak STF stopped both cars at a toll plaza and recovered 25,000 cartridges. We are continuously updating this story…

stories.title: Mother kills 18-month-old son:Strangles him while he sleeps in Jalaun; sits holding his body in her lap
stories.summary: A woman allegedly strangled her one-and-a-half-year-old son while he was asleep and then sat holding his body in her lap. When her husband noticed that the child was not moving, he became suspicious. On checking, he found that the boy was not breathing. The child’s death triggered panic in the house. Neighbours informed the police, who took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. Woman was undergoing treatment, say relatives According to relatives, the woman was reportedly unwell and undergoing treatment. They also claimed that she had attacked her older children in the past. The incident took place at around 4 am on Tuesday in the Kotara police station area, about 30 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures... Here is the full case, explained step by step- Rajesh, 40, lives in Sikri Vyas village with his 35-year-old wife, Rupa, and their four children. Their eldest son, Rishabh, is seven, followed by their five-year-old daughter Rashmi and three-year-old daughter Mohini. Their youngest son, Hrithik, was one-and-a-half years old. Rajesh said that at around 4 am on Tuesday (3 Nov), she brought Hrithik into their room from his grandmother’s room. When he woke up at around 5 am, he found the child dead. He alleged that Rupa had strangled the boy. Rajesh further said that Rupa had been experiencing mental health issues and had been receiving treatment in Gwalior and Orai for about a year. He also claimed that she had previously assaulted family members, including the child’s grandmother. Had previously made murderous attacks on her children According to family members, about a year ago she attacked her elder son, Rishabh, with a stick. Seven months later, she tried to strangle a daughter, but family members rescued her. About three months ago, she also attacked her younger daughter, Mohini. Woman in custody, police questioning her After receiving information about the incident, Kotda police reached the village. The police took the woman into custody and began questioning her. The child's body was sent for a post-mortem examination. Police said all aspects of the case were being investigated. Further action will be taken on the basis of the post-mortem report and the investigation.

stories.title: Unnao custodial death case:Delhi HC seeks CBI response to convict Jaideep Singh Sengar's plea
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has sought a response from the CBI on a plea filed by Jaideep Singh Sengar alias Atul Singh seeking suspension of his 10-year sentence in the Unnao custodial death case on medical grounds on Tuesday. Sengar has sought relief citing his health condition following cancer surgery. The court has listed the matter for further hearing on December 10. The court also directed the jail authorities to provide him with all the medicines he requires. During the hearing, Sengar’s counsel submitted that he was not being provided the prescribed medicines despite the High Court’s direction, as they were expensive. The counsel further told the court that Sengar’s family was willing to bear the cost of the medicines.

stories.title: Swami Jitendranand says he trusts Champat Rai and always will:At Kashi's Sanskriti Sansad, says those protesting at Jantar Mantar do not represent Gen Z
stories.summary: The three-day Culture Parliament will begin today in Kashi, the city of religion and spirituality. The event will open at 10 a.m. at the Rudraksha International Cooperation and Convention Centre. Around 3,000 saints and more than 7,000 young people from across the country will attend. Scholars, scientists, artists and educationists from India and abroad will also take part in the parliament. Discussions will be held on preserving and promoting Indian culture and strengthening its global identity. The event will continue until 5 November. The Culture Parliament will discuss subjects including Sanatan traditions, social harmony and national consciousness. Six major programmes will provide saints, experts and young people with a platform to present their views. Six major programmes to be the main attractions The Culture Parliament will feature the main deliberation sessions, the Gen Z Conclave, a culture festival, a national painting exhibition, a national and international photography exhibition, and rangoli and children's painting competitions. Sessions featuring saints, religious leaders, scholars, and experts will be held in the main auditorium every day from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The Gen Z Conclave will be held in a separate seminar hall, where young people will speak and ask questions on contemporary issues related to Indian culture. Around 90 per cent of the speakers at the conclave will be young people. Culture festival to be held from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. The culture festival will be held on all three days from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. It will feature performances of folk and classical music, dance, and traditional arts. Paintings and photography exhibitions will offer glimpses of Indian civilisation, spiritual traditions, historical heritage, and folk life. Children will showcase their creativity in rangoli and children's painting competitions.

stories.title: Mermaid show tank bursts, 15 injured, including 4 children:Glass shards pierce heads and faces; tank held 20,000 litres of water; accident at Bahraich fair
stories.summary: A water-filled tank used for a mermaid show suddenly burst at the Bahraich fair on Monday night, injuring 15 people, including four children. Around 40 people were watching the performance when the tank burst, releasing nearly 20,000 litres of water with tremendous force. The force of the water shattered the tank’s glass wall, triggering panic among the audience. The sudden surge swept some children several metres away, while flying glass shards pierced the faces and heads of several people. A performer dressed as a mermaid was also injured. Four children among 15 injured; two referred for further treatment Police and local residents rushed the injured to the nearest Community Health Centre (CHC). Two children were referred to another hospital for further treatment. Several glass fragments were reportedly lodged in their heads and faces. The children seriously injured in the incident were identified as Arsh (8), Burau (7), Ahad Khan (8) and Mohammad Sadiq (9), all residents of the village. Four detained, cases registered against seven people City Superintendent of Police Ayush Vikram Singh said, “Police have detained four people, including the fair committee president and the operator of the mermaid show. Cases have been registered against seven people. The tank burst because the water pressure was too high.” The incident occurred around 9 pm on Monday at the Urs fair in Khalepur village, under Fakharpur, about 20 km from the district headquarters. Two pictures of the accident: Learn about the mermaid show: A three-day fair is held every November in Khalfepur village to mark the Urs of Dada Mian. This year, a mermaid show was organised at the fair for the first time. During the performance, a girl dressed in a fish-like costume performs stunts inside a water tank. The tank, measuring around 20 feet in length and 10 feet in width, was filled with 20,000 litres of water and had a glass wall on the outside. Two Footage Clips from Before the Accident Find out how the accident happened, in the eyewitness's own words Salim Khan, a resident of Khalidpur village in Fakharpur, said the fair at Dadamiyan's Urs began on Monday. He had gone to visit it with his family. A mermaid show had also been set up there. I bought a ₹50 ticket and went to watch the show with my family. While the mermaid was performing a stunt during the show, the tank suddenly burst with a loud bang. Around 20-25 people were present at the venue at the time of the incident. No permission had been obtained for the show Fakharpur station in-charge Rajkumar Rajbhar said that permission had not been obtained for the mermaid show. A case was registered against five people, including Urs Committee president Wajid Khan and mermaid show operator Shadab. The injured are being treated at the Fakharpur CHC.

stories.title: Shivraj Singh targets Akhilesh in Lucknow:Says 'you'll be finished by February'; calls Modi a blessing from God, urges slogans that make Rahul tremble
stories.summary: BJP took out 'Save Democracy' rallies in Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday. More than 50,000 party workers and supporters took to the streets in Lucknow and Bareilly. They carried BJP flags and posters bearing the slogan 'Save Democracy'. In Lucknow, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan joined the march. He said, "Congress and Rahul Gandhi are unable to defeat Modi, so they have started hatching conspiracies. Let me tell you, Modi is the crown jewel of the country. He is a blessing from God." He said, "Raise slogans that make Rahul tremble in Delhi." Referring to the protests against the SIR, he asked Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, "Tell me, should a person's name be removed from one place if it appears on the voter list at two places?" Taking a dig at Akhilesh, he said, "From Bengal to Rajasthan, the INDI Alliance has faced defeat everywhere. So, Akhilesh Babu, you too will be finished by February." Meanwhile, in Bareilly, Union Health Minister JP Nadda, Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya joined the rally along with thousands of party workers. JP Nadda said, "These are hit-and-run people. They throw stones and then run away. Their leader has just delivered a speech at Ramlila Maidan. Now, he will run away abroad." Jayant Chaudhary said the opposition was like children who had lost a cricket match and were looking for excuses. "When they have nothing else to say, they start blaming the umpire," he said.

stories.title: Cold intensifies in UP, fog covers 7 districts:Noida-Ghaziabad record the worst air quality; 'Murasu' cyclone has no impact
stories.summary: Cold weather has begun in Uttar Pradesh after three consecutive days of rain. The Meteorological Department has forecast normal or above-normal rainfall in most parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh in November. In western Uttar Pradesh, rainfall is expected to remain below normal. Meanwhile, dense fog covered more than 10 cities, including Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Deoria, on Monday morning. Visibility in Varanasi fell to 200 metres at 7 a.m. As a result, two aircraft were unable to land. IndiGo flights arriving from Bengaluru and Delhi were diverted to Lucknow. Sunshine has begun to weaken in Awadh and western Uttar Pradesh. The daytime temperature has fallen by 8 degrees. The night-time temperature has dropped below 15 degrees. This has intensified the cold in the mornings and evenings. Meteorologists said that a new Murasu cyclone had formed in the Bay of Bengal. However, it is not expected to have any direct impact on Uttar Pradesh. Partly cloudy skies will prevail in some places. Isolated showers are possible in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Four pictures from tomorrow... October received 14% more rain than average According to the Meteorological Department, Uttar Pradesh received 32.1 mm of rain in October, against the average estimate of 28.2 mm. This means the state received 14% more rain than average. Take precautions while sowing and irrigating rabi crops In view of the possibility of rain in November, farmers have been advised to remain cautious while managing rabi crops. Particularly in Purvanchal, ensure proper drainage in the fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Waterlogging in low-lying fields may damage crops. Avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where there is sufficient moisture due to rain. Decide on sowing and irrigation only after taking weather conditions and soil moisture into account. CM says: Provide immediate compensation to farmers for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken serious note of the damage caused to crops by excessive rainfall and Cyclone Arnab. He has instructed all district magistrates in the state to go into the field and immediately assess the crop damage. The CM said there should be no delay in providing compensation to affected farmers. Even if the crop damage exceeds the prescribed compensation limit, necessary action should be taken to provide relief to the farmers.

stories.title: Woman alleges village head and sons raped her:Stripped, tied to a pole and beaten publicly; approaches SP alleging police inaction in Siddharthnagar
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman from Siddharthnagar has accused a village head and his sons of gang rape, assault and harassment. She alleged that the accused drugged and raped her repeatedly under the pretext of providing medical treatment. She also claimed that she was stripped, tied to an electricity pole and beaten in front of villagers. The woman approached the Superintendent of Police (SP) on Monday (November 2), alleging that the police had failed to act on her complaint. The incident took place in Banhaiti village under the Khesraha police station area. According to the woman, her entire body turned black due to the assault, and she is unable to walk because of the pain. Village has a population of 1,500, with only 15–20 Hindu families Banhaiti village has a population of around 1,500, with approximately 150 Muslim households and 15–20 Hindu families. The village head, Ahmed Hussain (50), runs a hospital in his house along the roadside on the outskirts of the village. The hospital's signboard carries the name of a doctor, Sudhakar Pandey. However, Ahmed also practises medicine there. The woman alleged that he does not have a medical degree and that the hospital is not registered. Villagers reportedly visit the facility for treatment of minor illnesses. Ahmed lives in the village with his wife, Badrunnisha, four sons — Abdul Gani, Abdul Shami, Mohammad Salim and Mohammad Kaleem — and daughter Amina Khatun. He has also provided a separate house to a divorced woman, Rizwana Khatun, who lives there with her son Aslam. All four of Ahmed's sons are above 20 years of age. Woman lives in village with four children The 28-year-old woman said she got married in 2019 and has a six-year-old son. Her husband had been married once before and has three children from that marriage, aged 13, 10 and eight. She lives in the village with all four children, while her husband used to work in Mumbai. The woman said she developed blood pressure-related problems around a year ago and began experiencing dizziness. She went to Ahmed's hospital to get medicines. "Ahmed told me to return home and said he would bring the medicine there. He later came to my house, administered a sleeping injection and raped me. After that, his sons also raped me several times when they came under the pretext of treatment," she alleged. Ultrasound revealed pregnancy The woman claimed that she did not initially realise that she had been raped. "One day, I suddenly developed stomach pain and got an ultrasound done. It revealed that I was pregnant. My husband was away, and no outsider used to visit our house. "When I informed Ahmed, he said the child was his and asked me to convert my religion, promising to accept the child if I did so. When I refused, they forcibly took me to a settlement and arranged an abortion," she alleged. She further claimed that the accused had recorded obscene photographs and videos of her and repeatedly exploited her by threatening to circulate them. When the alleged harassment became unbearable, she called her husband home. On October 20, she submitted a written complaint addressed to the SP through registered post. However, she alleged that when the complaint was forwarded to the local police station for investigation, the police informed Ahmed about it. Dragged by hair after complaint The woman said that around 7 am on October 27, she was getting her children ready for school when Ahmed Hussain arrived at her house with his sons Gani, Sami and Aslam, Rizwana Khatun, Badrunnisha and 20–25 unidentified people. "They grabbed me by my hair and dragged me out of the house. I ran inside a neighbour's house to save myself, but they started breaking down the door. The neighbour got scared and asked us to leave," she alleged. Stripped and tied to electricity pole in front of villagers The woman alleged that the group then assaulted her with kicks, punches and sticks. "They dragged me in front of the villagers, tied me to an electricity pole and pulled off my saree, leaving me naked in front of everyone. They continued beating me. Nobody came to help because everyone was afraid," she said. She added that her husband called the police emergency number 100, following which personnel arrived and freed her from the pole. "My entire body has turned black. I cannot walk because of the pain," she alleged. Police tore up my complaint, woman claims The woman claimed that she had approached the Khesraha police station before the assault but received no help. "They tore up my complaint in front of me. After the assault, the police themselves saw how brutally I had been beaten. They also recorded a video of me tied to the pole. Despite this, they registered a case only under minor assault-related sections," she alleged. She said she also visited the DM and SP offices on October 28 but could not meet anyone. "These people are influential and travel in four vehicles. They keep threatening us and saying that I will not be allowed to enter the village. For the past week, my husband, relatives and I have been moving around outside the village out of fear. They say that if I want to live there, I will have to follow their rules," she alleged. Claims husband's first wife was also murdered after rape The woman further claimed that her husband's first wife was raped and murdered in 2018. She said Aslam, one of the accused in that case, and his brother-in-law Razzaq were sentenced to life imprisonment. She alleged that a complaint had also been made against Ahmed in that case, but the police did not register a case against him. The woman further accused Ahmed of sexually assaulting several other girls in the village, claiming that they remained silent out of fear. One accused arrested, later granted bail Meanwhile, police arrested Aslam on Monday. He was produced before the SDM court, which granted him bail. In a counter-complaint, another village woman, Jhinki, accused the victim of assault. Police registered a case against the victim under charges of assault, abuse and criminal intimidation. SSP Dr Abhishek Mahajan said the investigation had been assigned to Dumariyaganj Circle Officer Brijesh Verma. Further action will be taken based on the investigation report. Chief Medical Officer (CMO) Dr Sanjay Dohre said action would be taken if the hospital was found to be operating without registration.

BJP maintains silence over Dhirendra Shastri's remarks:Akhilesh steps up his attack; what lies behind the change in political behaviour?
stories.summary: Baba Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri’s controversial remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Krishna have triggered an aggressive response from Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Saints and religious leaders are also protesting. Meanwhile, the BJP has maintained complete silence on the issue. This is unprecedented. The BJP has always been highly aggressive in responding to controversial remarks about Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma. Akhilesh Yadav and the Samajwadi Party (SP), on the other hand, would usually avoid speaking at length about such statements. This time, the roles have been reversed. We will decode the reasons behind this ‘change in political behaviour’ of both parties in this UP Explainer… The BJP usually launches nationwide protests against any remarks targeting Sanatan Dharma, Hindu deities or religious symbols. However, the party's traditional aggression and sharp criticism are completely ‘missing’ in the controversy triggered by Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks. There are 4 key strategic and ideological reasons behind the silence of the BJP’s top leadership and spokespersons in this matter. 1. Ideological affinity with Dhirendra Shastri The BJP’s aggressive response is usually seen when religious remarks come from the opposition camp or someone associated with left-wing ideology. In such cases, it becomes easier for the BJP to fight a political battle. Senior journalist and political analyst Siddharth Kalhans says Dhirendra Shastri’s closeness to PM Narendra Modi, CM Yogi Adityanath and the entire BJP ecosystem is no secret. He openly acknowledges and publicises this association and, in a way, also appears to work in support of the BJP. This is why the party is silent. Senior journalist Rajendra Shukla says Dhirendra Shastri is a Kathavachak whose image is that of a supporter of Hindu Rashtra and unity among followers of Sanatan Dharma. Ideologically, he is considered part of the same right-wing and nationalist narrative represented by the BJP. In such a situation, the BJP cannot launch the kind of aggressive political campaign or police action against someone from its own ideological camp or a religious storyteller who identifies as a follower of Sanatan Dharma that it would against its political opponents. 2. Dhirendra Shastri has publicly apologised In cases involving opposition leaders and others, it has been observed that they stand by their controversial remarks or turn them into an ideological debate. This gives the BJP an opportunity to prolong its protests and turn the issue into an election campaign. However, when Dhirendra Shastri realised that saints from Mathura and Braj, along with devotees of Lord Krishna, were deeply upset by his remarks, he immediately apologised with folded hands in a video message on 2 November. He clarified that he had no intention of insulting Lord Krishna. After this, the BJP was left with no strong moral grounds to attack him over the issue. Former state BJP president Bhupendra Chaudhary has also said that the matter should be considered closed. UP Cabinet Minister and former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary said on Thursday that the matter should end after the Maharaj expressed regret. He added that it was not a political issue. 3. Maintaining silence in matters involving religious figures Rajendra says the BJP’s entire politics is built around respect for saints, religious heads and spiritual leaders. The party has always accused the opposition of insulting saints. Earlier, the BJP had also refrained from reacting to Swami Rambhadracharya’s remark calling someone a ‘lowly Brahmin’. This is why, if the BJP takes an aggressive stand against Dhirendra Shastri or cancels his programmes, it could get caught in its own trap. Therefore, instead of treating the controversy as a political offence or blasphemy, the BJP is viewing it as a mistake or lapse made on a religious platform. However, Jyotirmath Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand appears to be an exception. Following a controversy during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj in January 2026, some BJP leaders questioned the Shankaracharya’s conduct, while others called for a softer and more respectful approach towards saints. 4. Staying away from a political trap In the context of Uttar Pradesh politics, the BJP’s silence is part of a strategy. Akhilesh Yadav is being highly aggressive on the issue to corner the BJP among the Yadav community and the wider Hindu society. The BJP understands that if it jumps into the controversy and starts making statements against Dhirendra Shastri, the narrative created by Akhilesh will only grow stronger. The BJP’s aggression would have kept the issue alive in the media for several more days, potentially harming the unity of the Hindu majority. By treating the matter as ‘resolved at a personal and religious level’ and maintaining silence, the BJP is protecting itself from Akhilesh’s political trap. SP leaders are putting up posters against Dhirendra Shastri at various places. They are also asserting that the SP will form the government in the 2027 elections. Now, let us understand why Akhilesh Yadav is being so aggressive. Political experts point to 4 major reasons… 1. Cornering the BJP on its own turf In this entire episode, Akhilesh has spotted a strategic and political opportunity to weaken the BJP’s strongest electoral weapon — its ‘religious narrative’. He is trying to build a narrative that the BJP and religious storytellers considered its supporters use Hindu traditions and deities for political convenience. Akhilesh wants to convey to the public that the BJP’s Hindutva is driven only by electoral gains, while he himself stands for popular faith and genuine respect for saints. By demanding a ban on Dhirendra Shastri’s programmes, Akhilesh is questioning the BJP government. Akhilesh is asking why a government that orders immediate bulldozer action in other cases remains silent on Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks. He has also targeted Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav, who is himself a prominent Yadav face in the BJP, thereby creating an ideological and political conflict within the party. 2. Building an image of ‘soft Hindutva’ and a ‘true Sanatani’ The BJP often accuses Akhilesh and the Samajwadi Party of being anti-Hindu. Akhilesh has seen this controversy as an opportunity to completely change that perception. Rajendra Shukla says that instead of merely condemning Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks, Akhilesh has made strong demands, including cancelling his programmes and sealing the Uttar Pradesh border against him. Through this, he wants to show the public that he is extremely serious about any insult to Hindu beliefs. Akhilesh wants to establish himself and his party as true followers of Sanatan Dharma, who respect the traditions associated with deities and saints. He has clearly stated that every true Sanatani should boycott those who insult Hindu gods. Through this strategy, he wants to weaken the BJP’s image as a ‘pro-Hindu’ party. Dhirendra Shastri had called Lord Krishna ‘crooked’ during an event in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh, on 29 October. As the controversy escalated, he apologised with folded hands on 2 November. 3. Mobilising the core vote bank (Yadav community) Siddharth Kalhans says both Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are worshipped. However, Krishna’s geographical reach is somewhat wider. Several communities consider him their deity in one form or another. He is worshipped as Vitthal, Khatu Shyam and Shrinathji, among other forms. Siddharth says Shastri’s remarks had a negative impact on people. Akhilesh Yadav is being aggressive to capitalise on this sentiment. Akhilesh sees this as an opportunity to ‘expose the BJP’s true face’. Rajendra Shukla says Lord Krishna is considered the deity and ancestor of the Yaduvansh. Akhilesh Yadav has presented Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks on Lord Krishna not merely as religious comments, but as an attack on the identity and pride of the entire Yaduvanshi (Yadav) community. Social and caste identities are highly sensitive in Uttar Pradesh politics. Through this controversy, Akhilesh is sending a message to his core vote bank that any insult to their revered deity will not be tolerated at any cost. He is attempting to turn this religious debate into a social movement to ensure that his traditional voters remain firmly united behind him. 4. Expanding the vote bank (Raghuvanshi + Yaduvanshi) Akhilesh does not want to restrict this controversy to the Yadav community or Lord Krishna alone, thereby limiting his political appeal. This is why he has deliberately and strategically brought Lord Ram into the discussion. Akhilesh Yadav referred to both Braj (the land of Lord Krishna) and Awadh (the land of Lord Ram). He said the sentiments of both Yaduvanshis and ‘Raghuvanshis’ (descendants of Lord Ram, primarily Kshatriyas/Rajputs and the wider Hindu community) had been hurt. By raising the issue of respect for both Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Akhilesh wants to move beyond the Yadav vote bank and expand his acceptance among the wider Hindu community. By bringing Raghuvanshis and Yaduvanshis together on the same platform, he is trying to build a broader social and political alliance (upper castes + backward castes) to further expand the party’s support base.

stories.title: US influencer loses 1 lakh followers after mocking Shivani Kumari:UP woman says he travelled at her expense, then defamed her
stories.summary: An American influencer, Marvin Achi, who picked a fight with Auraiya-based influencer Shivani Kumari, has lost 100,000 followers. Shivani had drawn a moustache on his face using soot during the traditional Bundelkhand festival of ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’. Marvin called it an insult and posted several videos mocking Shivani. Shivani later told Dainik Bhaskar: “I spent thousands of rupees to show Marvin around India, but he left no stone unturned in tarnishing my image.” Read what she revealed about the incident… Shivani says tearfully: “If Marvin had a problem, he should have told us. We could have protected him. Why was there a need to defame me like this?” Shivani says Marvin Achi is a fitness model who wanted to visit India. He had messaged her himself last year, saying he loved rural life and Indian culture and wanted to experience and understand them closely. We welcomed him. Marvin first came to India in July 2025. He stayed in our village, Ariyari, for two days. During his stay, we hosted him warmly, served him traditional food cooked on a wood-fired stove and showed him around the entire village. He then returned to his home in Texas, US. We remained connected on social media. He then came to India for the second time in September 2026. Marvin thoroughly enjoyed rural life in Uttar Pradesh. He also tasted traditional chutney ground on a stone grinder. Shivani says Marvin came to India ahead of schedule Shivani says Marvin had promised during his first visit to their village that he would return only after reaching 10 million followers. However, he came to India ahead of schedule. His visit this time brought him significant social media gains. When Marvin arrived in India, he had 5 million followers. By the time he left, his following had crossed 6 million. Several videos featuring me went viral. One of them showed me feeding him with my own hands and received 87 million views. Perhaps this was why he had promised to return after reaching 10 million followers, but he came to India in September itself. This time, a woman named Fernanda also accompanied him. Marvin received a grand welcome on his arrival in India. Shivani took him around the entire village in a bullock cart. Took him to Jaisalmer and Rishikesh at our own expense Shivani says: “When Marvin arrived, we planned a trip to Jaisalmer. We covered all the expenses from Kanpur to Jaisalmer. Several reels were shot there, featuring camel rides and cooking, which garnered millions of views. After Jaisalmer, the entire team went to Rishikesh. I took care of all the arrangements and expenses there as well. Until then, it never occurred to us that there could be any controversy.” We asked Shivani what happened during the ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ festival that made Marvin angry. Shivani replied: “After visiting Rishikesh and Delhi, we returned to our village on 21 October. In Bundelkhand, there is a tradition of celebrating ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ for six days after Dussehra. A doll is called Tesu, while an earthen pot with a lamp is called Jhanjhi. A symbolic wedding is performed between the two, followed by their immersion in a procession with music and celebrations.” Marvin played the groom at the ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ event. A moustache was drawn on his face using soot. ‘I covered Marvin with a dupatta so he would not feel insulted’ Marvin himself had said: “I also want to celebrate this festival and see how people observe it.” On 26 October, a tent was decorated, and food was arranged for around 200 people. Marvin was then dressed up as Tesu. In our tradition, Tesu’s moustache is considered a symbol of pride. So, we drew a black moustache on his face and applied a tilak on his forehead. During the celebrations, villagers also throw mud and dust. That is why we covered Marvin’s head with a dupatta to ensure that his dignity was not hurt. You can watch the videos from that time. Marvin can be seen enjoying himself. The event videos were posted on social media. Marvin himself uploaded these videos on his Instagram account, saying he had become an Indian groom. Changed his tune after reaching Guwahati, claimed he was insulted On the morning of 27 October, we dropped Marvin at Kanpur airport, from where he left for Guwahati. However, at 11 pm, Marvin messaged us saying people were posting abusive comments on his video and that he had been insulted. Shivani’s team tried to explain the situation to him, saying it was a Bundelkhand tradition and not an insult. But Marvin did not respond. The next day, he uploaded a video on Instagram, alleging that he had been deliberately insulted in the name of culture. He then posted several mocking videos targeting Shivani, including one in which she appeared to cry. Marvin posted a video showing a moustache drawn on Shivani’s face. The background song was: ‘Chhachhundar ke sir par na bhaaye chameli.’ Shivani unfollowed him, Marvin started losing followers Shivani says she had begun considering Marvin a true friend. He was like a brother to her. But his behaviour deeply hurt her. She unfollowed Marvin on Instagram and posted a video explaining her side of the story. She says she had no idea that her decision would trigger such a reaction. Soon after she unfollowed him, Indian fans started trolling Marvin, and many also unfollowed him. The drop in Marvin’s Instagram followers was tracked through the Social Blade website. According to the figures: 1 November: Around 20,000 followers lost. 2 November: Around 25,000 more followers lost. So far: Marvin has lost nearly 100,000 followers. It also emerged that Marvin’s followers had been declining rapidly before his India visit. However, when he came here, travelled around and posted videos on his account, his following started growing. This is why he came ahead of schedule. During the trip, he gained nearly 2 million followers on Instagram and over 400,000

stories.title: Yogi pauses for a little girl carrying snacks:Takes a selfie with her and invites her on stage
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a young girl stopped CM Yogi at the 'One District, One Product' (ODOP) programme. Handing him a packet of moong dal savoury snacks, she said, "My mother made this." The Chief Minister smiled at her enthusiasm, accepted the packet and then took a selfie with her. Later, when the Chief Minister arrived on stage to address the gathering, he mentioned the girl. Yogi said that she had been calling out to him as he arrived at the programme. While handing him the packet of savoury snacks, she told him that her mother made and sold them. CM Yogi tours 'Taste of Uttar Pradesh' exhibition On Thursday, Yogi visited the 'Taste of Uttar Pradesh' food exhibition at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. During the visit, he honoured artisans and addressed the organisers and artisans. The exhibition showcased Uttar Pradesh's art, culture and traditional cuisine on a single platform. A video was recorded instead of a selfie, Yogi said, "No problem, do it" The chief minister took selfies with the children of artists associated with ODOP. During this, the children accidentally recorded a video instead of taking a photo. Someone then said from behind, "It went to video instead of photo." Smiling, Chief Minister Yogi said, "Oh, do it. What will happen? No problem, no problem." The people present there began laughing. Yogi says-With packaging, it could become a brand The Chief Minister said he was very happy to see the girl's enthusiasm. He said, "I will also tell the department that if we include her with a little packaging, could her product become a brand?" Yogi said the girl was not talking about profit; rather, she was enthusiastically saying, "You give us chocolates, so please take this savoury snack from us." He also took a selfie with the girl and later called her on stage with another girl. Such products can be prepared in every household The CM said that such products could be prepared in every household in the state. Local products and dishes are found in different districts. With this in mind, the government is promoting 'One District, One Cuisine' (one district, one dish).

stories.title: Ambulance stuck in rally traffic, injured cop dies:Father says he kept pleading before traffic police in Kanpur; 12 km took 3 hours
stories.summary: An injured constable died in an ambulance stuck in a traffic jam in Kanpur at around 1.30 p.m. on Wednesday. A traffic jam stretching for around 3 kilometres formed at Tatmil crossing because of a BJP rally. As a result, the ambulance remained stuck at the crossing for one and a half hours. Pramod Sachan, the father of the deceased constable, Pranshu Sachan, said, "I kept pleading with the traffic police to clear the way for the ambulance, but no help came." Even after crossing the junction, the ambulance encountered traffic jams at several points along the route. It took three hours to cover the 12-kilometre distance. When it reached Hallett Hospital at 4.30 p.m., doctors declared Pranshu dead. Pranshu was travelling by motorcycle with his father. A speeding dumper then collided with their motorcycle. Both fell onto the road, and Pranshu came under the dumper's wheel. He suffered serious injuries, while his father sustained minor injuries. Now read the full incident... Constable Pranshu was a resident of Motipur village in Ghatampur. He belonged to the 2025 batch of constables. He was currently posted at Tanda police station in Ambedkar Nagar. He was to serve summons in Kanpur Dehat, Kanpur, Fatehpur and Rae Bareli. For this, he had travelled from Ambedkar Nagar to Kanpur Dehat on Tuesday. After serving the first summons in Rasulabad, he went home. They reached Bidhnu in Kanpur Nagar by bus on Wednesday morning. After serving the second summons there, they left for Fatehpur. On the way, they met Pramod Sachan, Pranshu's father, who offered to drop Pranshu in Fatehpur on his motorbike. Pranshu then rode on his father's motorbike. According to Pramod Sachan, at around 12 p.m., a speeding dumper truck coming from behind collided with the motorbike near Buxar Mod in the Kalyanpur area of Fatehpur. Both of them fell on the road in the collision. Pranshu came under the dumper's wheel and suffered serious injuries. His father also sustained minor injuries. After the accident, the dumper driver fled the scene. Ambulance crawled from Tatmil Crossing to Hallet The villagers reported the accident on Dial 112. Kalyanpur police reached the spot and took the father and son to the CHC. Seeing Pranshu's critical condition, the doctors referred him to Kanpur's Hallett Hospital. His father also boarded the ambulance with him. According to Pramod Sachan, the ambulance left Kalyanpur CHC at around 12:30 p.m. and reached Tatmil Crossing at 1:30 p.m. A traffic jam had formed there because of the BJP's "Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy" rally. The ambulance was also caught in it. It took the ambulance around one and a half hours to clear the crossing. Even after that, it encountered traffic jams at several points on the way to the hospital. As a result, the ambulance continued towards the hospital at a slow speed. Father said-He kept pleading for a way through Pramod Sachan said, "He repeatedly got out of the ambulance and pleaded with traffic police personnel and people to give way. He kept saying, 'My son has met with an accident; let the ambulance through.'" The traffic police personnel also tried to get the ambulance through, but no way could be found. While stuck in the traffic jam, Pranshu writhed in pain. He was bleeding from his body. His father kept trying to stop the bleeding with his hands and a gamchha, but the ambulance could not move forward. Doctors said, "Sorry, Dada, you were late bringing him" The ambulance reached Hallet Hospital at around 4:30 p.m. After examining Pranshu, the doctors declared him dead. According to his father, Pramod, the doctors told him, "Sorry, Dada, you were late bringing him." Pranshu was the only son in the family. His father is a farmer. His mother, Vibha, and sister, Chandni, are inconsolable.

stories.title: Yogi promises 1 lakh jobs in next 6 months:Interview ends, results follow; joining letters handed to 28 forensic officers
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath handed joining letters to 28 newly appointed scientific officers on Thursday. The UPPSC selected these officers. The Chief Minister said, "We will provide 1 lakh jobs over the next six months. Uttar Pradesh has changed today. Young people are now getting jobs here without any recommendation or discrimination, and with complete honesty." Yogi said- "Merit is now the only criterion for selection in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone tries to jeopardise the future of young people, they will be sent behind bars." 'Nepotism used to prevail in government jobs' Yogi said, "There was a time when nepotism and corruption prevailed in Uttar Pradesh in the name of government jobs. Qualified young people were forced to wander from door to door. But today, our government has completely transformed the system." The recruitment of these 28 scientific officers is the biggest example of this. The results were declared without any delay on the same evening that the candidates' interviews concluded. 'Forensic science plays a crucial role in crime control' The Chief Minister explained the importance of their work to the newly appointed officers. He said that in today's times, it is essential to use technology and science to stay two steps ahead of criminals. Forensic experts play the most important role in ensuring that criminals receive the strictest possible punishment and that the innocent receive justice. Unless our forensic reports are strong and accurate, it will be difficult to secure the conviction of criminals in court. Therefore, all of you have a very great responsibility on your shoulders. 'The Scope of Forensic Laboratories Is Expanding in Uttar Pradesh' The Chief Minister referred to the steps being taken to strengthen forensic infrastructure in Uttar Pradesh. He also presented some figures- • Laboratories operational in 12 districts: Forensic Science Laboratories (FSLs) are currently operating at full capacity in 12 major districts of the state. • Work underway in six new districts: Work on setting up new forensic laboratories in six more districts of Uttar Pradesh is progressing rapidly and will be completed soon. • Facility to be available at every range level: The government's objective is to provide forensic laboratory facilities at every police range level, so that time is not wasted sending samples from districts and awaiting reports. The CM also mentioned the 'Uttar Pradesh Institute of Forensic Sciences' (UPIFS) in Lucknow. He said the institute had been established to produce some of the finest forensic experts in the country and the world, and that young people were receiving world-class training there. Suresh Khanna said-Major investors from India and around the world are coming to Uttar Pradesh Finance and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna, who was present at the event, also praised the state government's policies. He said that under Chief Minister Yogi's leadership, Uttar Pradesh had set new development records in every sector. The arrival of major investors from India and around the world in Uttar Pradesh today is the result of improved law and order. The arrival of these new scientists in the Forensic Department will make police investigations faster and more accurate. Newly appointed officers said-Their hard work had paid off The newly appointed scientific officers were visibly happy after receiving their appointment letters. Several female and male officers said, "We did not expect to be selected so easily and transparently without any lobbying." A newly appointed female officer said, "The interview board's approach was highly professional. The best part was that we did not have to wait for weeks or months for the result. The list was released that evening, on the day of the interview itself. It feels like a dream come true for us and our families."

stories.title: Mother jailed for life for poisoning three children to death:Mixed Sulphas pesticide in tea in Ghazipur; fourth child survived
stories.summary: The court on Thursday sentenced the mother who killed her three children in Ghazipur to life imprisonment. The court of Additional District and Sessions Judge-I Shakti Singh also fined her ₹50,000. The court had found the woman guilty on 3 November. The woman was at her parents' home when the crime took place. After an argument with her husband, she mixed aluminium phosphide poison in tea and made her two sons and daughter drink it. They died as a result. Her fourth child survived. The child had gone out of the house with their maternal grandmother and was therefore spared. Here is the full case Dhadni Bhanmal Rai village is located in the Suhwal police station area, around 18 kilometres from the district headquarters. Sunita (40), who lived there, was married to Baleshwar Yadav, who worked at a factory in Gurugram. The couple had four children. The eldest was 11-year-old Babbi, also known as Himanshu. Himanshu was followed by Priyanshu (8), Supriya (7) and the youngest son, Sheru (4). On Raksha Bandhan, Sunita had gone to Saitabandh in the Revati Pur police station area, her maternal home. From there, she asked her husband for ₹5,000 for the children's needs. They had an argument over the phone about this. On 15 August 2022, a holiday, Sunita became angry when the children began insisting that she buy them clothes. She first scolded the children and tried to silence them. When they did not listen, she took ₹20 from the house and bought a Sulphas poison tablet from a nearby shop. After returning home, she made tea and mixed the poison into it. She gave the poisoned tea to Himanshu, Priyanshu and Supriya. At the time of the incident, the youngest son, Sheru, had gone to the neighbourhood with his maternal grandmother. He was busy playing, which saved him. When Sunita's mother learnt what had happened, she reached the house. On seeing all three children in a critical condition, she raised the alarm. When she asked her daughter, Sunita told her that she had poisoned the children. The three children were rushed by ambulance to the district hospital, where Priyanshu died. Himanshu and Supriya were referred to Varanasi, where both died the same day. All three deceased children studied at the village council-run school. Himanshu was in Class 6, Priyanshu in Class 3 and Supriya in Class 2. Children's uncle had filed the case When he reached the village from Gurugram after receiving news of the incident, the children's uncle, Baleshwar Yadav, was devastated on seeing their bodies. He had said that his wife had previously spoken of poisoning the children, but he had not imagined that she would actually do it. After the incident, the children's uncle, Bullu Yadav, filed a murder case. The case had been under trial for four years. Sunita was never granted bail after her arrest. Additional District Government Counsel Akhilesh Singh produced seven witnesses.

stories.title: Couple found murdered in Kannauj government quarters:Wife strangled, husband’s skull smashed; daughter injured
stories.summary: A man and his wife were murdered in their accommodation at a government hospital in Kannauj. Their bodies were found lying in the room on Thursday morning. Their two-year-old daughter was found unconscious. She had injury marks on her face and a broken bone in her neck. She was breathing and was immediately taken to hospital. On Thursday morning, a relative of the couple who lived near the accommodation knocked on the gate of their home. When the door did not open for a long time, he looked inside. The bodies of the husband and wife were lying in the room. He then raised the alarm and called people living nearby. After receiving the information, police reached the spot, broke open the room's door and entered. The wife's body was lying on a wooden cot and the husband's body was on a charpoy. A rope was tightly tied around the wife's neck, while the husband had been struck on the head with a heavy weapon. His head and forehead had been split open. There were bloodstains on his clothes. Police have sent the couple's bodies for post-mortem examination. The incident took place in the Gursahaiganj area. See two pictures Now read the full details of the case The couple originally belonged to Pakhanavihar village in Farrukhabad district. The husband was Sanjeev Kumar (35), son of Vedram, and the wife was Shikha (32). Their two-year-old daughter, who was found injured, is named Vanya. They lived in a government house at the old primary health centre on Railway Road in the town of Gursahaiganj. The hospital has since been shifted to a new building on Tirva Road. It is reported that Sanjeev's mother, Kisuma Devi, worked privately at the primary health centre as a midwife, assisting the nursing staff with deliveries. Kisuma died several years ago. Shikha then began working as a midwife. The couple's elder son is Pratyaansh (seven), who had gone to his father's paternal aunt's house at the time of the incident. The family was living in the house on the hospital premises. Two more pictures from the spot Family members accuse them of murder Family members who arrived from Farrukhabad began protesting, accusing the couple of being murdered. They allege that the police had the bodies removed from the spot before they arrived. The two were killed after the room was locked. The police should arrest the accused. Although police officials assured them that the bodies had been kept in the mortuary and would be brought in shortly, they calmed down after that. SP says: One gate was locked, while the latch on the other was bolted from inside District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and SP Vinod Kumar reached the spot after receiving information about the murder. The SP said the initial investigation had found that the house where the couple lived had two doors for entry and exit. One door was locked, while the other had been bolted from inside. Therefore, the possibility of an outsider entering was low, but the condition in which the bodies were found raised a strong suspicion of murder. According to the SP, a boy named Shiv, a relative of the deceased Sanjeev, also lives in Gursahaiganj. When the door of their house did not open after 10 a.m., he climbed onto the roof and saw their bodies lying in the room. The field unit and forensic team have currently been tasked with investigating the case. DIG says-5 teams assigned for investigation Kanpur Zone DIG Yamuna Prasad reached the scene. He spoke to police officers and formed five teams to solve the case. He said the post-mortems of both bodies were being conducted. The entire incident will be solved soon.

stories.title: Diwali brings festive cheer to Lucknow markets:Demand rises for everything from earthen lamps to handmade idols
stories.summary: Diwali festivities are beginning to brighten Lucknow's markets. Earthen lamps and handmade Lakshmi-Ganesha idols are being displayed in some places, while colourful string lights and terracotta products are attracting shoppers elsewhere. What stands out this time is that the shopping also reflects tradition and employment for local artisans. Some people are buying earthenware to revive childhood memories, while others are doing so to connect their children with their old traditions. The largest crowds of women are being seen in the markets of Aminabad, Patrakarpuram, Yahiyaganj, Nishatganj and Chowk. See 3 pictures... Lakshmi-Ganesha idols priced between ₹100 and ₹5,100 Manoj Gupta has been selling Lakshmi-Ganesh idols during Diwali for the past 15 years. He has idols priced from ₹100 to ₹5,100. Alongside ordinary traditional idols, fancy and Kolkata-style idols are also available. He said the price of the idols depends on their size and decoration. The ₹5,100 idol features intricate kundan work. Lalita has been setting up a Diwali stall for 10 years Lalita, who is from Rajasthan, has been setting up a stall in Lucknow during Diwali for the past 10 years. She sells decorative items that are hung on both sides of doors. Their prices range from ₹100 to ₹500, depending on their size. Lalita said that because she has a young child, she has to sell the items while sitting at the stall. One-rupee diya, bargaining even for sets Reshma has been making and selling earthenware since childhood. The business has been passed down in her family since her grandparents' time. The shop stocks several types of lamps, including khappars with five, seven, 10 and 11 diyas. The plain diya is the best-selling item. Reshma said the small diya costs ₹1, while a full set is available for ₹50 to ₹60. Despite this, customers ask for the set at ₹20 to ₹30. There was not as much bargaining earlier, but now customers bargain extensively. Handmade idols have a distinct identity Vineet Rawat, who sells terracotta items, has been in this business for 10 to 12 years. His shop stocks elephants, Buddha figures, urlis, bowls, tables, tortoises and Ganesha idols. Ganesha idols are priced at ₹1,500 to ₹1,600, while Buddha figures cost ₹2,500 to ₹2,600. Vineet said that POP idols are made in moulds and are available for ₹250 to ₹300. Clay idols, on the other hand, are made by hand. Their prices range from ₹700-800 to ₹1,000-1,200. Some items come from Gorakhpur, Kolkata and Delhi, while many products are made locally. Connecting children with the tradition of clay utensils Himangi, who had come to Anaura Kala to shop, bought household items instead of decorative Diwali products. For her four-year-old child, she bought a traditional grinding stone, a chakla-belna and other household items. She said she wanted to familiarise the child with the old household items used in everyday life. Himangi said that amid the glitter of the markets, earthen pots add to the beauty of Diwali. This tradition is gradually disappearing. She wants her child to experience the things she saw during her own childhood. Childhood memories brought back by earthenware Pushplata Singh, who came from Banaras, was reminded of childhood traditions after seeing earthen houses, small jata-jatoli, ghariya and plates. She said that worshipping earthen lamps and utensils is part of their tradition. It also provides employment to potters. She bought the items after liking the shop. Shopping at the market instead of online Dr Rashmi Singh, who came from Arjunganj, does not shop online. She said that small shopkeepers and people from poor families work hard to sell goods during the festival. They wait for customers. Therefore, she buys Diwali items, including lamps, wicks and candles, only from local shopkeepers so that their livelihoods receive support.
