Chandrashekhar's former girlfriend Rohini challenges him in Hastinapur:Says she will contest from wherever he does; public will avenge daughter's insult
stories.summary: Rohini Ghavari, the former girlfriend of Chandrashekhar Azad, will contest the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. She has chosen the Hastinapur seat, from where Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar also wants to contest this time. Rohini told Dainik Bhaskar: Wherever Chandrashekhar contests the Assembly elections, I will also enter the fray against him from the same seat. She claims that she has also received an offer from a major political party to contest the elections from Hastinapur. Except for the 1969 Assembly elections, the party whose candidate won the Hastinapur seat from 1957 onwards also formed the government in the state. This is why political parties remain interested in the election results from this constituency. Read this week's Sunday Big Story to find out how Rohini Ghavari has stirred up political activity in Uttar Pradesh… In February 2026, Chandrashekhar had said that he would fully respect the party's decision if it asked him to contest from any constituency in the state. He made this statement amid discussions about him contesting from the Hastinapur Assembly seat. Later, in June 2026, he said that it would be a matter of privilege for him to contest from Hastinapur. Party sources say that Chandrashekhar is preparing to resign as an MP and enter the Assembly election fray. Chandrashekhar's party has so far announced the names of 87 Assembly in-charges in two phases for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The party is currently following the BSP's approach of announcing potential candidates as Assembly in-charges. However, Hastinapur has not been included in these lists. This means the party has not yet announced an in-charge for the seat. Ghavari says, 'A daughter will certainly get justice' Rohini Ghavari told Dainik Bhaskar, "Wherever Chandrashekhar contests the Assembly elections, I will contest from the same seat. There are discussions about him contesting from Hastinapur. Which party might I contest from? This is not the right time to reveal the party's name. However, I have already received a call from a major party in Uttar Pradesh. Everything will depend on where Chandrashekhar contests." Rohini said, "The land of Hastinapur has always delivered its verdict in favour of justice. During the Mahabharata, the Kauravas had to face the consequences after insulting Draupadi. Now, the people of this constituency will also make Chandrashekhar answer for the humiliation and exploitation of a daughter." Now, let us understand whether Rohini's path in Hastinapur will be easy… Chandrashekhar's preparations and his 'silence' over the past 3-4 months According to Ravindra Singh Rana, an expert on western Uttar Pradesh politics, Chandrashekhar Azad began building support for his candidature in the Hastinapur Assembly constituency around seven months ago. His supporters had undertaken wall paintings in the area, and discussions about his possible candidature were gaining momentum among local residents. His impact will become clear only if Chandrashekhar enters the fray If Chandrashekhar contests from Hastinapur, Rohini Ghavari could have a considerable impact in the constituency. Her open challenge to Chandrashekhar could create difficulties for the Nagina MP. If he contests, the Samajwadi Party could make a major political move. The SP may openly support Rohini Ghavari or field her as its official candidate. Political analysts believe that if Chandrashekhar does not contest from Hastinapur, Rohini Ghavari is unlikely to gain much political advantage from the seat. In such a situation, it remains to be seen which political party's banner Rohini contests under and how favourable the caste equations in the constituency are to her. Rohini Ghavari could become the Samajwadi Party's first choice only if Chandrashekhar is her opponent. The main reason is that the SP already has two influential local faces in Hastinapur: Given the strong claims of these two leaders, the SP would not want to take a chance on an outsider without a significant political advantage. What is behind the dispute between Chandrashekhar and Rohini Ghavari? Rohini has accused Chandrashekhar of lying to her and promising to marry her despite being married and having a child. She claims that he subjected her to physical and mental exploitation. According to Rohini, she also provided financial assistance to Chandrashekhar to help establish him in politics. The two had shared a dream of securing respect for the Dalit community. However, she claims that she came to know Chandrashekhar's 'true nature' after he became an MP. Rohini also claims that she later learnt that Chandrashekhar had behaved in a similar manner with several other women. She has said that she approached the National Commission for Women and the Rohini police station in Delhi with complaints. However, she alleges that no FIR was registered despite this. Rohini has linked her campaign to the issue of caste-based justice. In a social media post, she wrote that an FIR was registered in the case of a girl from a Valmiki family because the accused belonged to the Jatav community. Leaders from the Congress, AAP and other parties stood by the woman, but no one supported her. She alleged that this was because the victim was a daughter of the Valmiki community, while the accused, Chandrashekhar, belonged to the Jatav community. Even before returning to India, Rohini had written on social media that if she was attacked, Chandrashekhar and the Bhim Army would be directly responsible. She said, "I will visit different states and hold social meetings." Everyone keeps an eye on the results from the Hastinapur seat… The electoral history of the Hastinapur Assembly seat is also interesting. Except for the 1969 elections, the party whose candidate won here from 1957 onwards also formed the government in the state. Prabhudayal Valmiki, who had served as a minister in the SP government, also lost the election in 2017. Meanwhile, BJP's Dinesh Khatik has been the MLA for the past two terms. He is also a Minister of State in the Uttar Pradesh government. However, he has already said that he will not contest from the seat for a third time, describing Hastinapur as Draupadi's cursed seat. Until now, no MLA from Hastinapur has managed to win two consecutive elections from the same party. Voters have changed their choice of MLA several times. On some occasions, MLAs themselves switched parties, contested again and won. In 1974, Revati Sharan Maurya was elected MLA from this seat on a Congress ticket. In the 1977 elections, he switched parties and contested on a Janata Party ticket, winning for the second time. The party he represented formed the state government after both elections. Political picture changed after denial of ticket There have also been instances of candidates switching parties after being denied tickets in Hastinapur's electoral history. In 2007, Yogesh Verma of the BSP was elected MLA. In 2012, after being denied a BSP ticket, he contested on a Peace Party ticket but lost. The SP candidate won the seat that year. The BSP also lost power in the state, and the SP formed the government. Similarly, in the 1977 elections, Revati Sharan Maurya had left the Congress and contested on a Janata Party ticket. He won the election, and the Janata Party formed the state government. Whoever wins Hastinapur also forms the government Muslim and Dalit voters play a decisive role in Hastinapur The number of Muslim voters in the Nagina Lok Sabha constituency, from where Chandrashekhar is an MP, is higher than that of Dalit voters. The Hastinapur Assembly constituency has around 3.50 lakh voters. The number of Muslim voters here is said to be more than one lakh. The Gujjar community has around 65,000 voters, while the Dalit community has more than 60,000. This means Chandrashekhar will face the challenge of bringing together the Dalit-Muslim vote combination. The Jatav community is considered to have the largest share among Dalit voters. Apart from this, voters from the Jat, Sikh, Yadav and Valmiki communities also influence the electoral equations. The Brahmin, Tyagi, Saini, Kashyap, Dhimar, Khatik, Prajapati and Giri communities are also present in the constituency. Hastinapur has never escaped Draupadi's curse! According to popular belief, around 5,000 years ago, a game of dice was played between the Kauravas and the Pandavas. During the game, Dharmaraj Yudhishthira lost Draupadi as a wager. The Kauravas then insulted Draupadi in the royal court. She was dragged into the assembly by her hair. It is said that, deeply hurt by this humiliation, Draupadi cursed Hastinapur, saying that the city would never prosper. According to the belief, the city where a woman was insulted in such a manner would always suffer hardship. Local beliefs also link Hastinapur's political instability and the frequent changes in its elected representatives to Draupadi's curse. However, this is a religious and popular belief.

stories.title: Owner of ₹3 crore found in drum unidentified:Wife says he earned it driving taxis and rickshaws; alleges harassment
stories.summary: Around 8 pm on the night of October 28, 2026. A village in Prayagraj… Silence prevailed everywhere. The police had got the electricity supply to the village cut off. Taking advantage of the opportunity, 25-30 policemen stormed into a house. The family members had finished eating and were preparing to go to sleep. Seeing such a large police force arrive suddenly, the women and children in the house were terrified. However, the men had already sensed that something was wrong. After a brief conversation, the policemen began digging in the courtyard. By then, a crowd had gathered outside the house. The villagers were also stunned by the police action. There was talk that the police had arrived because of a dispute during Durga Puja a week earlier, which had led to a major uproar. The family members had even clashed with a sub-inspector. People thought the police had come because of that incident. But when the real reason came to light, everyone was stunned. Three drums filled with cash were found buried underground in the courtyard. There were 640 bundles of ₹500 notes. No one had imagined that a 'treasure' was buried beneath the ground in a house in the village. Ten days have passed since the incident, but it is still not known where the money came from. There are three theories circulating among the villagers: To find out where the money came from, a Dainik Bhaskar team visited the village. Let's find out what we discovered… Baripur Ramnagar is a village around 35 km from the Prayagraj district headquarters. After reaching the village, we tried to speak to the residents about the incident. However, people kept avoiding questions. They said that speaking against the family could lead to trouble, as its members often got into fights. After much persuasion and on the condition that their names would not be published, some villagers narrated the story of how the brothers became wealthy. Rajesh, whose house the money was found in, had moved to Pune (Maharashtra) at a very young age to earn a living. There are 10 siblings in the family, including six brothers and four sisters. All four sisters and two brothers, the eldest Rajesh and the second eldest Satish, are married. The remaining four brothers, Rakesh, Lavkush, Rajneesh and Chhotu, are unmarried. Their father was a farmer; they could not study and started earning at a young age While their father was alive, he supported the family by farming and working as a labourer. The family's financial condition was not good enough to afford the children's education, so the boys started looking for ways to earn a living at a young age. In 2001, when Rajesh was 13, he moved to Mumbai. He continued doing small jobs there. After some time, he moved to Pune. He would send home whatever money he could save after paying for food and accommodation. He also called his younger brother Satish to Pune. The two began working at Marshall Trading Company. Rajesh also got jobs for two other brothers, Rakesh, alias Mahakal, and Rajneesh, at the same company. Rajesh got married in 2013. All the brothers lived together in Pune. In 2018-19, Rajesh left his job and opened a footwear shop called 'Raj Footwear' in Pune's Rasta Peth area. All the brothers returned to the village in 2022 and built property worth crores Villagers say that all the brothers suddenly returned to the village in 2022. They brought a large amount of money with them. The brothers first built a house with eight rooms. At Mendara Chauraha, on the main road outside the village, they bought around four biswa of land for ₹25 lakh. They spent around ₹50 lakh to build a two-storey shopping complex. They built six shops on the first floor. Rajesh and Rakesh opened a cement and sand shop across the entire ground floor. They also helped one of their brothers set up a DJ and sound business. In addition, they bought around 22 bighas of farmland in the highly fertile Kachhar area. They also contributed money towards building a temple in the village. The villagers had understood that the brothers had a considerable amount of money. After gathering information about Rajesh and his family, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached their house. On learning that media personnel had arrived, Rajesh and Rakesh fled from the house. The women in the family initially avoided speaking to us, but after considerable persuasion, they agreed to talk. Rajesh's wife says, 'We built the house and started a business by driving taxis and rickshaws' We met Pushpa, Rajesh Yadav's wife. She said, "My husband left home to earn money when he was very young. He drove rickshaws and taxis in Mumbai day and night. He paid for the marriages of all four sisters with his own earnings. He never borrowed money from anyone. He built the house and then arranged his brother's marriage. After returning from Pune, he started a business here. We have no disputes with anyone in the village. Everyone stays busy with their own work and business." We asked her where the money found in their house had come from. Pushpa said, "We do not know where the money came from. Now, all we ask is that we be allowed to live in peace. How long can we keep running away? The children are unable to study. If we continue to be harassed like this, we will have no option but to take our own lives." Pooja, the wife of Satish, the second eldest brother, repeated what Pushpa had said. She said, "The men in our family are running from one place to another. We want to appeal to the government to let them stay at home. How long can anyone keep living at someone else's house? Even the people where they are staying are telling them to return home. Now, the government will decide what happens next." Cousin says, 'They brought the money but could not use it' At the house, we also met Karan Yadav, a cousin of Rajesh and Rakesh. Karan said, "I also worked for four years at the company in Pune where they were employed. The work there involved cutting iron. They had been working there five years before I joined. I got the job at a salary of ₹18,000. Since they had been working there for longer, their salaries were ₹28,000-30,000. They earned good money by working day and night shifts." Karan said that a dispute had taken place with some villagers during Durga Puja a few days earlier. Someone from the village or even the family itself had filed a complaint, leading to the raid. "I do not know where this money came from. But the man brought the money and could not even use it. He had earned it legitimately and brought it home. He kept it in his own house, but now everything is gone. On top of that, he is being harassed. This should not happen," he said. Dispute with police during Durga idol immersion led to the raid To find out more about the dispute mentioned by Karan, we went to another part of the village. Residents said that a procession was being taken out for the immersion of the Durga idol. The DJ system at the procession belonged to the family. An argument broke out with someone in the village over the DJ. As the dispute escalated, Rakesh and his brothers allegedly began assaulting people. When the police arrived, they clashed with the officers as well. First, two or three personnel from Dial 112 arrived. Later, a sub-inspector and constables from the Shringverpur police outpost reached the spot. Rakesh also clashed with the sub-inspector. To bring the situation under control, a senior sub-inspector and a large police force arrived from Nawabganj police station. The situation was brought under control only then. The police took the incident seriously and began investigating the family's background. Villagers say that during the investigation, the police received information that the family had come into possession of a large quantity of gold and silver from somewhere. They were allegedly using the money from it to continuously acquire property. Acting on this information, the police conducted a raid on the night of October 28. No gold or silver was found, but three drums filled with cash were recovered from beneath the ground. The Income Tax Department also joined the investigation. When the money was counted, the total amount was found to be ₹3 crore 20 lakh 93 thousand. Pune police team to visit Prayagraj soon Villagers say that the brothers had been very careful about how they spent their money. They bought land in the Kachhar area. They had kept the money at home, which had allegedly made them arrogant. This was why they started getting into disputes with villagers. Their brothers and brothers-in-law all lived in Pune. They suddenly left the city with the money, so those people must have known about it. Now, one of them may have revealed the matter. Ten days have passed since the incident. The Income Tax Department has deposited all the money in a bank. However, it is still not known where the money came from. After the name of Pune-based Marshall Trading Company emerged, a report was sent to the Pune Police Commissioner. A Pune police team is expected to visit Prayagraj soon to investigate the matter.

stories.title: Yogi called 'Toffee Baba' by children in this village:Celebrating Diwali with Van Tangia families in Gorakhpur for 18 years; villagers say all facilities are now available
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will celebrate Diwali with Van Tangiya families in Jungle Tinkonia Number Three in Gorakhpur today. This will be the 18th consecutive year that he visits the community to celebrate the festival with them. Yogi started this tradition in 2009, when he was an MP. The village, where people once lived in huts and struggled for basic facilities such as roads, electricity and water, has now undergone a transformation. Yogi adopted the Van Tangiya village and ensured that facilities such as paved roads, drains, houses, toilets, electricity, water and gas connections reached the area. Families have also started receiving benefits under government welfare schemes. Children in the village affectionately call the Chief Minister 'Toffee Wale Baba'. Every year, on Diwali, Yogi gifts them sweets, toffees and educational materials. This year, apart from celebrating Diwali with Van Tangiya families, Yogi will also present development projects worth ₹78 crore to the district's gram panchayats. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited the Van Tangiya village, around 15 km from the city, and spoke to its residents. Read what they had to say… 'There were no facilities earlier, but now the village has everything' Harishchand, a resident of Van Tangiya village, said, "There were no facilities here earlier. Ever since Yogi ji started visiting, the village has received all kinds of facilities. We now have roads, drains, water, electricity, toilets, gas connections and pensions. He visits the village every year and gives children notebooks, pens, chocolates, sweets and gifts." 'No one listened to us; we spent our lives in huts' Dhruv Lal, another resident of the village, said, "I was born here, and my entire life has passed here. Our birth and our livelihood are both connected to this place. We were going through a lot of hardship. We lived in extremely poor conditions, and no one listened to us. "Earlier, the Forest Department had ordered firing to evict us from here. In that incident, 28 of our people were injured and two died. After Baba (Yogi) came, we got houses, electricity, steps and roads. We received all these facilities because of Baba. There was no one else. No one listened to us. "We used to clean drains and plant saplings here. We worked for the Forest Department and served in this very area. We lived in huts. Now that all the work has been completed and our responsibilities have been fulfilled, we feel very happy when the Chief Minister visits. All we want is for Baba to continue doing what he thinks is right for us." 'We have left our dilapidated house and now live in a permanent home' Chanda, a resident of the village, said, "Our house was in a very poor and dilapidated condition. People used to run away from here. Now Baba has provided us with a house. He has given us electricity, water and roads. We have got ration cards and are receiving pensions. "Baba has provided us with many facilities. The only thing still missing is a permanent solution regarding our road and land. Even if we have a small piece of land, it should be registered in our name so that our lives can improve." Panchayat assistant says people's problems are now being resolved Kavita, a resident of Tinkonia Number 2, said, "I work here as a panchayat assistant. I help resolve the problems faced by people in the village, whether related to housing, Ayushman cards or any other issue. Work has been done in the past as well. If anyone approaches me with a problem in the future, I will help get it resolved. "It feels good to see this village because we had earlier heard that conditions here were not good. However, considerable development has taken place due to Yogi ji's efforts. "Whether it is housing, tap water, electricity or problems related to schools, everything has been addressed, and people are happy. I am also keeping an eye on the issues people face and will continue working to resolve them." How did the Van Tangiya community settle here? Find out During British rule, railway tracks were being laid across the country. At the time, large numbers of sal trees were cut down from forests to make railway sleepers. To compensate for this loss, the British government settled poor landless people and labourers in the forests to plant new sal saplings and look after them. The 'Taungya method' from Burma was used to develop sal forests. People who lived in the forests and looked after the saplings under this method came to be known as Van Tangiyas. In 1918, five settlements of the community were established in five areas of the Kusmhi forest: Jungle Tinkonia Number Three, Rajahi Khale Tola, Rajahi Nursery, Aambagh Nursery and Chilbilwa. Around the same time, 18 more villages of the community were established at different locations in the forests of Maharajganj. India became independent in 1947, but the lives of the Van Tangiyas remained much the same as they had been during British rule. Despite being the community that helped establish forests, its members did not even have Indian citizenship. Access to basic facilities was out of the question. They were not allowed to construct anything other than huts in the forest. Apart from plucking and selling leaves from trees and working as labourers, they had no other means of livelihood. They also lived under the constant fear of eviction drives carried out by the Forest Department from time to time. Projects worth ₹74.12 crore to be launched; works worth ₹3.88 crore to be inaugurated On Diwali, Yogi will present development projects worth ₹78 crore to several gram panchayats in the district during his visit to the Van Tangiya village in Jungle Tinkonia Number 3. The projects include the foundation-laying of works worth ₹74.12 crore and the inauguration of development works worth ₹3.88 crore. Most of these projects are aimed at improving basic facilities in villages.

stories.title: Diwali today, Kashi astrologer shares 3 auspicious timings:CM Yogi to light diyas with Van Tangiya families in Gorakhpur; fireworks planned in evening
stories.summary: Today is Diwali. People across Uttar Pradesh will celebrate the festival by lighting diyas and bursting firecrackers. CM Yogi will celebrate Diwali with Van Tangiya families in a village around 15 km from Gorakhpur city at 11 am. He will also give gifts to children. This year, there will be three auspicious periods, known as Sthir Lagna, for worshipping Goddess Lakshmi on Diwali. The puja can be performed at three different times between 1.22 pm and 2.40 am. According to Varanasi-based astrologer Shriram Sharma, the first auspicious period will be during Kumbh Lagna, the second during Vrishabh Lagna and the third during Singh Lagna. The evening Vrishabh Lagna is considered particularly auspicious for householders. During this period, the puja can be performed between 6 pm and 7.54 pm. Big businessmen can worship Goddess Lakshmi during Singh Lagna between 12.26 am and 2.40 am. According to religious beliefs, worshipping during a Sthir Lagna ensures that wealth, prosperity, happiness and abundance remain in the home and business. Special significance of Lakshmi Puja on Diwali Worshipping Goddess Lakshmi at home holds special significance on Diwali. According to popular belief, performing Lakshmi Puja at home brings happiness and prosperity. Households that have a brass or silver idol of Goddess Lakshmi should worship it properly every day. There are not just religious reasons behind this practice; it also has a psychological aspect. It inspires us to earn money and use it wisely. It is also considered important to have an idol of Lord Ganesha alongside Goddess Lakshmi in the temple. The reason is that Lakshmi is the goddess of wealth, while Ganesha is the god of wisdom. If Lakshmi resides in a home, its members should use their wisdom to make proper use of the wealth. Religious scriptures also lay down certain rules for Lakshmi Puja. It is believed that if these rules are followed during daily worship, Goddess Lakshmi makes the home her permanent abode. Friday is considered a special day dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi. Therefore, if a household wishes to install her idol, doing so on a Friday is considered auspicious. Worshipping the planet Venus is also believed to bring favourable results and remove certain astrological defects in one's horoscope. Find out what items are needed for Diwali Puja Find out how to perform Diwali Puja References to Diwali in the Puranas According to the Skanda Purana and Padma Purana, lamps should be donated on this day. The Brahma Purana says that Goddess Lakshmi visits the homes of virtuous people at midnight on Kartik Amavasya. This is why there is a tradition of celebrating Diwali after cleaning and decorating homes. According to the Shrimad Bhagavatam and Vishnudharmottara Purana, Goddess Lakshmi emerged from the ocean during the Samudra Manthan on Amavasya in the month of Kartik. The tradition of Lakshmi Puja began after this. According to a story in the Brahma Purana, King Prithu made the Earth prosperous with wealth and food by cultivating it. This is why Diwali is celebrated. The Markandeya Purana says that when there was only darkness on Earth, a goddess appeared seated on a lotus, accompanied by a brilliant light. She was Goddess Lakshmi. The world came into existence through her radiance, which is why Lakshmi Puja is performed on this day. There is also a tradition of celebrating Diwali to welcome Lord Ram on his return to Ayodhya. Perform Goddess Lakshmi's aarti after the puja

stories.title: Ayodhya lights up with 30 lakh diyas:Laser show depicts Ramayana, 2,100 drones recreate Ram-Ravan battle; Yogi pulls Ram Rath
stories.summary: Ayodhya celebrated its 10th Deepotsav on Saturday, with around 30 lakh diyas lit across 56 ghats along the Saryu river. The Ramayana was depicted through laser shows at Ram Ki Paidi and the Saryu ghats. A special show featuring 2,100 drones was also organised. A total of 2,147 priests performed the grand Saryu Aarti on the riverbank. Fireworks followed the ceremony. Earlier, a procession lasting around 3 hours was taken out in Ayodhya. It featured 21 tableaux depicting the seven kandas (chapters) of the Ramayana. People from across the country, including Mumbai, Gujarat and Bihar, arrived to witness the Deepotsav. Foreign tourists also participated in the Saryu Aarti. Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and several ministers were also present. See 2 photographs: 2,100-drone show depicts episodes from the Ramayana Episodes from the Ramayana were depicted in the sky using 2,100 drones. A scene showing the battle between Lord Shri Ram and Ravana was recreated. Devotees raised slogans of praise as they witnessed a grand image of Ram Lalla. The depiction of Lord Shri Ram travelling towards Ayodhya aboard the Pushpak Vimana was particularly captivating. The scene portrayed Lord Ram's return to Ayodhya after his victory over Lanka. Fireworks light up the sky The fireworks added to the festive excitement. The Saryu riverbank and Ram Ki Paidi offered a spectacular view as colourful lights illuminated the sky. A large number of people were seen capturing photographs and videos of the fireworks. The sky lit up with colourful bursts of light. A light and sound show was also organised at Ram Ki Paidi, illuminating the entire complex with colourful lights. Around 36 lakh diyas lit across 56 ghats Diyas were lit across Ayodhya, including homes, monasteries, temples, ashrams, intersections and buildings. More than 36 lakh diyas were lit across 56 ghats, including Ram Ki Paidi. More than 35,000 volunteers associated with Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Avadh University, colleges, intermediate colleges and voluntary organisations helped arrange the diyas. They also filled them with oil, placed the wicks and helped light them. Tourists from India and abroad were also delighted by the celebrations. 2,147 priests perform grand Saryu Aarti The Vice-President, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, 2,147 priests, saints and devotees performed the grand Saryu Aarti on the riverbank. The Vice-President praised the efforts of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the administration, artists and volunteers. He said, “The light of millions of diyas is not just illuminating Ayodhya but also reflecting the changing face of Uttar Pradesh. Today, Uttar Pradesh is moving towards becoming a truly 'Uttam Pradesh'.” Flowers showered from a helicopter; CM Yogi pulls the chariot When 'Ram, Lakshman and Mata Sita' descended from the Pushpak Vimana in Avadhpuri, flowers were showered on them from a helicopter. The Chief Minister, Deputy Chief Minister and several ministers and public representatives also pulled their chariot. The sight of devotees expressing their devotion to their king in Ayodhya brought tears of joy to many people's eyes. The Vice-President, Chief Minister and all the ministers performed the coronation of Lord Shri Ram and offered prayers. They honoured Lord Shri Ram, Mata Sita, Lakshman and Lord Hanuman by applying tilak and presenting gifts. The entire complex echoed with chants of 'Jai Shri Ram'. 2,500 artists perform folk dances; 21 tableaux taken out Twenty-one tableaux were taken out during the morning procession. More than 2,500 artists from India, abroad and different parts of Uttar Pradesh got an opportunity to showcase their talent in Ayodhya. They performed various folk dances. A 12-member team from Ghazipur performed Dhobiya, a 15-member team from Mathura presented the peacock dance, a team from Telangana performed Gusadi, while artists from Jharkhand presented the Jhaur dance. Dressed in traditional attire and accompanied by the beats of drums, the artists moved forward with the tableaux. Devotees and tourists welcomed them by showering flowers. What did Yogi say? Read on Manthara and Marich, sitting in the Kop Bhavan, conspiring to create anarchy Yogi targeted his political opponents from the Deepotsav stage. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the new India was eliminating terrorism and Naxalism. However, Manthara and Marich, sitting in the Kop Bhavan, were once again conspiring to create terrorism, Naxalism and anarchy to destabilise the country. He said that forces trying to divide society in the name of caste, community, region and language must be given a united and fitting response. Those who ordered firing on Ram devotees must apologise first Yogi said that 36 years ago, the waters of the Saryu had turned red with the blood of Ram devotees. Those who had stained the streets of Ayodhya with blood and created obstacles to the construction of the Ram temple were once again trying to raise their heads. He said that those who once claimed that not even a bird could fly over Ayodhya were now dreaming of visiting the Ram temple. Such people must first publicly apologise to Ram devotees, kar sevaks and saints. They must repent for their actions. Lord Shri Ram is compassionate and devoted to his followers. His blessings are bestowed equally upon everyone, but being a devotee of Ram also requires sincerity and humility. Syndicates under previous governments looted the state treasury Accusing previous governments of corruption, Yogi said that Uttar Pradesh's economy was in a poor condition in 2017. There was not even enough money to pay government employees' salaries. Syndicates under previous governments had looted the state treasury and purchased properties abroad. He said that only 25,000 diyas were lit during the first Deepotsav. As the number of diyas increased over the years, the state's prosperity also grew. Uttar Pradesh's economy has expanded from ₹12 lakh crore to ₹36 lakh crore. This year, 36 lakh diyas are being lit in Ayodhya. This is also a symbol of the state's economic prosperity.

stories.title: Girls' Thar runs over scooter rider in Kanpur:SUV crashes into house garden; another girl jumps out and flees
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a speeding THAR hit a scooter rider, killing him on the spot. A girl was driving the THAR, while another girl and a boy were also in the vehicle. After the accident, everyone in the THAR abandoned the vehicle and fled. People present at the scene said the THAR was travelling at high speed. The driver gave the scooter rider no chance to react. After the collision, the vehicle entered the front garden of a house, breaking its boundary wall. The deceased scooter rider was identified as 55-year-old Santosh Singh Chauhan, a resident of Swaraj Nagar in Panki. Police are investigating the incident using footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby. The accident took place at around 7:40 p.m. on Saturday in the Kalyanpur area. See 3 pictures... Death 500 metres from home, son breaks down in tears Santosh Singh Chauhan's body was identified by his son, Rahul Chauhan. He broke down in tears after seeing his father's body. Rahul said that his father had left on a scooter at around 7:30 p.m. He had taken his mother's sari with him. He had said, "I will be back shortly." Meanwhile, the accident occurred. Owner identified through the THAR's registration number Two girls and a boy who were in the car fled the scene after running over a scooter rider. Police obtained the vehicle's details from the THAR's number plate. Based on the number, the vehicle owner is registered as Krishna Kumar. The address is in B-Block, Panki. Based on these details, police are contacting the THAR owner. The owner will reveal who was driving the vehicle and who was travelling with the girl driver. Girls fled in another car after running over scooter After running over the scooter, the THAR broke through the boundary wall of the garden of a house owned by Professor Kailash Chauhan. The house of Anita Mahadevan, a GST superintendent posted in Bengaluru, is next door. The THAR first broke through the boundary of Kailash Chauhan's house and then collided with the boundary of Anita Mahadevan's house. Professor Kailash Chauhan said that when the boundary was damaged, they came out of the house after hearing the sound. Two girls and a boy were travelling in the car. All three were drunk and shouting. A girl was sitting at the steering wheel. After the collision, all three fled. A car arrived at the spot, and the three got into it and left. Kalyanpur ACP Dileep Singh said: Police reached the spot after receiving information about a road accident in Kalyanpur. A vehicle collided with a scooter, killing the scooter rider on the spot. The deceased's family has lodged a complaint.

As the dispute escalated, the shopkeeper attacked both men with a sharp weapon. The incident triggered chaos at the fair. Fearing for their safety, traders shut their shops and fled. Police reached the spot after being informed. The incident took place in the Dataganj police station area. See two pictures... Now, the full details of the case According to the information received, the deceased has been identified as Rohit, 25, son of Puttu. stories.title: Yogi invites 'those behind firing on Ram devotees' to Ayodhya:Says they must apologise; Akhilesh to visit Ram Lalla on December 12
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has hit back at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav over his plan to visit Ayodhya on 12 December to offer prayers to Ram Lalla. Yogi said, "Those who ordered firing on Ram devotees should certainly come to Ayodhya. But when they come here, they should apologise before leaving. Lord Ram will forgive them." In an interview with 'Dainik Bhaskar' on Saturday, former minister and Samajwadi Party leader Pawan Pandey had said that Akhilesh would be accompanied to Ayodhya by his wife, Dimple Yadav, and their children. The entire family would offer prayers at Hanumangarhi and also meet sadhus and saints. This will be the first time Akhilesh Yadav offers prayers at the Ram temple after the consecration of Ram Lalla on 22 January 2024. So far, the BJP has repeatedly targeted the Samajwadi Party chief over the issue. Yogi says those who denied Lord Ram's existence were forced to accept it At the Deepotsav event held in Ayodhya, CM Yogi Adityanath referred to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. He said, "The saints fought a long struggle for this movement. The movement progressed under Ashok Singhal's leadership and the guidance of the saints." There was a time when lathis and bullets were used in Ayodhya merely for taking Lord Ram's name. An attempt was made to ban the name of Ram. Some people assembled a large army of lawyers and tried to deny Lord Ram's existence and the facts related to Ram Janmabhoomi. But today, at least, they are being forced to accept Lord Ram's existence. He described this as an ideological victory. Yogi said, "This victory belongs to the idea in which Lord Ram embraced every section of society. From north to south, forest dwellers, hill dwellers, Vanaras, bears, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari were all his own. Lord Ram did not discriminate against anyone." Know who said what about Akhilesh visiting Ayodhya Brajesh Pathak said, "May God grant him wisdom" Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said, "He came late, but he came right. I will only say that may God grant him wisdom. However, he should also embrace Sanatan culture. He should also apologise for the firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya." Rajbhar said, "He should also announce the dates for visiting Mathura and Kashi" Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said, "Akhilesh went to Ayodhya carrying a trident in one hand and a discus in the other. However, he did not seek Lord Ram's blessings. He went to Varanasi but did not worship Lord Shiva. His visits have no meaning now. If he has announced the date of his visit to Ayodhya, he should also announce the dates for visiting Mathura and Kashi." Minister Danish Ansari said, "The SP has not remembered Ayodhya until now" In Lucknow, Minister Danish Azad Ansari said, "As the elections draw closer, the SP has started visiting every place. Until now, it did not remember either Ayodhya or the backward classes and Dalits." Pankaj Chaudhary said, "Akhilesh should refrain from insulting Sanatan Dharma" UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary said, "Akhilesh Yadav is going to seek Ram Lalla's darshan; that is a good thing. Akhilesh goes for darshan when he sees an opportunity. He should certainly seek darshan, but should avoid continuously insulting Sanatan Dharma." BJP MLA says Akhilesh should beg forgiveness before kar sevaks Telangana BJP MLA Raja Singh said, "Before seeking Ram Lalla's darshan, Akhilesh Yadav should bow before the kar sevaks and apologise." Referring to the firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya in 1990, he said the country had not forgotten the sacrifice of Ram devotees.

stories.title: Woman killed in explosion while making firecrackers in UP:Part of body found on roof, limbs found 10 metres away; house collapses
stories.summary: An explosion occurred while a woman was making firecrackers inside her house in Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh. She died in the incident. The blast was so powerful that her body was split into two. Half of it landed on the roof, while the remaining body parts were flung around 10 metres away. The incident took place at around 4 pm on Saturday. According to the information received, the woman was making firecrackers illegally at home. During the process, a powerful explosion occurred inside a refrigerator. The firecrackers also exploded after coming in contact with the blast. The incident occurred in the Hathgam police station area, around 50 kilometres from the district headquarters. Now, here are the full details of the incident Rafi Ahmed lives in Ward No. 2 with his 55-year-old wife, Nasreen. At around 4 pm on Saturday, Nasreen was making firecrackers inside the house. Suddenly, a powerful explosion occurred in the refrigerator kept inside the house. This set off the firecrackers, triggering another massive blast. The explosion split Nasreen’s body into two, while her hands and legs were flung away. The house was also badly damaged, and its roof collapsed. The loud blast frightened people living nearby, who rushed out of their homes. Police and forensic teams investigate the site Local residents informed the police about the incident. A team from Hathgam police station, along with local administration officials, reached the spot. The police took custody of the mutilated body and sent it for post-mortem. The police and forensic teams have begun a detailed examination of the scene.

stories.title: Son lived with father's body for 7 days:Foul smell coming from Kanpur house; daughter discovered death when she arrived with sweets on Dhanteras
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the son slept beside his father's decomposed body for seven days after the doctor died. On Dhanteras, his elder sister bought a car and went to the flat to give him sweets. When she knocked on the door, her brother opened it and a strong stench came from inside. When she entered the room, she screamed on seeing her father's decomposed body lying on the bed. She called people living nearby. After receiving the information, the police and forensic team reached the spot. The incident took place at Aman Enclave in Ratanpur, Panki. The daughter had bought a new car on Dhanteras Archana, who lives in Ashok Nagar in the Nazirabad police station area, is a homemaker. Her family comprises her husband, Vinay Kumar, and their son, Anmol. Archana said she had bought a new WagonR car on Dhanteras. Late on Friday night, she drove the car first to Panki Temple and offered prayers. After that, she went to feed sweets to her 82-year-old father, Dr Prem Prakash, and brother Vijay Srivastava, who live in Aman Enclave in Ratanpur. Father's decomposed body found on bed When they knocked on the flat's door, Brother Vijay opened it. As soon as Archana entered, she noticed a strong stench. Household items were scattered around the house, and filth was spread everywhere. When she reached her father's room, his body was lying on the bed. The body had decomposed, as it was several days old. Archana screamed when she saw it. The family then called 112 and informed the police. Archana said that they are four siblings. Vijay is the youngest. Their father ran a private clinic but stopped practising after 2015. Son stayed in the same room even after his father's death Dr Prem Prakash used to run a private clinic. His son Vijay lived with him. He worked at Elmco but lost his job a few years ago. Since then, he had been mentally distressed. According to relatives, Vijay's mental condition was not stable. His father looked after him and cooked for him. Even after his father's death, he continued to stay with him in the same room. It is not clear why he did not realise that his father had died. Food had been kept beside the body; utensils were rotting in the kitchen Archana said that their father would cook food for her brother and feed him. When she reached the flat, food had been placed near their father's body. Dirty utensils and food were lying in the kitchen, and the food had started to rot. There was a strong stench in the room. This indicated that the body had been lying there for several days. What did Vijay eat for seven days? According to the family, their father would cook food and feed Vijay every day. In these circumstances, the question remains what Vijay ate for five to seven days after his father's death. Did he cook for himself or eat food that had been prepared earlier? According to the police and forensic team, the body was around five to seven days old. The exact time and cause of death will be established from the post-mortem report. ACP says action will be taken after post-mortem report ACP Panki Amit Chaurasia said: The body appeared to be around five to seven days old. It has been learnt that the son was present in the room. The family described him as mentally distressed. The cause of death will be known after the post-mortem report is received.

stories.title: Woman boxer found murdered in Kanpur:Mother suspects boyfriend; 26-year-old gym trainer had gone shopping for Diwali
stories.summary: The body found in Kanpur on Friday morning was that of woman boxer Mantasha Kumari. The 26-year-old was working as a trainer at a gym in Jajmau. Her parents and family members reached the post-mortem house on Saturday afternoon. The body was identified then. Her mother said that her daughter had gone out to shop for Diwali and had gone missing. She said her daughter had been murdered and her body dumped. They have suspected that her daughter's boyfriend was behind the murder. The police are now searching for the killer. The case concerns the Kanpur-Prayagraj National Highway in the Maharajpur police station area. See two pictures... Now, the full story... A blood-soaked body was found near the Maholi Cold Storage turn along the Kanpur-Prayagraj Highway on Friday morning. On Saturday afternoon, the woman was identified as 26-year-old Mantosha Kumari, a resident of Ikhlaq Nagar in Unnao's Gangaghat police station area. Her mother Sanjana, father Prem Kumar and other family members reached the post-mortem house and identified the body. On seeing their daughter's body, the parents broke down and became inconsolable. Mother says-She went shopping for Diwali on 5 October Mantasha's mother Sanjana said, "At around 5 pm on Thursday, my daughter went to Kanpur's Chakeri Lalbangla market to shop for Diwali. She did not return home after that. Her mobile phone had been switched off since around 7 pm." After her daughter went missing and her phone was switched off, the family filed a missing-person report at Gangaghat police station on Saturday. After a girl's body was found in Kanpur, Gangaghat police informed the family. The family then reached the hospital. Father says daughter was killed and her body dumped; suspects her friend Her father, Prem Kumar, said, "Mantasha was the youngest of two sisters and one brother. Her elder sister Khushboo is married. My son Deepak and Mantasha lived at home." Mantasha began learning boxing with her father after completing Class 12. Her father used to teach boxing to children at Sports Line. He is also a gold medallist. Mantasha has won a gold medal at the Uttar Pradesh level Mantasha had also won a gold medal in boxing at the Uttar Pradesh level. In addition, she had worked as a gym trainer at several places. She was currently a trainer at Fusion Fit Gym in Jajmau. She underwent surgery two months ago The father said that Mantasha had undergone surgery around two months ago after a lump was found in her uterus. As a result, she had not been going to the gym for some time. She had started going out of the house only two days earlier. Mantasha used to travel to Lalbangla market on a scooter, but she went by auto-rickshaw on Thursday because she was unwell. The father said that a young man used to come to the gym for training and would talk to his daughter. When she was ill, the young man also visited her in hospital several times. The father has suspected the same man of carrying out the murder. However, the motive for the murder has not yet been established. Niece's wedding on 18 November; preparations were under way at home The family said that Mantasha's niece was due to get married on 18 November. Mantasha was also involved in the wedding preparations. She had gone to the market to shop for the wedding. The family's wedding celebrations turned into mourning following her death. Meanwhile, Unnao City Circle Officer Vini Singh said, “A missing person report was registered on the family's complaint. The entire matter is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge from the evidence found at the scene, the forensic examination and the post-mortem report.”

stories.title: UP raises government employees' dearness allowance by 3%:Rate rises to 63%, taking this year's increase to 5%; 28 lakh employees to benefit
stories.summary: The Yogi government has given a major Diwali gift to state government employees and pensioners. The government has increased the Dearness Allowance (DA) of employees from 60% to 63%. The enhanced dearness allowance will come into effect retrospectively from 1st July 2026. There are 1.6 million employees and 1.2 million pensioners in the state. In total, 2.8 million individuals will benefit from this decision. Employees will receive the increased DA amount with their November salary. Meanwhile, the arrears for the period from July to October will be credited to their PF accounts. For pensioners, the arrears of the increased dearness allowance will be deposited into their pension accounts. Apart from state government employees, staff from aided educational institutions, technical education institutions, and local urban bodies will also benefit from this decision. Prior to this, the government had increased the dearness allowance by 2% in May. This means that in the year 2026, the dearness allowance of employees and pensioners has seen a total increase of 5%. How much will salaries increase? Understand the calculation Dearness allowance is calculated on the basis of an employee's basic salary. Let us understand through an example how much extra money this 3% increase will put into the pockets of UP government employees. Suppose an employee's basic salary is ₹30,000. At a 60% DA rate, they were previously receiving ₹18,000. Now, with a 63% DA rate, they will receive ₹18,900. Accordingly, the salary will increase by ₹900. Similarly, employees with a basic salary of ₹100,000 or more will see a monthly salary increase ranging from ₹3,000 to ₹6,000. Dearness allowance was also increased twice last year The UP government had increased DA twice in 2025 as well. The first time, in April, DA was raised from 53% to 55%, with the increased salary applicable from 1st January 2025. The second time, in October, DA was raised from 55% to 58%, with the increased salary applicable from 1st July 2025. 30-day bonus gift granted on Diwali Two days ago, the Yogi government gifted a 30-day bonus to government employees for Diwali. Eligible employees will receive a maximum bonus of ₹6,908 for the financial year 2025–26. Of this, 75% of the amount will be credited to their PF accounts, while the remaining portion will be paid in cash. What is DA and why is it important? Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost-of-living adjustment provided to government employees. It is calculated as a percentage of the basic pay. Its main objective is to protect the real income of employees amidst rising prices so that their salaries keep pace with inflation.

stories.title: Sweets priced up to ₹60,000/kg in Lucknow:Gold-coated treats, baklava in demand; ₹400 crore business expected
stories.summary: Lucknow is once again seeing brisk sales of sweets priced at ₹60,000 per kilogram this Diwali. This gold sweet is made with dry fruits from 10 countries. Besides being suitable for ordinary people, it is also beneficial for those who are ill. Alongside gold-plated sweets, firecracker-themed sweets have also arrived in the market this year. Sweets made with figs, dates and mango are available. Chhena, khoya, motichoor laddoos, Turkish baklava, milk cake, son papdi, white chocolate and date sweets are also selling briskly. Along with taste, full attention is being paid to health. The manufacturing and expiry dates are being printed on the sweets. See 3 pictures: Hampers priced from ₹20 to ₹3,000 Renowned brand Chhappan Bhog has adopted a highly creative approach to Diwali gifting this year. Instead of traditional boxes, sweets and dry fruits are being packed in special containers shaped like red cylinder-shaped firecrackers, green sutli bombs, anar fireworks and chakris. Not only that, attractive gift hampers decorated on a paper hot-air balloon theme are also drawing customers in large numbers. These hampers, featuring unique and premium packaging, are priced from ₹20 to ₹3,000. Blueberries from the USA and pistachios from Iran used The super-luxury gold-plated sweet has attracted the most headlines. Shopkeeper Kshitij said, "The most unique sweet at our shop is Exotica, which is coated with a layer of gold and costs ₹60,000 per kilogram. We began making the most expensive sweet in 2009, when it was priced at ₹25,000 per kilogram." Its speciality is that ingredients from different parts of the world are used in it. Blueberries from the USA, pistachios from Iran, almonds from Afghanistan, macadamia nuts and Brazil nuts from South Africa, chilgoza from Kinnaur, saffron from Kashmir and a layer of gold make it special. We keep this special sweet decorated in a chest. With a single bite, a person can taste flavours from around the world. 50 types of sweets Dinesh Sharma, owner of Sharma Sweets House, said there are more than 50 varieties of sweets. This time, however, fig cutlets, date ladoos and mango bites have been specially prepared. The sweets made from figs and dates have been prepared keeping in mind the health of patients with conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure. These are premium sweets made with roasted dry fruits, which further enhance their taste. He said mango bites cost ₹1,000 per kg. Kaju katli is priced between ₹1,400 and ₹5,000 per kg. People are buying sweets priced between ₹1,500 and ₹5,000 in gift packing. Business worth more than ₹400 crore expected More than 3,000 small and large sweet shops have been decorated across the city. Traders said they were receiving large corporate orders for sweets. People continue to buy sweets until the final day of Diwali and have them packed as gifts. Accordingly, the sweet business is expected to exceed ₹400 crore.

stories.title: Jhansi youth crushed to death as gravel-laden tractor overturns:Child playing outside house escapes by running away
stories.summary: A young man from Jhansi died in a road accident. He was travelling home in a gravel-laden tractor-trolley when the speeding tractor lost control and overturned on the road. The young man was trapped underneath. People managed to pull him out and brought him to Jhansi Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. The accident took place on Friday in the Chakarpur area of Madhya Pradesh, adjoining Jhansi. Live CCTV footage of the incident has emerged. The camera was installed at a house on the roadside. A child closes the gate of the house and walks towards the road. Just then, the speeding tractor suddenly turns on the road and overturns. The trolley's hook (hitch) also breaks. As the tractor moves towards the child, he panics and runs towards the house. His slipper is left behind on the way. He survives because he saw the tractor in time. After this, people nearby rush to help. Two young men were injured in the accident. Watch 3 CCTV Footage Clips Read the full story in detail He was the fourth of seven brothers The deceased was identified as Lakhan Yogi (37), son of Kailash Yogi. He was a resident of Khajraha Buzurg village in the Babina police station area of Jhansi. Lakhan was the fourth of seven brothers. He also had three sisters. Lakhan was unmarried. His father, Kailash Yogi, had died. Lakhan lived with his brother, Manoj Yogi. He was returning home on a tractor The deceased man's brother, Manoj Yogi, said, "My brother Lakhan Yogi worked on a tractor. As usual, he had gone to work on the tractor. The tractor-trailer was returning towards the village after being loaded with gravel in Jhansi's sawmill area. Sandeep and Rupendra Parihar were travelling on the tractor with Lakhan. Part of the route falls in Madhya Pradesh. When the tractor reached near Kali Pahadi in the Chakarpur area of Madhya Pradesh, the driver lost control and it overturned. My brother was trapped under the tractor in the accident. The gravel from the trailer also spilled all over the road." Died on the way while being taken to medical college People from the surrounding area gathered after the accident. Sandeep and Rupendra were thrown some distance in the accident, while Lakhan was trapped underneath. After a great deal of effort, the injured Lakhan was pulled out from under the tractor. He was being taken to Jhansi Medical College in a blood-soaked condition, but he died on the way. On reaching the medical college, doctors declared him dead. After receiving the information, his family reached the hospital in tears. The family was inconsolable after seeing Lakhan's body. Jhansi police completed the inquest formalities and had the body post-mortem examined. The body was then handed over to the family.

stories.title: 8-year-old girl raped, murdered in Bulandshahr:Neighbour lured her away; crushed her head with iron rod, dumped body in vacant plot
stories.summary: An eight-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Bulandshahr. On Friday afternoon, the accused took her out of the house on the pretext of buying her golgappas. He raped her in an empty plot 500 metres from the house, then killed her by striking her on the head with an iron rod and fled. When the girl did not return home for a long time, her family began searching for her. Despite an extensive search, they could not find her. Meanwhile, the police informed the family about the incident. At 2 a.m. on Saturday night, the police recovered the girl's body. The incident took place in the area under the jurisdiction of the Industrial Police Station, 30 kilometres from the district headquarters. The accused, Raju Kashyap (36), worked at a factory with the girl's father. The accused lived with his wife in the same building as the girl's family. The police are questioning his wife. According to the police, the girl's family is originally from Badaun but lives in a rented house in Bulandshahr. The family has taken the girl's body to Badaun, where her last rites will be performed. City SP Abhishek Pratap said the police had begun investigating as soon as they received the information. Police teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. Raids are being conducted at his possible hideouts.

stories.title: ₹5 crore gold theft was planned in MP, not UP:Maharashtra criminals targeted the loot to repay ₹20 lakh debt; arrived in a Scorpio
stories.summary: "Our gang carried out thefts and robberies in seven states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, but had never committed an offence in Uttar Pradesh. This time too, we had planned to carry out the crime in Madhya Pradesh. The plan was to steal gold worth ₹5 crore from a businessman in an area adjoining the Jhansi border, but the plan failed. The businessman boarded a bus, and the bus reached Jhansi. He was using his mobile phone. During this time, we stole two bags filled with jewellery and fled. Later, we learnt that we had committed the crime in Uttar Pradesh. If we had known we were in Uttar Pradesh, we would not have stolen." This was stated by Maharashtra-resident accused Amol Maruti Pitekar (29), who was arrested. He committed the crime in Jhansi on 29 October along with his father and other members of the gang. The robbery was carried out to repay a ₹20 lakh loan. All six accused in the gang are from Maharashtra. They had travelled to Jhansi in a Scorpio. At present, five accused, including Amol's father, are absconding. Police are searching for them. The stolen jewellery has also not been recovered. Read the full case in detail Punjab businessmen were travelling to Jhansi to supply jewellery Jhansi SSP Vikas Kumar said, "Gurkirat Singh, who lives in Amritsar, Punjab, is a major bullion trader. He makes gold jewellery and supplies it to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh." This time, he travelled from Amritsar to Jhansi first. From there, he went to Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh and then to Chhatarpur. He supplied jewellery at both places. After this, he boarded a private bus in Chhatarpur on 29 October to travel to Jhansi. Five bags filled with jewellery were kept above their seats Businesspeople travel carrying jewellery in ordinary bags like regular passengers. They placed five bags filled with jewellery on the luggage racks above their seats. Two of the bags were placed on their side and three on the other side. Three gang members were already travelling on the bus. As soon as the bus stopped at Mauranipur bus stand, the three criminals got off with two bags filled with jewellery. The criminals fled in a white Scorpio CCTV footage shows the three men getting off the bus with the bags. They then escaped in a white Scorpio. The bags contained 6,937 grams of gold jewellery. After removing the stones and other attachments, the haul included 3,152 grams of gold and 200 grams of pure gold. It was valued at ₹5 crore. The bags also contained ₹15 lakh in cash. CCTV footage across 2,000 km searched before vehicle number was found SSP Vikas Kumar said eight police teams were deployed to crack the case. It was a difficult case because the police had no concrete clues. They had only one blurry CCTV recording. The investigation was launched on the basis of this footage. The police team searched CCTV footage covering more than 2,000 kilometres while tracking the Scorpio. This led them to the vehicle's registration number. The police then reached the gang in Maharashtra through the FASTag details. On 3 November, police arrested Amol Maruti Pitekar (29), an accused member of the gang, with the stolen money. He is a resident of Mahalangi village in the Karjat police station area of Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra. According to the SSP, the accused has been brought to Jhansi from Maharashtra on transit remand. He will be produced in court, where the police will seek custody remand. The Scorpio used in the crime is registered in Amol's name. Police suspect: Businessman's close associate provided the gang with his location Police suspect that someone close to the businessman or a local person was also involved in the gang. That person provided the criminals with the businessman's location. According to the police, more details about the conspiracy may emerge after the arrest of gang mastermind Amol's father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar. Eight police teams are searching for the father and five other absconding criminals. Father gave ₹20 lakh to repay debt According to the SSP, Amol told investigators during questioning that his father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar, was the gang leader. They travelled in a Scorpio via Jabalpur to Chhatarpur and then Mauranipur. After the theft, they returned to Maharashtra by the same route. According to Amol, after the crime, his father called him to Rashin town. After selling the stolen jewellery, he gave Amol ₹20 lakh and told him to repay his debt. Amol deposited the money into his bank accounts. On 3 November, he was on his way to the registry office to repay the debt when the police arrested him. The police recovered ₹1.40 lakh in cash and two mobile phones from the accused. In addition, they had ₹17.06 lakh deposited in his three bank accounts frozen.

stories.title: Gangster trains inmates in beauty skills at Gorakhpur jail:Woman accused of cheating people of ₹12 crore teaches children; BSA offers career guidance
stories.summary: Garima Singh, an accused in a ₹12 crore fraud case who is lodged in Gorakhpur District Jail, is teaching children. Meanwhile, Anshika Singh, who is accused in a gangster case, is providing beautician training. Former BSA Shalini Srivastava, who is lodged in connection with a teacher's suicide case, is giving other women inmates tips on building their careers. All three women are using their skills to help women inmates in the jail. There are currently 73 women inmates in the district jail. Six children are also living with them. The jail administration is providing books, notebooks and essential supplies for education and training so that the women can become self-reliant after their release. Read the report... Gangster Anshika providing beautician training Anshika Singh, alias Antima, who is in jail, is now training other women inmates as beauticians. She has completed a beautician course at a reputed college. Anshika used to live in rented accommodation in the Singhadia area. She is accused of blackmailing 165 people, including circle officers and sub-inspectors, over five years. On 20 January 2026, she got into a dispute with the manager of a private hospital during a birthday party in the Singhadia area. She was accused of pointing a pistol at the manager. During the scuffle, the bullet struck the manager's friend in the abdomen. The police subsequently arrested Anshika and her associates. Several obscene videos were found on Anshika's mobile phone During the investigation, the police found several obscene videos on Anshika's mobile phone. She contacted people through Messenger and WhatsApp. She recorded the person on the other end during video calls. She then extorted money by threatening to make the videos viral and implicate them in rape cases. It also emerged that more than 15 police personnel had fallen into her trap. The police subsequently took action against her under the Gangster Act. Accused in ₹12 crore fraud teaching children Garima Singh, who is in jail, holds a PhD. She is the daughter of a railway official. Her husband, Bhanu Pratap Singh, is a teacher. In jail, she teaches the children of women inmates. According to the police, Garima defrauded doctors and officials along with her father, husband and other members of the gang. The gang has been accused of fraud amounting to more than ₹10 crore. So far, 10 complaints have reached the police. FIRs have been registered in five of these cases. On 13 August, 45-year-old Dr Paramatma Singh died by jumping from the eighth floor of an apartment. Police found a suicide note in their pocket. In it, they held Garima responsible for their death. The doctor had been defrauded of ₹1.40 crore. Complaints from six other victims are also being investigated. Former BSA jailed in teacher suicide case gives career advice Suspended Deoria BSA Shalini Srivastava is in jail for allegedly forcing teacher Krishna Bhagwan Singh to die by suicide. Teacher Devaria, a resident of Kushinagar, was an assistant teacher at Laghu Madhyamik Vidyalaya Madarson in the Gauri Bazar development block of Deoria. On 20 February 2026, he died by suicide at his brother's house in Shivpur Shahabganj, in Gorakhpur's Shahpur area. In his suicide note and video, he accused Shalini Srivastava and Sanjeev Singh, a clerk at the BSA office, of harassment. Police arrested Shalini, who carried a ₹25,000 reward, in Delhi. Shalini has good knowledge of education and careers. In jail, she gives other women inmates tips on building their careers. Efforts to make inmates self-reliant through training Jail Superintendent Dilip Pandey said help is being sought from several organisations to make women inmates self-reliant after they leave the jail. They are being provided training in beauty therapy and sewing and embroidery. He said efforts were being made to provide inmates with a positive environment through education, training and other creative activities. The prison administration is also providing books, notebooks and the materials needed for training. The aim is to help inmates begin a better life after leaving prison, using their skills.

stories.title: Fog blankets 15 cities in UP, haze engulfs Lucknow:Night temperatures drop below 20°C across state; cold conditions likely to intensify on Diwali
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified across Uttar Pradesh. Fog covered 15 cities, including Shravasti, Deoria, Maharajganj, Sambhal and Barabanki, on Saturday morning. A layer of haze was also visible in Lucknow as air pollution levels rose, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) nearing 200. Meanwhile, rising pollution levels in the NCR and western Uttar Pradesh have become a major concern. Noida's AQI crossed 400, while air quality in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat also slipped into the red zone. Over the past 24 hours, night-time temperatures fell below 20°C across the state. Hardoi recorded the lowest temperature at 14°C. Daytime temperatures also dropped below 35°C, with Jhansi recording the highest at 34°C. Prof. Manoj Srivastava, a meteorologist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said, “Temperatures are likely to fall further during Diwali week. Fog may persist in the mornings. With the change in weather, the chill during the morning and evening hours will become more pronounced.” 2 pictures of fog and haze- What will the weather be like from western Uttar Pradesh to Purvanchal on Diwali? Western UP: The weather is expected to remain dry for now in Noida, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Agra and Mathura. Light mist may be seen in the morning. Central UP: There is currently no possibility of rain in Lucknow, Kanpur, Unnao, Sitapur, Hardoi and Rae Bareli. The day may remain sunny, while light chill may be felt at night. Purvanchal: The weather is also expected to remain dry in Varanasi, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur and Deoria. Light mist may be seen in some places in the morning. Bundelkhand: There is currently no indication of rain in Jhansi, Banda, Chitrakoot, Mahoba, Hamirpur and Lalitpur either. Exercise caution while sowing and irrigating rabi crops In view of the possibility of rain in November, farmers have been advised to remain vigilant in managing rabi crops. In particular, they should ensure proper drainage in their fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard, especially in Purvanchal. Waterlogging in low-lying fields could damage the crops. Avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where there is sufficient moisture due to rainfall. Make decisions on sowing and irrigation only after considering the weather conditions and soil moisture. stories.title: Blast at Ghaziabad police outpost, ACs and windows shattered:1 injured; Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen claims responsibility
stories.summary: A powerful blast occurred at a police outpost in Ghaziabad on Friday night. The blast was so powerful that the windows in the rooms were shattered. Air conditioners exploded, and a crack appeared in the wall. The sound of the blast could be heard nearly one kilometre away. Fortunately, no police personnel were inside. However, a 20-year-old food delivery worker was injured in the incident. He is undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital. Meanwhile, the terrorist organisation 'Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen' claimed responsibility for the blast in a social media post. Police have begun investigating the social media post. ACP Indirapuram and DCP Trans Hindon Rijul also reached the spot and gathered information about the incident. The incident took place at 9 p.m. at the Vasundhara police outpost in the Indirapuram police station area. See pictures of the blast- Police examine CCTV footage from elevated road The Vasundhara police outpost is located beneath an elevated road. Police sources claim that someone may have thrown an explosive substance from the road above, triggering the blast. CCTV footage from cameras installed along the elevated road is being examined as part of the investigation. Blast may have been caused by seized firecrackers Local residents said police personnel used to keep firecrackers seized from shops selling them illegally in the area at the outpost. They suspect the explosion may have occurred due to these seized firecrackers. However, the police have not openly commented on the possibility of a firecracker blast. Forensic team examines site, says DCP DCP (Trans Hindon) Rijul said an investigation was underway after the police received information about the blast. A forensic team is present at the spot. He said it would be appropriate to comment on the cause only after the investigation is complete. He also said the outpost remained closed for most of the time. Terror outfit claims responsibility, says police were targeted Following the blast, a terror outfit named Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen Hindustan posted a video on social media claiming responsibility for the explosion. The group also shared a note in English alongside the video. The video shows a masked man speaking first in Urdu and later in Hindi, claiming responsibility for the blast. He says the group targeted the police as part of an action against the “saffron regime”. He also claims that they have the right to protect their homes and alleges that the police, Army and judiciary are all being used against them. After the video surfaced, the police stepped up their investigation, while the cyber cell also began examining the matter. Police and investigating agencies found that the account from which the video and post were uploaded during the night had since been deleted. BJP MLA warns of strong retaliation against those behind the blast BJP MLA from Loni, Nand Kishore Gurjar, said the organisation claiming responsibility for the blast should know who governs Uttar Pradesh. He said the government would not tolerate such acts by what he described as jihadists during the festival of Diwali. He added that the police would soon send those responsible “to the 72 virgins”. Appealing to people not to worry during Diwali, Gurjar urged them to celebrate the festival without fear. “They will receive such a response that their next seven generations will remember it. Even if we have to enter Pakistan and strike them, our country will not back down,” he said.
