stories.title: Air worsens in 10 UP cities; haze in Lucknow, Kanpur:Prayagraj's AQI crosses 500; severe cold likely in 3 days
stories.summary: Pollution levels increased across Uttar Pradesh after firecrackers were burst on Diwali night. At 7 am on Monday, the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossed 500 in Prayagraj, Gorakhpur and Lucknow. Ten cities, including Noida, Ghaziabad, Kanpur and Varanasi, recorded AQI levels in the red zone. Meanwhile, cold weather and fog have also started affecting the state. More than 15 cities, including Sambhal, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Gonda and Maharajganj, witnessed fog in the morning. Night temperatures have dropped below 15°C. Visibility on roads has fallen to just 50 metres in some areas, making it difficult for drivers to see ahead. The weather department has said that severe cold is likely to begin in Uttar Pradesh after three days. Professor Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said minimum temperatures would fall further as dry north-westerly winds become stronger. He added that the cold would become more intense across the state. Find out how major cities are doing- See the weather pictures- What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates air quality and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. The higher the AQI, the more hazardous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it through the graphic below: How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone in the air penetrate deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream and can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate effects to long-term complications. Prolonged exposure reduces lung capacity and increases the risk of chronic diseases. Understand it through the graphic below:

stories.title: Lucknow's AQI crosses 300 on Diwali night:Firecrackers worsen air quality; elderly people face breathing problems
stories.summary: Heavy firecracker bursting on Diwali night has worsened air quality in Lucknow, with the city's Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 300. Several areas recorded poor air quality, while people faced breathing difficulties due to smoke and haze. The elderly and people with breathing problems have been advised to take special care. Talkatora recorded the highest AQI at 304, followed by Lalbagh at 283. The AQI in Aliganj was also close to 300. The high pollution levels have made it difficult for people to breathe. Meanwhile, the AQI remained in the yellow zone at some other locations. Ambedkar University recorded an AQI of 156, Gomti Nagar 169 and Kukrail Picnic Spot 167. Daytime temperature reaches 31 degrees The maximum temperature on Sunday was recorded at 30 degrees Celsius, while the minimum was 17 degrees Celsius. On Saturday, the maximum temperature stood at 31 degrees Celsius and the minimum at 17.3 degrees Celsius. Humidity was recorded at 66%. Fog is likely in the coming days. Moderate fog may occur in some areas during the morning hours but is expected to clear as the sun rises. Impact of Cyclone Arnab ends Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said the impact of Cyclone Arnab has now ended. There is no chance of rain at present. Bright sunshine is expected to make the days feel slightly warmer, while night temperatures will remain below 20°C. The cold is likely to become more intense during the early morning hours.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in Lakhimpur market, 50 shops gutted:Fire engines called in from Nepal; blaze triggered by Diwali lamps
stories.summary: A massive fire engulfed a market in Lakhimpur Kheri on Diwali night. More than 50 shops were reduced to ashes one after another. The fire spread so rapidly that the shopkeepers did not even get a chance to remove their goods. Fire engines had to be called in from Nepal as well as India to bring the situation under control. The shopkeepers suffered losses running into lakhs. The fire broke out in the Gauriphanta Kotwali area, 110 kilometres from the district headquarters. The matter concerns the Gauriphanta Kotwali area. Pictures of the massive fire.... Bangawan market is located right next to the India-Nepal border. The Nepal border is around 2 km from here. Nepal's Dhangadhi city is around 5 km away. The market has hundreds of fruit and vegetable shops, as well as grocery shops. A fire suddenly broke out in the market on Diwali night. Before long, it spread to the nearby shops. More than 50 shops were reduced to ashes. Fire engines also arrived from Dhangadhi in Nepal Fire engines from Lakhimpur, Gola and Nighasan reached the scene. In view of the severity of the fire, the administration sought help from Nepal as well as India. At the request of BJP leader Ravi Gupta, Gopi Hamal, mayor of Nepal's Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City, sent two fire engines and a JCB to Bangawan Mandi. Nepal's municipal police team also assisted in the relief and rescue operations. It is suspected that, because of Diwali, the shopkeepers lit lamps in their shops and went home. The fire may have started from a burning lamp in one of the shops before spreading to the neighbouring shops. However, the actual cause of the fire has not yet been confirmed.

stories.title: BJP plans to pacify 10,000 leaders for 2027 victory:Strategy aims to resolve rifts among UP MPs and MLAs
stories.summary: Discontent among MPs, MLAs and party workers has become a major headache for the BJP. Uttar Pradesh has more than 10,000 senior leaders who have a strong hold in their respective areas but are unwilling to work together. With assembly elections just three months away, the BJP does not want to risk losing support because of their resentment. Home Minister Amit Shah has also realised the seriousness of the situation. During a meeting in Lucknow on October 30, he said, “Whatever disappointment or resentment you have, leave it in the Gomti river when you leave this place. We have to remain united.” The party is now working on two strategies to win back its disgruntled old workers. State president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh are reaching out to unhappy MPs, MLAs and office-bearers. At the same time, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) functionaries are also trying to persuade these leaders to work in line with the party. Lists of 25 such people have been prepared for every Assembly constituency in UP. They are former key party office-bearers who have not been active for a long time because of their resentment. The internal rifts are of three types: 1. In several districts, MPs and MLAs are at loggerheads. 2. MLAs and heads of urban local bodies are involved in disputes. 3. There are disagreements between MLAs and district presidents. The Opposition is gradually coming together ahead of 2027. If differences among these leaders are not resolved, the BJP could face a bigger challenge in the Assembly elections. First, let us understand how these disputes came to light… BJP state in-charge Vinod Tawde, state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh have been visiting different districts since September 17. An outreach campaign is being conducted across the Gorakh, West, Braj, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Awadh and Kashi regions. According to party sources, wherever the state in-charge and state president have visited, they have found more internal rivalry among party leaders than enthusiasm among workers. In some places, block chiefs and municipal council presidents do not even want to see each other. In others, MPs and MLAs are working against one another. Several district panchayat presidents are also not supporting their own MPs and MLAs. From west to east: Understanding the battles being fought in the name of ‘respect and recognition’ Fatehpur Sikri: Two separate rivalries 1. MLA Babulal and MP Rajkumar are at odds Chaudhary Babulal was an MP from Fatehpur Sikri in 2014. When Babulal was denied a ticket in the 2009 election, the party fielded Rajkumar Chahar instead. Political rivalry between the two has continued ever since and remains unresolved. 2. Bah MLA Rani Pakshalika Singh is also at loggerheads with MP Rajkumar Chahar The conflict between Rani Pakshalika Singh, MLA from Bah and a member of the Bhadaur royal family, and MP Rajkumar Chahar is primarily linked to influence and political credit. Both leaders claim credit for government projects in the Bah area, including roads, bridges and the foundation-laying ceremony for a government college. Bulandshahr: MP and MLAs unable to work together Dr Bhola Singh has been elected MP for the third consecutive time and also serves as a national secretary in the party organisation. On the other hand, Sadar MLA Pradeep Chaudhary and Dibai MLA Chandrapal Singh have strong public support and influence in their respective constituencies. Both camps function as parallel centres of power in their areas, leading to clashes over political dominance. Gautam Buddha Nagar: MP and MLA compete for credit for development work The political distance between BJP MP Dr Mahesh Sharma and Dhirendra Singh, the party's MLA from Jewar, has persisted for several reasons. Dr Mahesh Sharma has long been regarded as one of the most influential leaders in Gautam Buddha Nagar. Meanwhile, Dhirendra Singh is popular in the Jewar Assembly constituency, and his influence is gradually expanding across the district. The competition to claim credit for development work has strained relations between the two. Muzaffarnagar: Allegations of working to defeat each other The rivalry between former MP Sanjeev Balyan and former Sardhana MLA Sangeet Som is now out in the open. Balyan alleges that Som worked against him in the Lok Sabha election. Balyan is now accused of creating obstacles for Som in return. The rivalry involving Muzaffarnagar and Sardhana has emerged from the results of the 2022 and 2024 elections, regional caste polarisation involving the Jat and Thakur communities, and the competition to maintain political standing within the party. Saharanpur: Allegations of not supporting the party in the Lok Sabha election Yogi government minister Brajesh Singh and Raghav Lakhanpal Sharma, the party's candidates in the 2024 election, are locked in a dispute. The Raghav Lakhanpal camp believed that voting in favour of the party in Rajput-dominated areas and constituencies influenced by the minister was lower than expected. Meanwhile, the minister's supporters argued that they had fulfilled their responsibility by helping Raghav Lakhanpal secure a lead in the Deoband seat. Kairana: Claim of contesting against the sitting MLA The dispute between former Kairana candidate Pradeep Chaudhary and Gangoh MLA Keerat Singh has escalated to such an extent that Pradeep Chaudhary is now staking a claim to contest from the Gangoh seat himself. Pilibhit: Minister of State and municipal chairperson clash over credit A power struggle is continuing between Minister of State Sanjay Singh Gangwar and municipal chairperson Aastha Agarwal. The dispute in Pilibhit Municipal Council centres on administrative control over development projects in the city, the tender process and the competition to establish political dominance in the municipal area. Here are some other disputes in different districts… Several reasons behind the disputes within the BJP BJP sources say that MPs and MLAs want to establish their own dominance in most constituencies. They try to project themselves as more influential than other leaders so that they can claim credit for getting development funds allocated and released. There is also internal competition over securing posts for their supporters and close associates within the organisation. Caste-related tensions are also visible within the party. In some places, Jats and Thakurs are at odds, while in others, disputes involve Brahmins and Thakurs or Kurmis and Thakurs. Senior leaders are still struggling to adjust to the newer faces in the party. Leaders who have joined from other parties are also not being readily accepted. Preparing to settle scores over the Lok Sabha election The BJP's biggest concern is the alleged internal sabotage during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Former MPs who lost those elections and sitting MPs are now taking on MLAs from their own party. Several leaders allege that some party MLAs worked to defeat or weaken their own candidates during the Lok Sabha polls. Candidates who lost the Lok Sabha elections and sitting MPs are now trying to get these MLAs denied tickets for the Assembly elections. Several MPs are making visits to Delhi and Lucknow to pursue the matter. They argue that if these MLAs are given tickets again, the party could lose those seats. Strategy to win back 25 disgruntled workers in every constituency BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary believes that boosting the morale of workers at the grassroots level can turn the tide in an election. Therefore, the party is preparing a list of 25 former influential workers from every Assembly constituency who have become inactive after falling out with the party. RSS cadres will also be sent to the homes of these workers to make them feel valued and remind them that they are part of the organisation.

stories.title: Ayodhya lights up with 30 lakh diyas, fireworks illuminate sky:Ramayana showcased through laser show; Vice-President, CM Yogi attend
stories.summary: The 10th Deepotsav is being celebrated in Ayodhya today. Around 30 lakh diyas were lit across 56 ghats on the banks of the Saryu River. The story of the Ramayana was displayed through a laser show at Ram Ki Paidi and Saryu Ghat. A special aerial show was conducted using 2,100 drones. On the banks of the Saryu, 2,147 priests performed the Maha Aarti of the Saryu River, which was followed by a fireworks display. Prior to this, a grand procession was taken out in Ayodhya for about 3 hours, featuring 21 tableaux (jhankis) that depicted the seven Kands (chapters) of the Ramayana. People from across the country, including Mumbai, Gujarat, and Bihar, arrived to witness the Deepotsav. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and several ministers were also present at the event.

stories.title: All top 50 cities with worst air quality are Indian:Half are in UP; this is the pre-Diwali situation, what lies ahead after the festival?
stories.summary: The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several Uttar Pradesh cities is crossing 1,000, according to private websites that monitor air quality. However, government figures remain around 500. This is because government monitoring systems do not report readings above 500. This is happening even before Diwali firecrackers have been burst. Why do government machines not report figures above 500? Is the government hiding something from the public? Why has air quality suddenly deteriorated before Diwali? Let's find out in UP Explainer… Question 1: What is the government trying to hide by capping AQI at 500? Answer: The intention behind this is not to hide information. When the AQI system was introduced in India in 2014, this limit was set because of the technical limitations of government systems, administrative rules and scientific assumptions at the time. However, experts believe this formula is now outdated and needs to be changed immediately. In 2014, when scientists at IIT Kanpur developed India's AQI system, they had not anticipated that pollution levels in the country could ever cross 500. The computer software and mathematical formula they developed had its highest range ending at 500. The government has not upgraded this outdated formula in the past 12 years. As a result, government machines cannot process data beyond 500. Former director of SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research), Prof Dr Gufran Beig, explains that the government system flattens the data. All readings above 500 are treated as the same, even when pollution levels may vary significantly. He says removing this cap is essential. On the other hand, private agencies such as IQAir and aqi.in can calculate readings above 500. When the concentration of pollutants in the air rises sharply, their formulas calculate the AQI and can show readings of 800, 1,000 or even higher. Therefore, their figures provide a fuller picture of the actual and extremely dangerous air pollution levels. According to NDTV, on November 20, 2025, IQAir recorded Delhi's AQI at 506, while the government reading was 399. This means an independent monitoring agency recorded a figure above 500, while the government system did not. A comparison of AQI figures for November 5 between 2022 and 2026, based on US standards, shows that air quality in major Uttar Pradesh cities has deteriorated sharply over the past five years. In 2022, Meerut's AQI was 180. By 2026, it had risen to 582, an increase of 223%. The situation looked even worse at 9 am on November 6. According to international AQI monitoring website aqi.in, the city's AQI stood at 1,059 at that time. According to the website's live AQI tracking, at 4.18 pm on November 6, all 50 cities with the worst air quality in the world were in India. Of these, 21 were in Uttar Pradesh. Firozabad topped the list in the state with an AQI of 463, followed by Agra at 430. If a similar situation occurred in an American city, a health emergency would be declared. More or less the same conditions are being seen in major UP cities such as Ghaziabad, Noida, Hapur, Lucknow, Prayagraj and Gorakhpur. This situation has continued since November 1, a week before Diwali. Data from the past five years shows that pollution levels were at their lowest in almost all these cities in 2024. However, there was a sharp rise in 2025 and 2026. Air quality in districts bordering Delhi, such as Meerut and Ghaziabad, has deteriorated to extremely dangerous levels much faster than in Awadh and Purvanchal. A joint analysis of both datasets – the five-year figures and the maximum AQI readings recorded over 24 hours – reveals two important aspects of Uttar Pradesh's air quality. I) Morning walks can harm your health: The worst AQI readings of the day are being recorded in the morning, particularly from 6 am onwards. This is also when people go for morning walks, children head to school and office-goers commute. An AQI of 1,059 in Meerut means that people's lungs are being exposed to pollution equivalent to the smoke from around 50 cigarettes every day. II) A silent pollution trap at night: The AQI in Kanpur reaching 664 at 12.30 am shows that night-time air is just as polluted as during the day. Falling temperatures, industrial emissions and the movement of heavy goods vehicles in and out of the city are contributing to the problem. Question 2: Why is air quality extremely poor this year even before firecrackers are burst? Answer: There is no single reason behind this. Changing weather conditions, slow wind speeds and the accumulation of smoke and pollutants at the local level are the main factors. The situation can be understood through the following points… I) Falling temperatures and cold winds create a trap As the weather gets colder, the air close to the ground cools down and becomes heavier. This year, temperatures dropped sharply due to Cyclone Arnab and active western disturbances. Between late October and early November, temperatures in UP fell suddenly by 8 to 9 degrees. Cold air acts like a lid, preventing smoke released by vehicles and factories from rising into the atmosphere. Instead, it traps the pollutants close to the ground, where people breathe. II) Slow wind speeds Strong winds carry smoke and dust away. However, wind speeds remained very low in the days leading up to Diwali this year. With little wind to disperse them, pollutants accumulated in the same areas, making the air increasingly toxic with each passing day. III) Change in the timing of stubble burning In 2025, Diwali fell on October 20. At the time, winter was just beginning, winds were blowing and temperatures were relatively warm. As a result, firecracker smoke was carried away by the wind, while paddy harvesting had not yet begun. This meant there was little smoke from stubble burning. This year, temperatures have already dropped by November. Around 85% of the paddy crop has been harvested in neighbouring states such as Punjab and Haryana. As a result, smoke from stubble burning has been drifting towards Uttar Pradesh. IV) Rising pollution at the local level Markets are witnessing heavy crowds due to the Diwali festivities. Smoke from vehicles stuck in traffic jams for hours is further worsening air quality. Dust rising from roads and fine particles (PM2.5) released by ongoing construction work are also suspended in the air. Simply put, even before firecrackers are burst this year, a combination of natural factors (weather conditions and low wind speeds) and human activities (stubble burning, traffic and dust) has trapped pollutants close to the ground. This is making the air feel twice as polluted as it was last year.

stories.title: Anant Singh reaches Varanasi with 400-vehicle convoy:Police stop him, ask him to go to BHU with 5 vehicles; he refuses
stories.summary: Anant Singh, MLA from Mokama in Bihar, arrived in Varanasi at around 5 p.m. on Friday with a convoy of 400 vehicles. However, citing the traffic arrangements amid the Dhanteras and Diwali crowds, the police stopped him in the Dafi area outside the city. Anant Singh wanted to go to BHU and lay flowers at the statue of Mahamana Madan Mohan Malaviya. The administration said it would allow him to go to BHU with only five vehicles. Anant Singh refused to go under those conditions. He said, "We do not travel with so few vehicles. If permission has not been granted, we will not go." After this, at around 5.30 p.m., the police sent him to Prayagraj from outside the city. During this time, his supporters also argued with the police. MLA Anant Singh left Patna for Prayagraj in the morning with 100 vehicles. Supporters kept joining him along the way. At around 8 p.m., he attended a wedding ceremony at the home of his old friend Pappu Salman in Prayagraj. He left Prayagraj at 9 p.m. See 2 pictures... Garlanding the Malviya statue at BHU BHU student leader Dr Saurav Rai said that Anant Singh was due to visit his home. He was also scheduled to meet his mother. In addition, he was to lay a wreath at the statue of Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya at BHU. Dr Saurav Rai said he had obtained permission for the programme from the administration in advance, but later the convoy of 400 vehicles was stopped at Dafi itself. Only five vehicles were allowed to enter, following which Anant Singh said he would not go with five vehicles, and the convoy left from there for Prayagraj. Anant Singh had also set out to distribute invitations to his daughter's wedding Anant Singh was travelling from Bihar to Prayagraj. He was to attend the Walima ceremony for the son of his old friend, Pappu Salman. During the journey, he was also distributing invitations to the wedding of his daughter, Shivangi, which is scheduled for 25 November. Supporters welcomed him in Ara, Buxar and Chandauli along the way. In Chandauli, he met BJP MLA Sushil Singh and also gave him an invitation to his daughter's wedding. JD(U) expelled him for six years on 24 October Anant Singh is the MLA from Mokama in Bihar. The Janata Dal United (JDU) expelled him from the party for six years on 24 October. The party accused him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. In the election for the Patna Graduates' constituency of the Bihar Legislative Council, Anant Singh supported Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh instead of JDU candidate Neeraj Kumar. He also campaigned against the party leadership's instructions. In addition, he was accused of making statements against senior party leaders. Following this, the JDU expelled him. Must surrender by 4 December, daughter's wedding on 25 November In the Dularchand Yadav murder case, the Supreme Court has ordered Anant Singh to surrender before the concerned investigating officer by 4 December or earlier. Anant Singh's younger daughter Shivangi is to get married on 25 November. Despite the wedding preparations, he has remained continuously active in his constituency.

stories.title: ‘I wouldn’t have stolen if I knew it was UP’:Accused confesses to stealing ₹5 crore jewellery on bus
stories.summary: I did not even realise when the moving bus entered Uttar Pradesh. Had I known I was in UP, I would not have committed the theft. This is the confession of Amol Maruti Pitekar, the accused in the theft of jewellery worth ₹5 crore. He allegedly stole the jewellery from a private bus in Jhansi on October 29. To trace the accused, the police examined CCTV footage covering nearly 2,000 kilometres, from Jhansi to Maharashtra. During the investigation, they obtained the vehicle's registration number and FASTag details. Based on these clues, the police raided a location in Ahilyanagar, Maharashtra, on November 3 and arrested Amol (29). He was brought to Jhansi on Friday under transit remand. His father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar, is the alleged mastermind of this Maharashtra-based gang of thieves. The police are searching for his father and five other gang members. During interrogation, Amol said that the gang had planned to commit theft in Madhya Pradesh, but the bus unknowingly entered Uttar Pradesh. According to him, this was the gang's first theft in UP. Read the full case in detail Jhansi SSP Vikas Kumar said that Gurkirat Singh, a resident of Amritsar in Punjab, is a major jewellery trader. He manufactures gold jewellery and supplies it to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. This time, he had travelled from Amritsar to Madhya Pradesh. After supplying jewellery in Jabalpur and then Chhatarpur, he boarded a private bus on October 29 to travel from Chhatarpur to Jhansi. The businessman travelled with valuable jewellery in ordinary bags, like other passengers. He placed five bags containing jewellery on the luggage racks above the seats. Two bags were on his side and three on the opposite side. Three members of the gang were already travelling on the bus. As soon as the bus stopped at the Mauranipur bus stand, the three thieves got off with two bags containing jewellery. CCTV footage shows them getting off the bus with the bags. They then escaped in a white Scorpio. The stolen jewellery is estimated to be worth around ₹5 crore. CCTV footage helped investigators make progress SSP Vikas Kumar said that eight police teams had been formed to solve the case. It was a difficult investigation because the police had no concrete leads. They had only a blurry CCTV recording, which became the starting point of the investigation. The police teams tracked the Scorpio and examined CCTV footage covering more than 2,000 kilometres, working day and night. This helped them identify the vehicle's registration number. The FASTag details then led the police to the gang in Maharashtra. The police arrested one of the gang members, Amol Maruti Pitekar (29), along with money allegedly linked to the theft. He is a resident of Mahalangi village in the Karjat police station area of Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra. His father's name is Maruti Rajaram Pitekar. According to the SSP, the accused was brought from Maharashtra to Jhansi on transit remand. He will be produced before a court, where the police will seek his custody for further questioning. The Scorpio used in the crime is registered in Amol's name. Father gave him ₹20 lakh to repay his debt The SSP said that during interrogation, Amol revealed that his father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar, was the gang leader. His father had carried out the theft with four associates. They had travelled in the Scorpio via Jabalpur to Chhatarpur and then to Mauranipur. After the theft, they returned to Maharashtra along the same route. According to Amol, after the theft, his father called him and asked him to meet in the town of Rashin. After selling the stolen jewellery, his father gave him ₹20 lakh and told him to repay his debt. He deposited the money in his bank accounts. On November 3, he was on his way to the registry office to repay the debt when the police arrested him. The police recovered ₹1.40 lakh in cash and two mobile phones from the accused. They also froze ₹17.06 lakh deposited in his three bank accounts. Gang has committed thefts in 5 to 7 states According to the SSP, the gang mainly targets gold traders. It has allegedly committed thefts in five to seven states, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

stories.title: Five women die in Sitapur road accident:Truck hits tractor-trolley returning from mundan ceremony, 17 injured
stories.summary: A speeding truck rammed into a tractor-trolley carrying devotees from behind in Sitapur. The impact caused the trolley to overturn, killing five people. Around 17 people, including two women and a child, were seriously injured. They were returning to Bargawan village after attending a mundan ceremony at a Shiva temple in Khatele, Hardoi. There were screams and cries for help at the scene following the accident. With the assistance of local residents, the police took the injured to the Community Health Centres (CHCs) in Pisawan and Maholi. Some of those in critical condition have been referred to Sitapur for further treatment. The police are taking necessary action in the case. Read the full details of the incident… Around 15 people from Bargawan village had travelled to Hardoi in a tractor-trolley on Friday to attend a mundan ceremony. At 5 pm, they were returning after the mundan ceremony of Abhi, the son of Guddu's sister. Meanwhile, a truck coming from behind rammed into the tractor-trolley near Himmatnagar village in the Pisawan police station area. The impact caused the trolley to overturn, injuring the people on board. On Friday, Abhi, the son of Guddu's sister, a resident of Bargawan village, had gone with Harinam, a resident of Narikhera village (Pihani police station area, Hardoi), to attend a mundan ceremony at the Shiva temple in Khatele. Other residents of Bargawan village had also accompanied them in the tractor-trolley. Everyone was returning after the ceremony on Friday. Meanwhile, a truck coming from behind rammed into the tractor-trolley near Himmatnagar on the Bargawan-Kulha Ghat road in the Pisawan police station area. The impact was so severe that the tractor-trolley went out of control and overturned on the road. The passengers were trapped underneath and injured. 17 injured taken to Pisawan and Maholi CHCs After the accident, local residents rushed to the spot. On receiving information, the police, with the help of local people, rescued those trapped and took the injured by ambulance to the CHCs in Pisawan and Maholi. The 17 people injured in the accident were identified as Premwati (50), Ramwati (50), Asha (73), Chameli (55), Gudiya, Ruby (28), Kalpana (30), Kanchana (12), Dulari (30), Rambeti (48), Ramdevi (50), Ramsukhi (55), Jahnavi (12), Munni Devi, Jitu (10), Mayawati (65) and Unnati (12). Premwati sustained an injury to her right leg, while Ramwati suffered a head injury. Dulari is reported to have fractured her leg. As Premwati, Ramwati and Unnati were in a critical condition, they were referred to Sitapur for better treatment. The other injured are also undergoing treatment at hospitals. Five women die at Maholi CHC Five other women injured in the accident had been taken to the CHC in Maholi for treatment. They died during treatment. The deceased have been identified as Kajal, daughter of Dataram; Sushila (50), wife of Vishnu; Ruby (22), daughter of Vishnu; and Sunita (40), wife of Ramkumar. All four were residents of Bargawan village. The identity of the fifth woman is yet to be established. The police are working to identify her. Police reach the spot after accident, action underway According to the police, a team reached the spot as soon as it received information about the accident and made arrangements to take the injured to hospital. Necessary action is being taken in connection with the accident. The village is in mourning following the incident.

stories.title: Woman killed over alleged affair with nephew:Husband attacks her with grinding stone in Prayagraj; she returned home 3 days ago
stories.summary: A woman was allegedly beaten to death by her husband with a grinding stone in Prayagraj on Friday. He repeatedly hit her face, eyes and forehead, killing her on the spot. The incident took place around 2:30 am on Thursday in the Puramufti police station area. After receiving information, the police reached the spot and took the accused husband into custody. During questioning, he told the police that he suspected his wife of having an affair with her nephew. The couple often argued over the issue, according to the police. Now read the full case Suman Kumar lived with his wife, Bijma Devi (28), in Mandra village under the jurisdiction of Puramufti. They had been married for 10 years. Bijma was a resident of Sheikhpur village in the Charwa police station area of Kaushambi. They have three children. Their eldest daughter is four years old. The other two children are three and two years old. Murder reported at 2:30 a.m. At around 2:30 a.m. on Thursday night, a murder was reported on Dial-112. It was reported that a woman had been murdered inside her home in Mandra village. The Dial-112 team reached the spot first. Puramufti police then arrived at the scene. The woman's blood-soaked body was lying inside the house. Police cordoned off the scene, began an investigation and detained her husband, Suman Kumar, on suspicion. The woman had returned from her parental home just three days earlier The police's preliminary investigation has revealed that the husband and wife had been involved in a dispute for a long time. During questioning, the accused husband, Suman Kumar, said that his wife was having an illicit relationship with his nephew. The couple would quarrel frequently over this issue. The accused said that his wife had met the young man again on Wednesday night. This led to another dispute between them, after which he killed his wife. Suman had brought his wife back from her parental home just three days earlier. Father informed of daughter's murder at 7 a.m. After the incident, the police informed the woman's family. They then took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. The woman's father, Rambhavan, said he received a call from Puramufti police station at around 7 a.m. The police informed him that his daughter had been murdered. DCP City Sagar Jain said: “The initial investigation suggests that the case stems from a dispute between the husband and wife. Police are investigating all aspects. The husband has been taken into custody and is being questioned.”

stories.title: Wife meets Azam Khan at Dasna Jail:Claims he is being kept without a bed amid unhygienic conditions
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's wife, Tanzeen Fatima, reached Dasna Jail in Ghaziabad at around 12 noon to meet him. She spoke to Senior Jail Superintendent Sitaram Sharma for about an hour. She was then allowed to meet Azam Khan. After the meeting, Tanzeen Fatima said, "The actual conditions are not good. There is neither a bed nor a cot." Tanzeen Fatima was accompanied by her elder son, Adeeb Azam, and her foster daughter, Ekta Kaushik. Other family members and supporters remained outside the jail. The district administration arranged her meeting with Azam Khan in the same way as it does for other inmates. The Local Intelligence Unit (LIU) also remained on alert during the meeting. Azam Khan has been lodged in Dasna Jail since 1 November. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him at the gate of Rampur Jail. He was then produced before the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad, which sent him to Dasna Jail in 14 days' judicial custody. She said, 'Azam Khan is being kept in filthy conditions' After meeting Azam Khan, his wife and former Rajya Sabha MP Tazeen Fatima expressed anger over his conditions in prison. She said, "A person who has been an MLA 10 times and has served as a member of both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha is being kept in filthy conditions in prison. I, too, have been a Rajya Sabha MP." Tazeen Fatima said Azam Khan was being kept as though he might escape. "Murderers roam around openly, but such treatment is being meted out to Azam Sahib," she said. We have informed the court that his health is not good. He has suffered a stroke. We have also submitted all his medical reports to the court. Despite this, he is being kept in such conditions in jail. She said - getting him out of jail is the first objective Tanzeen Fatima said that their first objective was to get Azam Khan out of jail. "We are making every effort to achieve this. A hearing has been scheduled in the High Court. We hope that Azam Khan will soon be released from jail and receive justice from the court," she said. ED arrested Azam Khan as soon as he was released from jail On 29 October, the Allahabad High Court suspended the 10-year sentences of Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam in the fake PAN card case and granted them bail. Both were released from Rampur Jail on 31 October. However, as soon as he came out of jail, the ED arrested Azam Khan, while his son Abdullah Azam went home. The ED took Azam Khan directly to its head office in Delhi. There, he was asked more than 50 questions about the alleged use of government funds in the construction of Jauhar University. Sent to Dasna jail on the court's order On 1 November, the ED produced Azam Khan before the special PMLA court in Ghaziabad. The court sent him to Dasna jail in 14 days' judicial custody. When Azam Khan rolled down the car window during his court appearance, the media asked him, "Won't you say anything?" He replied, "What is left to say?" The ED action was taken in connection with alleged misuse of government funds in the construction of Jauhar University and a money-laundering case.

stories.title: Akhilesh says SIR could lead to loss of citizenship:Questions how 1.27 crore Hindu voters' names went missing and how CM knew about it
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Friday, "Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has claimed that the names of 1 crore 27 lakh Hindus have disappeared from the voter list. The question is: how does he know that the missing voters are Hindus?" He said, "The BJP had earlier been scaring people in the name of infiltrators, and is now talking about Hindu votes being removed. When your name is not on the voter list, the threat of losing your citizenship after the SIR will also arise." The Samajwadi Party chief claimed that the BJP would be defeated in Uttar Pradesh permanently this time. The people would give the BJP a grand farewell. Akhilesh sought a response from the Election Commission, alleging a conspiracy to remove names from the voter list. Suggestion to link voter ID with Aadhaar Akhilesh suggested linking the voter list to identity cards. He said that biometric data and retinal images of everyone are available. In such a situation, the identification system could be linked to the voter list. Alleged misuse of Form-7 Akhilesh alleged that after the SIR and SSIR, a conspiracy was hatched to delete votes on a large scale through Form-7. He said that Samajwadi Party workers and PDA sentinels detected this alleged irregularity. The practice of filing fake forms stopped after that. Citing the example of Nand Lal Nishad, he said that Form-7 was being filed in the name of a person who did not even know how to sign, with a signature obtained in his name. Akhilesh demanded that the Election Commission investigate the entire matter and take action against the officials responsible. Who is Nandlal Nishad, whose name Akhilesh mentioned According to the Samajwadi Party, Nandlal Nishad of Sultanpur does not know how to sign. The BJP allegedly had forged signatures made in Nandlal's name and used them to fill out the Election Commission's Form 7 (the form used to delete votes or remove names), so that the votes of around 26 people could be deleted. To bring the matter to light and expose the truth, Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav honoured Nandlal Nishad with a cash reward of ₹1 lakh for his bravery. After the matter came to light, the Election Commission took cognisance of it, and an FIR was registered in connection with the fraud and forged signatures.

stories.title: Uproar in Agra Municipal Corporation:Women councillors clash; BJP stages mock funeral of mic
stories.summary: A major commotion broke out during the Agra Municipal Corporation meeting on Friday as BJP and BSP councillors argued over who would speak first. The argument soon turned into a clash, with women councillors pushing and shoving each other. During the incident, BSP councillor Yashpal Singh picked up a microphone and threw it on the floor. His fellow councillor Sunil Sharma tied a black band over his eyes and sat in the well of the House. Several other councillors joined him and started a sit-in protest. Mayor Hemlata Diwakar repeatedly asked the councillors to calm down, but they did not listen. She then called the police and expelled Yashpal Singh from the meeting. Meanwhile, BJP councillors made a symbolic funeral bier for the microphone. They carried out a symbolic protest by beating their chests and pretending to cry. The commotion continued despite the mayor's repeated appeals. Upset over the situation, she left the meeting. After some time, BSP councillors persuaded her to return. The mayor came back, and the meeting resumed. Here is the full sequence of events- As the 17th session of the Agra Municipal Corporation began, BSP councillor Sunil Sharma told Mayor Hemlata Diwakar that he wanted to speak first. However, the mayor did not allow him to do so. She told him to let the House proceedings begin and that he could speak afterwards. However, Sunil Sharma ignored the mayor and began creating a ruckus. Expressing his displeasure with the mayor's decision, Sunil Sharma, the leader of the BSP councillor group, threw the microphone. BJP councillors then began raising slogans of "Hooliganism will not be tolerated". Soon, the two groups were confronting each other. BJP councillors staged a symbolic funeral procession for the broken microphone. Councillor Rakesh Kanojia placed a garland on the bier and expressed his grief. He then began beating his chest and crying. The mayor tried to calm him down, but the uproar did not stop. Seeing the situation spiral out of control, the mayor called the police. They brought the situation under control. Mayor leaves in anger, BSP councillors arrive to pacify her Meanwhile, the mayor left the House in anger. Some time later, BSP councillors went to persuade her to return. They said discussing people's problems was more important than the uproar. What happened was wrong. It should not have happened. The mayor then returned to the House. Mayor says - Incident is not forgivable, decision will be taken after inquiry Yashpal Singh and Sunil Sharma said that what happened should not have happened. If anyone has been hurt, they regret it. The mayor said that today's incident was condemnable. It was not worthy of forgiveness. However, both of you are also members of the House, so you are forgiven. The matter of breaking the microphone is subject to an inquiry. A decision will be taken after the inquiry.

stories.title: 3-day traffic diversion in Gorakhpur for Dhanteras Diwali:No entry for autos, e-rickshaws in Golghar, Ghantaghar and major markets
stories.summary: The traffic police have issued a three-day traffic diversion plan in view of the crowds expected in Gorakhpur's markets during Dhanteras and Diwali. Traffic restrictions will remain in place from 10 am to midnight on November 6, 7 and 8 on roads leading to major markets and nearby areas. During this period, loaders, auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed on several roads leading to Golghar, Ghantaghar, Reti, Nakhas and other major markets. People coming for shopping in cars and on two-wheelers have been asked to park their vehicles only at designated parking spots. Superintendent of Police (Traffic) Amit Srivastava said drivers have been asked to use the marked parking areas and follow traffic rules. Action will be taken against those who violate the rules. These routes will remain closed to three-wheelers Loaders, auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed from Kali Temple towards Golghar. Vehicles will not be allowed from Kachahari Chauraha towards Ganesh Chauraha or from GM Post Office Tiraha towards Ganesh Chauraha. Auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed from Tamkuhi Tiraha towards Kachahari Chauraha. These vehicles will also not be allowed from Shastri Chauraha towards Kachahari Chauraha. Auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed towards Ghosh Company, Reti Chowk and Nakhas Chauraha. Three-wheelers will not be allowed from the Normal Taxi Stand towards Ghantaghar Road or from Alhadadpur Tiraha towards Raiganj. These vehicles will also not be allowed from Durgabari Chauraha towards Charanlal Chauraha. Auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed from Sumer Sagar Tiraha towards Vijay Chowk or from Jatashankar Tiraha towards Alinagar. Three-wheelers will not be allowed on the routes from Barfkhana Tiraha towards Basantpur Chauraha, Ghantaghar Chauraha and Laldiggi. Auto-rickshaws and e-rickshaws will not be allowed from Madina Masjid Tiraha towards Shahmaruf. Heavy vehicles will follow these routes During the diversion, roadways buses, oil tankers, gas tankers, milk vehicles and other government vehicles will reach Bargadwa Chauraha through University Chauraha, Mohaddipur Chauraha, Charfataka Overbridge, Kauwabagh Bypass, Asuran Chauraha, Khajanchi Chauraha and Sports College Chauraha. From Bargadwa, they will move towards Farenda and Sonauli. Heavy vehicles coming from Farenda and Pipiganj towards Gorakhnath Temple will not be allowed to enter the city through their usual routes. They will be diverted towards Deoria and Kushinagar through Bargadwa Chauraha, Sports College, Khajanchi Chauraha, Asuran Chauraha, Kauwabagh Road, Charfataka Overbridge and Mohaddipur. Parking available at 8 locations The traffic police have marked eight parking locations for people visiting the markets for shopping. These include: Multilevel parking facility at Jalkal, Golghar Area opposite United Talkies on Cinema Road Kachahari Town Hall ground Kachahari Club parking Jalan Campus in Golghar Gorakhpur Haat near City Mall Vacant land next to Radha Madhav Parking areas of the malls and other establishments concerned

stories.title: 45 booked for blocking road in Varanasi:Protesters placed body on Chaubeypur-Babattpur road, ambulance stuck in traffic
stories.summary: Police have registered a case against 45 people after a road blockade following the death of 76-year-old Indrawati Devi in a road accident in Guruvat village, under the Chaubepur police station area of Varanasi. The accused include Brijesh Mishra and Ajay Yadav. They have been named for allegedly blocking the Chaubepur-Babatpur main road by placing the woman's body on it. Police have registered a case under eight sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and started an investigation. After Indrawati Devi's post-mortem, her body was handed over to the family on the evening of November 5. When the body reached home, villagers blocked the main road. This led to long queues of vehicles, and several ambulances also got stuck in the traffic. Police tried for a long time to persuade the family and villagers to end the protest. They finally agreed to clear the road, after which traffic returned to normal. Accused of inciting people for political gain Station in-charge Sadhuban Ram Gautam said the woman's body was handed over to her family after the post-mortem on November 5. The family was preparing for her cremation when Brijesh Mishra, a resident of Rajapur village, and Ajay Yadav, a resident of Guruvat village, allegedly encouraged them to block the road. Police said the two men allegedly wanted to use the protest for political gain ahead of the upcoming Assembly and panchayat elections. The blockade began around 6 pm and caused problems for patients and other commuters. Long queues of vehicles formed on the road, and ambulances were also stuck. Police cleared the road before registering the case The station in-charge said police started talks with the family after receiving information about the blockade. However, Brijesh Mishra and Ajay Yadav allegedly continued to encourage the protesters. After repeated efforts, police managed to calm the villagers. The body was then taken for cremation under police protection, and traffic was restored. Late at night, a case was registered at Cholapur police station on the complaint of Station House Officer Sadhuban Ram Gautam. The case names 45 people, including Brijesh Mishra and Ajay Yadav. Police have invoked Sections 61(2)(b), 126(2), 189(2), 190, 221, 223(b), 285 and 292 of the BNS. The investigation is underway, and further action will be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: Three family members killed after car falls into ditch:Couple and their child were returning home for Diwali
stories.summary: An uncontrolled Tata Tiago car fell into a deep, water-filled pit by the roadside in Hardoi. The husband, wife and their three-month-old son died in the accident. One young man travelling in the car was injured. Police reached the spot about an hour later and, with the help of villagers, pulled the occupants out using ropes. By then, the couple and their child had died, while the young man was found unconscious. He has been admitted to the district hospital in Kannauj. The accident took place at around 3:30 a.m. on Friday near Jafarpur turn on the Bilgram-Kannauj Road. The spot is about 50 km from the Hardoi district headquarters and 15 km from Kannauj. The family travelling in the car was returning to their home in Hardoi from Gurgaon for the Diwali holiday. See two pictures.. Know the full story Ramesh Kumar Kushwaha, 35, a resident of the Chand Baitha locality in the Hardoi Kotwali area, worked for a private company in Gurgaon. He had two brothers and one sister. Ramesh was the second of the three siblings. In December 2022, he married Neelam, 32, a resident of Gausganj in Sandila. After the wedding, Ramesh lived in Gurgaon with his wife. Neelam had given birth to their son, Abhimanyu, three months earlier. Ramesh's maternal uncle's son, Aditya, 28, also lived in Gurgaon with him. Aditya is a resident of Kakadeo in Kanpur. Brother said: They spoke at 6 p.m. Ramesh's brother, Sumesh, said, "My brother worked in Gurugram. He was returning home for the Diwali holiday. Aditya was driving the car. We spoke to him at 6 p.m. yesterday. My brother had said they would leave by car at 7 p.m. and reach home by morning." Kotwal says: Information received at 4 a.m. Bilgram Kotwal Vijay Kumar said information about the accident was received at 4 a.m. When the police team reached the spot, the car was completely submerged in water. With the help of villagers, they entered the water using ropes, opened the car doors, and pulled out the people inside. By then, the couple and child had died. A young man was found unconscious. He was immediately sent to Kannauj district hospital. The three bodies have been sent for post-mortem examinations.

stories.title: Defamation case filed against Dhirendra Shastri in Agra:Lawyers claim his comments hurt reputation of Krishna's descendants
stories.summary: A criminal defamation complaint has been filed against Baba Bageshwar Dham head Pandit Dhirendra Shastri in Agra over his remarks describing Lord Krishna as 'crooked'. Advocate Ajay Pratap Singh has filed the complaint in the civil court. He alleged that the remark had hurt the social reputation of descendants of Lord Krishna. The complaint mentions the Jadaun, Jadeja and Bhati Kshatriya lineages. The court registered the complaint on Thursday. The next hearing is scheduled for December 14. Dhirendra Shastri had apologised with folded hands On October 29, during a Ram Katha in Karera, Shivpuri, Dhirendra Shastri had said, "Hamare Ram Sidhe Hain, Jabki Tumhare Krishna Tedhe Han." As the controversy grew, he apologised with folded hands. He said Lord Ram and Lord Krishna were one and that he had no intention of distinguishing between them. Mohammad Faiz Khan backs Dhirendra Shastri Meanwhile, Mohammad Faiz Khan, national convenor of the Muslim Rashtriya Manch, has supported Shastri's remarks. He said the Opposition was worried about the Uttar Pradesh elections and six religious discourses. He added that Dhirendra Shastri was promoting Sanatan Dharma in India and abroad, and that attempts were being made to defame and implicate him for this reason. Complaint cites historical books In his complaint, Ajay Pratap Singh referred to the Mathura Gazetteer and Alexander Cunningham's book Report on Eastern Rajputana 1882–83. He claimed these documents mention the Jadaun, Jadeja and Bhati Kshatriya lineages. He also claimed to be a descendant of Lord Krishna through his maternal lineage. The complaint was filed before Judge Kanchan Kumari in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)-5. What did Shastri say during the Ram Katha? Pandit Dhirendra Shastri had addressed devotees attending the discourse, asking them to look at pictures of their deity, Lord Krishna. He said, "Look at even one picture of your Thakur Ji. See how he is seated or standing. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One leg rests over the other, his waist is bent and his head is tilted before he plays the flute." He then compared Lord Krishna with Lord Ram, saying, Hamare Ram Ekdum Sidhe Khade Hote Han. Unka Naam Bhi Sidha Hai, Unki Chaal Bhi Sidhi Hai Aur Ve Dikhte Bhi Sidhe Han. Tumhare Devta Ka Naam Tedha Hai, Ve Tedhe Chalte Hain Aur Khade Bhi Tedhe Hi Hote Han. 'Playing the flute is a pastime, but wielding a bow is not' While comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Shastri also referred to playing the flute and wielding a bow. He said, "Playing the flute is just a pastime, but wielding a bow is not." He then addressed the devotees, saying that Lord Krishna was also being praised that day. Pointing towards a musician playing the flute, he asked what their Thakur Ji did and remarked that playing the flute was not a big achievement. 'Grazing cows is easy, but making monkeys dance is not' Shastri also referred to Lord Krishna grazing cows and lifting Govardhan mountain. He said people might argue that their deity grazed cows, but anyone could do that. He sang, "Grazing cows is a pastime, but making monkeys dance is not." Referring to Lord Krishna lifting Govardhan mountain, he said people might claim that their deity could lift a mountain, but that was not a major achievement. He then said that a disciple of Lord Ram had lifted an entire mountain, referring to Lord Hanuman.

stories.title: Yogi says some appointment letters will be kept on hold:Plans to distribute them after third term; 4,543 get joining letters
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Friday that the BJP government had already provided 9.50 lakh government jobs. The promise of another one lakh jobs would also be fulfilled soon. "However, this time we will hold back some appointment letters and distribute them when we form the government for a third time." While handing appointment letters to 4,543 young people selected for the post of sub-inspector in Lucknow, the Chief Minister quipped. He asked, "Did anyone have to pay a bribe or use a recommendation?" He said that getting a job in Uttar Pradesh through financial dealings or intimidation was no longer possible. He said, "I have seen what happened between 2012 and 2017, and I have also seen what happened between 2003 and 2017. Several appointments were made in which one person applied, but the appointment letter was given to someone else. Several such cases are still pending in court." Yogi said, "I worry about what will happen if the court cancels those old recruitments in which irregularities were found. However, I would be very happy if the court ordered the confiscation of the property of the officials and dishonest people who played with the futures of young people." Key points from Yogi's address- 1. More appointment letters to be distributed immediately after Diwali Yogi said, "Immediately after Diwali, we will issue more than 1,200 appointment letters in the Revenue Department. After that, 4,000 young people will be given joining letters under the Home Guards recruitment process. Appointment letters will also be given to 32,000 constables." 2. If the BJP had not come to power, the selection process would have remained a dream Yogi said, "We have seen Uttar Pradesh change. I say this because if the 'double-engine' government had not come to power in Uttar Pradesh in 2017, this selection process might have remained just a dream."

stories.title: Brij Bhushan calls Rahul Gandhi ‘drunk without drinking’:Says Mann may drink, but not during the day; hits back at Congress MP
stories.summary: In Gonda, former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said, "Rahul Gandhi makes controversial statements every time. He is intoxicated even without drinking. His intoxication never wears off. He should reduce his intoxication." Rahul Gandhi holds the record for losing 91 elections. Perhaps no party in the country has lost so many elections under his leadership. He should get down to the ground and raise issues concerning the people. Speaking to news agency ANI on Thursday, Brij Bhushan Singh hit back at Rahul Gandhi's statement that there was an alcohol smell coming from Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's mouth. The former MP said, "This is not a good jibe. We do not believe that there would be an unpleasant smell coming from the Chief Minister's mouth. He may drink, but he would not drink during the day." Read what Rahul first commented on Bhagwant Mann Rahul Gandhi said during the Insaf Rally in Sangrur, Punjab, on Thursday, "I was in the Lok Sabha. At that time, your Chief Minister would sit with us and tell jokes. The smell of alcohol came from his mouth at 11 a.m." "I am not saying that he should not drink alcohol. Drinking alcohol is his personal matter, but brothers and sisters, if you want to fight against drugs, your Chief Minister cannot remain intoxicated every evening." Punjab needs a Chief Minister who will fight for the state and feel deeply about Punjab and its drug problem. Read Brij Bhushan's two key points 1. Shah has vowed to make Punjab drug-free and will fulfil that pledge Brij Bhushan said, "Punjab and Haryana were once a single state. This region was a leader in the field of sports. Punjab has produced many players for the country in sports such as basketball, athletics, volleyball and running." "Punjab is in the grip of a severe drug problem today. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was the first to call for making Punjab drug-free. If Amit Shah makes a pledge, he does so after careful consideration. He has fulfilled every pledge he has made so far." 2. Extending Agniveers' service period is a commendable step Speaking about the decision to extend Agniveers' service period by two years, Brij Bhushan said, "The decision has been taken keeping in mind the demand and supply needs of the Army and young people. This is a welcome step." He said that when the Agniveer scheme was introduced and linked to employment, there was some opposition. However, there are several countries where military training is mandatory for every young person.

stories.title: Yogi's Diwali gift to 10 lakh farmers:Compensation for crop losses increased by up to 30%; ₹8 lakh for deaths in disasters
stories.summary: The Yogi government has given farmers a major gift ahead of Diwali. The chief minister announced that farmers will now receive 25% to 30% more compensation for crop damage. An estimated 10 lakh farmers in the state are expected to benefit. Along with this, the government has significantly increased disaster relief assistance. The families of those who die in disasters will receive double the relief amount. This means that in the event of a death caused by a natural disaster, the deceased's family will now receive ₹8 lakh instead of ₹4 lakh. In fact, while significantly increasing disaster relief assistance, the government has made major changes to the disaster relief norms. An order issued by the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said the decision would compensate for losses incurred between 1 April and 4 November. Three days ago, Yogi made a major announcement for farmers, saying that their crops had suffered heavy damage due to rain, floods and drought. Compensation for the losses was being provided, but the government would soon introduce a separate special economic package for 3 crore farming families. Livestock owners to receive higher compensation for animal deaths The assistance provided under the State Disaster Response Fund and the National Disaster Response Fund has been increased. Compensation for the death of large animals in disasters has now been raised from ₹40,000 to ₹50,000. For the death of small animals such as goats, sheep and pigs, owners will receive ₹5,500 instead of ₹4,000. Compensation for the death of pack animals such as horses and mules has been increased from ₹20,000 to ₹25,400. Poultry farmers will receive ₹130 per chicken, up from ₹100. Farmers to receive more assistance for crop losses Compensation for crop losses in irrigated areas will now be ₹22,000 per hectare, up from ₹17,000. For rain-related losses, compensation will be provided at the rate of ₹11,000 per hectare, instead of ₹8,500. Compensation for losses to perennial crops and agroforestry has been increased from ₹22,500 to ₹30,000 per hectare. Assistance increased for losses in silk production The government has also increased assistance for losses in silk production. Compensation for eri, mulberry and tasar silk production has been raised from ₹6,000 to ₹7,800 per hectare. Assistance for muga silk production has been increased from ₹7,500 to ₹9,800 per hectare. Assistance will be provided in relief camps for 30 days Assistance for removing silt from agricultural land will be increased from ₹18,000 to ₹23,000 per hectare. For damage to land caused by landslides and avalanches, assistance will be increased from ₹47,000 to ₹60,000 per hectare. Disaster-affected families will receive assistance in relief camps for 30 days. In the event of drought, provision has been made for drinking water assistance for 90 days. Homes, schools, roads and hospitals to receive greater assistance The government has also set new assistance norms for the repair of homes, schools, roads and hospitals. Assistance of ₹1.85 lakh will be provided for a completely damaged house in the plains, while ₹2.06 lakh will be provided for a completely damaged house in hilly areas. Assistance of ₹93,000 will be provided for a partially damaged house in the plains.

stories.title: Mother sentenced to life imprisonment for poisoning three children:Mixed pesticide in tea and gave it to them in Ghazipur; fourth child survived
stories.summary: A court on Thursday sentenced the mother who killed three children in Ghazipur to life imprisonment. The woman remained standing in court as the verdict was pronounced. There was no sign of remorse on her face. Four years ago, after an argument with her husband, the woman mixed aluminium phosphide in tea and gave it to her two sons and daughter. All three children died after drinking the poisoned tea. The fourth child survived because he was outside the house with his maternal grandmother at the time of the incident. The court of Additional District and Sessions Judge Shakti Singh also fined the woman ₹50,000. Advocate Akhilesh Singh said police personnel had brought the woman to court. She repeatedly asked them when the verdict would be delivered. After she was sentenced, the woman went to jail with the police personnel without showing any reaction. Here is the full case Sunita (40), a resident of Dhadhni Bhanmal Rai village in the Suhwal police station area, had a husband, Baleshwar Yadav, who worked at a factory in Gurugram. There were four children in the family. The eldest was 11-year-old Babbi, also known as Himanshu. Himanshu was followed by Priyanshu (eight), Supriya (seven) and the youngest son, Sheru (four). On Raksha Bandhan, Sunita had gone to her maternal home in Saitbandh, under the Revtipur police station area. From there, she asked her husband for ₹5,000 for the children's needs. They argued over the phone about this. On 15 August 2022, a holiday, Sunita became angry when the children began insisting that she buy them clothes. She initially scolded the children and made them quiet. When they did not listen, she took ₹20 from the house and bought a Sulphas tablet from a nearby shop. After returning home, she made tea and mixed the poison into it. She gave the poisoned tea to Himanshu, Priyanshu and Supriya. At the time of the incident, her youngest son Sheru had gone next door with his maternal grandmother. He was engrossed in playing and therefore survived. When Sunita's mother learnt of it, she reached the house. Seeing all three children in a critical condition at the same time, she raised an alarm. When she asked her daughter, Sunita told her that she had made the children drink poison. The three children were rushed by ambulance to the district hospital, where Priyanshu died. Himanshu and Supriya were referred to Varanasi, where both died the same day. All three children studied at the village's council-run school. Himanshu was in Class 6, Priyanshu in Class 3 and Supriya in Class 2. The children's uncle had an FIR registered After receiving information about the incident, Baleshwar Yadav reached the village from Gurugram. He was completely shattered after seeing the children's bodies. He had said that his wife had spoken about poisoning the children before as well, but he had not imagined that she would actually do it. After the incident, the children's uncle, Bullu Yadav, had a murder case registered. The case had been under hearing for four years. Sunita was never granted bail after her arrest. Additional District Government Counsel Akhilesh Singh produced seven witnesses.

stories.title: Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki see strong demand on Dhanteras:Gorakhpur's Gen Z buyers prefer Bobber, Bullet, Apache and Pulsar bikes
stories.summary: The automobile market in Gorakhpur is buzzing ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali. People are visiting showrooms to buy everything from two-wheelers to four-wheelers. Dealers are also expecting strong growth in the market this time. Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki vehicles are in particularly high demand in Gorakhpur. Among two-wheelers, Gen Z is showing the greatest preference for bobbers, Bullets, Apaches and Pulsars. Based on the booking figures, more than 5,000 bikes, scooters and electric scooters are expected to be sold in the district on Dhanteras. More than 1,200 cars are also expected to be delivered. According to traders, the automobile sector could see growth of up to 10% to 15% this time compared with last year. The notable point is that this time, there is strong demand not only for vehicles in the regular price range, but also for expensive bikes priced at ₹4 lakh to ₹5 lakh and cars costing ₹25 lakh to ₹30 lakh. Vehicles such as the Scorpio-N, Apache, Bobber and Bullet continue to be popular with customers. Demand for electric vehicles has also increased, but several showrooms are facing a shortage of stock compared with demand. Bookings so strong that demand reached up to three times the stock The greatest enthusiasm is being seen in showrooms over the purchase of four-wheelers. Ajay Chaurasia, general manager of sales and marketing at a Maruti showroom, said the market appeared to slow down for a few days after Navratri. But the number of customers suddenly increased after this. This time, bookings have been far higher than expected. He said that bookings received were nearly three times the stock available at the showroom. At present, around 200 vehicles have been booked. The high demand for the Brezza has led to a shortage in its availability. However, customers are also showing interest in the Victories. The initial target was to deliver 70 to 80 vehicles on Dhanteras, but deliveries of 250 to 275 vehicles are now expected. Sales are reportedly more than double those of last year. Demand for petrol cars such as the WagonR, Dzire and Swift has also increased. Customers are showing interest in the petrol segment alongside CNG. Scorpio-N Sees the Highest Demand at Mahindra Mahindra showrooms are also witnessing a rush of customers. Sanjay Shahi, GM Sales at Mahindra Sardar Motors, said growth this year is around 20 per cent compared with last year. A total of 51 vehicles are scheduled for delivery on Dhanteras. The Scorpio-N is in the highest demand. Customers buying expensive vehicles are also showing no let-up this time. The top automatic variant of the Scorpio-N costs around ₹28 lakh. A seven-seater electric vehicle priced at around ₹32.50 lakh has also been sold. He said demand is good, but vehicle availability continues to be limited. Apache and Bobber in Demand Among Bikes; More Than 1,000 Bullets Booked There is also excitement over Dhanteras in the two-wheeler market. Ayush Srivastava, sales manager at Dhairya TVS in Nausadh, said the dealership is targeting the delivery of more than 70 vehicles on Dhanteras. The Apache is in the highest demand. Scooter bookings are also strong. Customers are being given two helmets with every vehicle, along with a coupon for a lucky draw to be held in December. Meanwhile, Ekta, manager of Bharat Trading Company, said that more than 50 vehicles had already been booked for Dhanteras. The Bobber is in the highest demand among them. Young people, in particular, are showing a preference for this bike. Its on-road price ranges from around ₹2.46 lakh to ₹2.60 lakh. The Continental GT is also in high demand among those who are fond of expensive bikes. It costs around ₹4 lakh. According to dealers, more than 1,000 Bullets have already been booked at different showrooms in the city, while only around 300 Bullets are expected to be available for Dhanteras and Diwali combined. Demand for electric scooters and cars higher, availability lower This time, customers have also shown greater interest in electric vehicles. People are visiting showrooms to buy electric scooters and cars. However, according to dealers, vehicle stock is low compared with demand. Several customers are waiting for delivery after booking their vehicles. Deliveries to continue from morning until night on Dhanteras Showroom operators have also made preparations in view of the crowds expected on Dhanteras. Ganesh Chaurasia, manager of Sunny Honda, said that customers are very enthusiastic this time. About 150 vehicles have been booked so far. For customers' convenience, the showroom will open from 8 a.m. to 8:30 a.m., and deliveries will be arranged until 9 p.m. Waiting for Dhanteras to buy a new bike Customers visiting the showroom are also waiting for Dhanteras to buy a vehicle of their choice. Dharam Singh Yadav of Jungle Kauria said he already owns a Classic 350. He has come to look at Jawa bikes this time to buy something new. Meanwhile, Pradeep Maurya of Indira Nagar said he had booked a Honda SP 125. He said buying a new item on Dhanteras is considered auspicious, so he decided to take delivery of the bike on the same day.

stories.title: Gorakhpur announces diversion for Ayodhya Deepotsav:Vehicles from Kushinagar, Deoria and Bihar to use expressways for 2 days
stories.summary: Gorakhpur traffic police have announced changes to traffic arrangements in view of the Deepotsav celebrations at the Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya on November 7. The diversion for heavy vehicles, including trucks, DCMs and buses, will remain in force from 11 pm on November 6 until 8 pm on November 8, or until the crowds disperse. Vehicles to use alternative routes Under the revised traffic arrangements, heavy vehicles coming from Kushinagar, Deoria and Bihar and heading towards Lucknow, Kanpur, Delhi or beyond will have to take the Gorakhpur Link Expressway and Purvanchal Expressway after crossing Baghagada. However, heavy vehicles travelling from within Gorakhpur district and city towards GIDA, Sahjanwa, Sant Kabir Nagar and Basti will be exempt from these restrictions. Light vehicles and heavy emergency vehicles will also be allowed to operate without restrictions. Traffic police have appealed to drivers to follow the designated routes and cooperate with the authorities during the diversion period.

stories.title: Fog covers UP on Dhanteras; five trains cancelled:Temperatures below 18°C in 20 districts, Hardoi records coldest night; chill expected to intensify during Diwali
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified across Uttar Pradesh, with a mild chill being felt during mornings and evenings. Fog has also started covering several districts. Meanwhile, air pollution in the western UP districts falling under the National Capital Region (NCR) has become a major concern. Noida's Air Quality Index (AQI) has crossed 400, while the air quality in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat has also entered the red zone. Meanwhile, due to fog in Mirzapur, the Railways has cancelled several trains, including the Barwadih-Chunar Passenger, for three months. The train will not operate between Chopan and Chunar from December 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027. Fog covered 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sambhal, Shravasti and Deoria, on Thursday morning. Visibility in Shravasti dropped to less than 10 metres, making it difficult for commuters to see clearly on roads. Weather scientists have predicted that cold conditions and the chill will intensify across the state during Diwali week. Professor Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University's (BHU) Varanasi campus, said, “Temperatures are likely to fall further during Diwali week. Fog may persist during the morning hours. With changing weather conditions, the chill will increase during mornings and evenings.” Air quality turns hazardous in four districts; GRAP Stage II enforced Ahead of Diwali, air quality in several NCR districts has entered the red zone. In view of rising pollution levels, Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) has been implemented across the NCR. Municipal corporations are sprinkling water on roads to control dust. Burning waste in the open has been prohibited, while areas prone to dust pollution are also being monitored. Diesel-powered generators have been banned. The use of coal and wood in tandoors at hotels, roadside eateries and restaurants has also been prohibited. Pollution-generating activities, including road construction using bitumen, have been restricted. See the weather pictures from 4 November Varanasi records highest daytime temperature; Hardoi coldest at night According to weather data recorded on November 5, Varanasi registered the highest maximum temperature in the state at 32.8°C. Hamirpur ranked second at 32.2°C, followed by Bahraich at 32°C. Among the minimum temperatures, Hardoi recorded the lowest at 13.5°C. Muzaffarnagar was second at 14.5°C, while the temperature in Bareilly was recorded at 15°C. Weather outlook from western UP to Purvanchal Western UP: Noida, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Agra and Mathura are likely to experience dry weather. Light mist may occur during the morning. Central UP: Rain is unlikely in Lucknow, Kanpur, Unnao, Sitapur, Hardoi and Rae Bareli. Sunny conditions are expected during the day, with mild cold at night. Purvanchal: Weather is likely to remain dry in Varanasi, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur and Deoria. Light mist may occur at some places during the morning. Bundelkhand: No rainfall is expected in Jhansi, Banda, Chitrakoot, Mahoba, Hamirpur and Lalitpur for now. CM orders immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has stepped up action over crop damage caused by continuous rainfall between October 29 and 31 due to Cyclone Arnab. He has directed all district magistrates across the state to visit affected areas and immediately assess the damage to crops. He has also ordered that farmers be provided compensation without delay. The Chief Minister said the government would introduce a special package for farmers. Farmers advised to take precautions while sowing and irrigating Rabi crops With the possibility of rainfall in November, farmers have been advised to remain cautious while managing Rabi crops. In particular, farmers in Purvanchal should ensure proper drainage in fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where rainfall has already provided sufficient moisture. Decisions regarding sowing and irrigation should be based on weather conditions and soil moisture levels. Crops that need attention during cold and foggy conditions

Gandhi contrasts her vision of an inclusive India with Modi's more exclusionary ideology shaped by the RSS. She also revisits the violence of the 2002 Gujarat riots during Modi's tenure as chief minister.

stories.title: Oklahoma family turns 1903 ancestral ranch into wildlife haven, rotating 600 cow-calf pairs across 25 paddocks
stories.summary: A ranch in Oklahoma has been awarded for its sustainable management practices that support both cattle and wildlife. It implements rotational grazing across 25 paddocks to protect native grasslands and improve ecosystem health. The management system is designed to promote water conservation and soil retention properties. Wildlife species, including deer and various birds, benefit from the preserved habitat.

stories.title: 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan criticized Sonia Gandhi's memoir, arguing it attempts to whitewash the historical mistakes of the Congress party. He highlighted her emotional responses to key incidents while questioning her silence on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and other tragedies. The memoir details Sonia's childhood, her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi, and her experiences as part of the Gandhi family.

stories.title: Fake GoFundMe raises $17,750 after deadly DC plane crash, then gets exposed
Netanyahu's daily calls to Trump over Iran war spark pushback within White House: Report
