stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi addressed questions about her family's leadership of the Congress party during an interview. She downplayed allegations of nepotism while asserting the party's potential to challenge the BJP. Gandhi reflected on her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi's Emergency decision and described it as a mistake. She recounted personal trauma from losing both Indira and her husband Rajiv Gandhi to assassinations.

stories.title: Hands-on inspection: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw buys tea via UPI, interacts with passengers at Anand Vihar Station
stories.summary: Passengers shared positive feedback regarding ongoing facility upgrades, cleanliness, and waiting area enhancements implemented by Indian Railways.

stories.title: Tiger Woods' former mistress Rachel Uchitel spends $100,000 on cosmetic surgery makeover
stories.summary: Rachel Uchitel, who made headlines in 2009 after being linked to golfer Tiger Woods, has reportedly spent $100,000 on cosmetic surgery. The 51-year-old podcast host underwent a facelift, brow lift and other procedures after years of facial fillers and aesthetic treatments left her unhappy with her appearance. She says she wanted a fresher, more natural look.

stories.title: Nazi spies landed on US soil days before German U-boat sank Canadian ship off Maine in 1944; 82 years later, divers find wreck 400 feet underwater
stories.summary: Divers from the Nomad Exploration Team located the wreck of the SS Cornwallis nearly 400 feet underwater. This ship was torpedoed by a German submarine in December 1944, resulting in the deaths of 43 crew members. The submarine also secretly landed two Nazi spies on the coast of Maine just days before. The discovery highlights an important historical event involving espionage during World War II.

stories.title: UK bride dances with hospitalised dad: she brings wedding to his ward; staff help arrange the dance
stories.summary: Sinead Jackson's wedding was uniquely touched by bittersweet circumstances as her father, Leslie Healy, was hospitalized only days before the event. Hospital personnel facilitated a heartwarming moment, allowing Sinead to don her wedding dress for a dance with her father. Though Leslie couldn't physically attend, technology enabled him to witness the ceremony.

stories.title: West Bengal SIR: Fourth retired judge resigns from appeals tribunals, cites ‘personal reasons’
'First apologise to devotees, saints': UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visit
Florida court rules legal-fees clause cannot automatically bind future owners after $40,000 trespass award
stories.summary: A recent ruling by the Florida Supreme Court clarified that attorney-fees clauses do not automatically apply to future property owners. The case originated with an easement agreement involving Crown Castle South LLC and RJ's International Trading LLC. Although RJ's secured damages for trespass, it sought attorney fees based on the original agreement. The court determined that the legal-fees clause lacked connection to the use or enjoyment of the land.

stories.title: Istanbul landfill generates power but leaks 7.4 tonnes of methane hourly, satellite data finds
'Run bulldozer over our bodies': Mamata protests after 'attack' on Abhishek Banerjee's house
New York founder turned 1,000 cancelled meals into a food initiative that has donated 4 million
stories.summary: The Migrant Kitchen was born from a cancelled catering order amidst the COVID-19 crisis, initially providing meals to healthcare workers. Over time, it evolved to tackle food insecurity by serving thousands of meals daily to marginalized communities, emphasizing culturally relevant dishes. Employing around 100 individuals, mostly immigrants, it mirrors the community it supports and has expanded its reach beyond New York City into Philadelphia, enhancing emergency meal delivery efforts.

stories.title: In 1935, a Black linguist recorded Louisiana Creole speakers on aluminium discs
stories.summary: Research into recordings made in 1935 is shedding light on the vital voices of Louisiana Creole and Louisiana French speakers. Linguist Lorenzo Dow Turner's findings reveal significant aspects of the language and its vibrant cultural ties within Black communities. Dr. Oliver Mayeux's work revived these gems, showcasing unique grammatical features and vocabulary. As the cultural importance of Louisiana Creole is recognized, initiatives are fostering language revival efforts across the region.

stories.title: Data protection law faces scrutiny: The key concerns explained
Diljit Dosanjh barred from singing ‘Patiala Peg’, 3 other songs at Indore concert amid child safety concerns
stories.summary: Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh faces a ban on performing four songs during his upcoming concert in Indore. Authorities cited worries over the songs' promotion of liquor and violence, especially regarding children's impact. The District Child Protection Officer received a complaint highlighting these concerns and the guidelines from the Punjab and Haryana High Court. Additionally, restrictions include limitations on children on stage and the singer's costume.

stories.title: 'Ask Karnataka to seek consent of co-basin states': Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges PM Modi over Mekedatu dam project
Ayodhya glows with 30 lakh diyas as Deepotsav lights up Saryu ghats on Diwali eve
stories.summary: Lakhs of diyas illuminated Ram Ki Paidi ghat, while more than 30 lakh earthen lamps were set to light up 56 ghats along the river, turning the temple town into a spectacular sea of lights. The annual celebration, which marks return of Lord Ram to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana, recreates the traditional welcome believed to have been given to him by the people of the city in the Treta Yuga.

stories.title: Nikki Haley's analysis of GOP's midterm loss: 'You can't blame media, academia, Hollywood'; Son Nalin Haley agrees
Indiana man loses visitation bid after raising ex-partner's daughter for eight years
100 days adrift in the Pacific Ocean: Nine leave Micronesia by boat; 5 survive, 4 die in Kiribati
stories.summary: Nine family members from Micronesia set out on what was supposed to be a one-hour boat journey to collect supplies. A storm swept their vessel off course, leaving them adrift in the Pacific Ocean for nearly 100 days. They eventually reached Kiribati, more than 3,000 miles away, but only five survived the ordeal.

stories.title: How much does the British Royal Family cost taxpayers? King Charles' £137.9m grant, William's wealth
stories.summary: The British Royal Family receives £137.9 million through the Sovereign Grant in 2026/27, but a new bill proposes reducing the funding to £99.9 million the following year. Meanwhile, reports reveal Prince William’s £1.2 billion Duchy of Cornwall valuation and King Charles’ estimated £640 million fortune, raising questions about royal wealth, income and taxes.

stories.title: Penguin was 'uneasy' with criticism of govt: Sonia Gandhi's 1st reaction to memoir row
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi voiced her dismay over Penguin Random House India's decision to withdraw her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', due to disagreements about sensitive subjects involving Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She interpreted this as an effort to inhibit her narrative and suggested possible government influence.

stories.title: 'Poor Biharis don't know anything': Congress UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam targets BJP chief Nitin Nabin
‘Grow up, Pramila’: Harmeet Dhillon hits back at Democrat leader Jayapal over ‘knitting’ jibe after DOJ exit
Iran ramps up threats against US, removes cap on ballistic missile range
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the removal of missile range restrictions while preparing for asymmetric warfare. This statement follows limited US strikes targeting Iranian anti-aircraft systems in the region. Reports indicated that explosions in Qeshm Island were due to Iranian air defense exercises and not hostile actions. US officials claim the Iranian air defense systems were severely weakened during previous conflicts.

stories.title: Army debunks Pakistan propaganda about 'Chinese troops inside Arunachal'
stories.summary: The Indian Army has strongly refuted false reports on social media suggesting that Chinese forces made significant territorial gains in Arunachal Pradesh. Claims of a 50 km advance in early November were thoroughly investigated, revealing six accounts deliberately pushing misleading information. Official sources assure that there has been no major defeat of Indian troops, emphasizing the importance of relying on credible sources for updates on border issues to combat misinformation.

stories.title: Find a new wife: Katie Miller reacts to news report detailing her 'lobbying' for husband Miller's promotion to Susie Wiles' job
Evening newswrap: Tech exec shot dead in Faridabad over parking spot; Iran claims its forces have downed 260 aircraft, and more
Digital arrest: A cyberfraud wrapped in a psychological trap; why intelligence falls prey to basic instincts
'Fight against Gyanesh Kumar will continue': CJP's Dipke targets CEC ahead of anti-SIR rally in Kochi
High drama in Kolkata: Mamata Banerjee joins TMC workers in protest against attack on Abhishek's home
'Remove your Italian lenses': BJP slams Sonia Gandhi for remarks on country's progress
Why death of tribal activist Nisha Bhagat has sparked row in Jharkhand
Utah millionaire father of seven built a 300-acre doomsday compound stocked with food, weapons and supplies to shelter 200 people if civilisation collapses
stories.summary: Jayson Orvis has created a 300-acre doomsday sanctuary in the heart of Utah, designed to accommodate 200 people during catastrophic circumstances. This unique compound showcases greenhouses and a flourishing food forest, underpinning his vision of cooperative survival. While Orvis maintains a level of skepticism about imminent apocalypse risks, he acknowledges the importance of community over solitude in potential crises.

stories.title: Texas court upholds refinery's gross negligence in worker's death, cuts award by $125,000
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court upheld a refinery company's gross negligence in a worker's asbestos-related death but reduced his family's damages award from $325,000 to $200,000. It also revived negligence claims that had earlier been dismissed, allowing the family to pursue them in further proceedings.

stories.title: Cancer in India: Screening exists, but why are patients still diagnosed late
PG doctors quit premier medical institutes
stories.summary: RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER; numbers decline at Delhi AIIMS and JIPMER, but several institutes lack consolidated records on counselling and workplace stress

stories.title: Massive anti-drug drive: 458 acres of illicit cannabis eradicated in Arunachal Pradesh
BJP attacks Rahul over 'out of context' Amit Shah video amid SIR row
Sharad Pawar discharged from hospital, doctor shares health update
Wedding ring lost on Dutch farm during WWII, found 83 years later
stories.summary: A Dutch man who lost his wedding ring while threshing grain in 1942 or 1943 has had it returned to his family 83 years later. A metal detector user found it buried 20 centimetres underground in Odiliapeel and personally returned it to the owner's son, Bert Nabuurs, refusing a reward. The ring's engraved wedding date confirmed its identity.

stories.title: ‘Relief to breathe Kerala’s clean air’: Shashi Tharoor takes swipe at Delhi govt over pollution crisis
'Democratic rights were curtailed but constitutionally': Sonia Gandhi reflects on Emergency
Als Nursing Hospital Opens: 14-year ALS drive builds specialised facility; 350,000 donors fund care
stories.summary: In March 2025, the Seungil Hope Nursing Hospital in Yongin welcomed its first ALS patients, marking a 14-year journey led by dedicated advocates Park Seung-il and Sean. This landmark facility, developed with the generosity of over 350,000 donors and government backing, aims to provide advanced care tailored to the unique needs of those with ALS, emphasizing a community's unwavering commitment to enhancing the lives of affected individuals.

stories.title: Two men charged over shooting at Kapil Sharma's restaurant in Canada
‘E20 turned into 420’: Rahul Gandhi alleges petrol samples from Karnataka exceed 20% ethanol limit
Republicans spent more, Democrats won more: Inside the costliest US midterm battle
stories.summary: In the 2026 US midterm elections, Democrats made notable gains among Latino voters, following a period of prior support for Republicans. Increased spending by GOP candidates did not secure the anticipated wins, resulting in losses in key districts. High turnout from Latino constituents significantly impacted voting dynamics nationwide, with many responding negatively to proposed data centre projects.

stories.title: 'No permanent solution': Congress slams Delhi govt as pollution levels remain severe
'Who has time to kill him?' BJP-TMC spar after attack on Abhishek Banerjee's house
France deploys 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests
stories.summary: French trade unions and student groups are organizing a day of protests against rising living costs. The Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris, despite an official ban on gatherings. Nationwide demonstrations have been ongoing for weeks, with participants demanding wage increases and better conditions for youth. On Monday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will meet with union representatives to discuss these issues.

stories.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
stories.summary: The United States has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program. This reward aims to gather details about facilities, equipment, and personnel involved with the program. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to resolve tensions and prevent further conflict. Iran has expressed the desire for negotiations but requires certain conditions to be met.

stories.title: US-China trade talks to continue as Washington presses Beijing to honour Busan deal
stories.summary: China and the US are engaged in ongoing dialogues to foster stable trade relations, with emphasis on prior commitments. US officials expressed concern regarding China's adherence to agreements related to rare earth materials and agricultural products. The latest discussions revealed the US's stance that China falls short in fulfilling its responsibilities under the Busan agreement. Moreover, China dismissed accusations of inadequate rare earth supplies and agricultural purchasing.

stories.title: SC to NewsClick: Reply to ED plea against HC order quashing ECIR
'Voices in head said to kill Trump': Man with firearms and ammunition arrested near White House
stories.summary: The Secret Service took Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos into custody after he exhibited alarming conduct in his vehicle. When confronted by officers, he insisted that he heard voices commanding him to execute President Trump. A subsequent search of his stolen car revealed three guns and additional ammunition. A Venezuelan national without legal status since March 2024, Chrinos now underscores the persistent dangers faced by the president.

stories.title: ED tracking $1m transfer to 'meddle in domestic affairs'
CBI files case against Biyanis, Future Retail in Rs 904 cr fraud
Creamy layer verdict only for those who challenged government decision, says SC
SC settles 60-yr Bhakra & Beas dispute between Punjab, Haryana and HP
Take us to UP in shackles, bulletproof jackets, plead undertrials; court agrees
Texas appeals court upholds $619K judgment against beverage company co-owner
'Dallas' star Victoria Principal, 76, now rescues animals on her ranch; shares miniature horse Halo's recovery
stories.summary: Former actress Victoria Principal has found her true calling in animal rehabilitation, dedicating her life to caring for rescued creatures at her ranch. One notable resident is Halo, a miniature horse currently healing with her support. Principal passionately advocates for the role of love and patience in nurturing these animals back to health, marking a significant departure from her Hollywood days as she embraces her new purpose.

stories.title: SC: Awareness alone can curb pollution; people violate restrictions ‘with vengeance’
'Jackass' star Steve-O turns 44-acre Tennessee ranch into a home for rescued animals
stories.summary: Steve-O, the famous Jackass star, has dedicated himself to animal welfare by establishing The Radical Ranch, a sanctuary for rescued animals situated near Nashville. Since its inception as a nonprofit in 2024, the ranch has provided a home for nine animals, including goats and pigs. Steve-O envisions expanding the sanctuary to include cows and chickens while fostering empathy towards all creatures.

stories.title: PM cites Para Games success to motivate athletes for Olympics 2028
Manipur rebel arrested from Delhi hotel
In 2017, Gaten Matarazzo helped form a charity; nine years later, its partners issued 37 care tips
stories.summary: Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD) affects bone and dental development in patients and requires specialized care. A recent study established 37 expert recommendations for diagnosing and managing this rare condition effectively. These guidelines emphasize the importance of coordinated care among various specialists and regular monitoring. Gaten Matarazzo, who has CCD, advocates for better recognition and treatment of the disorder. CCD Smiles organization aims to support patients through awareness and research initiatives.

stories.title: Post on CJI: SC's contempt notice to Keralam Cong office-bearers
With working strength of just 2, Sikkim HC unable to hear intra-court appeals
California condo parking dispute ends after decade; court rejects $292,544 legal fee claim
stories.summary: In a contentious parking dispute in Orange County, condominium owners WCST Enterprises and Berit Ling faced off in court. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of WCST, affirming its claim to garage space 38G-a. However, despite the legal victory, WCST could not reclaim its substantial legal fees of $292,544, as these claims did not meet California statutes for fee recovery.

stories.title: 125-year-old Idaho ranch gets permanent protection
stories.summary: A conservation easement has been established on the Flying A Ranch in Idaho to protect the land. This easement allows the Atchley family to continue their farming operations while preventing future development. The agreement also supports a crucial wildlife migration corridor for mule deer and various other species. Previous efforts to protect the ranch were led by Clen Atchley, who passed away in 2024.

stories.title: Court allows more evidence in Sonia Gandhi voter list case
HC judge vacancies at decade-low 26%, but pendency keeps piling up
NMC adds 9,783 PG medical seats, takes total to 68,305
New research rules out the theory of Stonehenge Altar Stone's Northeast Scottish Origin
stories.summary: Researchers continue to explore the origins of the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, which weighs approximately six tonnes. Recent studies suggested a possible origin from northeast Scotland, but findings have complicated this theory. A new international team's research found no matching source from the Scottish locations they examined, narrowing possibilities down. Previous assumptions about the Altar Stone's Welsh origins have been challenged by new geological insights.

stories.title: Brisbane Library House Auction: former private library cleared for sale; rebuild interest grows
stories.summary: After years of neglect, a three-bedroom home in Wynnum, Brisbane, has undergone a remarkable transformation. This property, once filled with a vast collection of books and memorabilia, required extensive teamwork to clear out its contents and evict wildlife. Now, it's being showcased as an exciting renovation or rebuilding opportunity in a sought-after neighborhood, with an auction date set for November 14, 2026, drawing potential buyers eager to invest.

stories.title: CBSE Class X & XII board exams to start from Feb 16
More than 30% ethanol in E20, says Karnataka minister
Ousted Videocon promoter Dhoot declared bankrupt over dues worth Rs 12,668cr
One more chance for excluded voters in Delhi, 6 other states
Louisiana woman fights uncle over mother's estate for 13 years; court revives part of lawsuit
stories.summary: A Louisiana woman accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of her late mother's estate to himself and businesses linked to him. More than 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived her claims concerning his handling of the estate but upheld the dismissal of other claims. It also cancelled a $10,000 damages award and ordered further proceedings.

stories.title: For more than 60 years, visitors walked through a cave in Spain; now 280 motifs identified
stories.summary: A remarkable archaeological find at Cova de la Font Major has revealed 280 Palaeolithic engravings, showcasing diverse motifs of animals and geometric shapes. This challenges the previously held notion that cave art was scarce in northeastern Iberia, where only two pieces were known. These engravings suggest the existence of unique artistic traditions independent of the famous Franco-Cantabrian region, offering new insights into the cultural practices of Ice Age Europe.

stories.title: Twenty black grouse were moved from the North Pennines to the North York Moors in 2024
stories.summary: In a remarkable conservation achievement, black grouse have successfully hatched chicks in North York Moors after a long absence of 200 years. In 2024, 20 black grouse were moved from North Pennines as part of a dedicated effort that includes habitat restoration and management of predators. Reports indicate a notable rise in the number of displaying males, with plans for further translocations underway to bolster their population even more.

stories.title: ‘Mad Men’ star John Slattery joins Ocean Conservancy campaign to protect oceans
North Carolina student wins top award for free tool mapping wildlife roadkill hotspots
stories.summary: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.

stories.title: Indian family seeks help to bring back man's body after he dies from burn injuries in New Zealand on birthday
Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
stories.summary: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

stories.title: Streamer Feud Over Halloween: Banks slams Plaqueboymax’s ‘whiteface’ stream; questions career slide
stories.summary: Plaqueboymax’s Halloween livestream led to disagreements with Adin Ross and FaZe Banks. Adin suggested a blackface stream after seeing Max’s crew dressed as stereotypical white men. Max questioned Adin’s respect for Black culture, while Banks said Max’s costume showed disrespect towards white people. Banks also criticised Max’s content, career direction and Super Bowl halftime show ambitions, and invoked Kai Cenat.

stories.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle back to US after shameful exit from Greece; moved in with ex-husband with a hit list: Report
What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff
stories.summary: Susie Wiles fired: Within three days of midterm rout, President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to the post of Chief of Staff replacing Susie Wiles, who served the longest on the post. The decision was not out of the blue as there were speculations which the president at that time dismissed.

stories.title: How Cristiano Ronaldo turned a Madeira nightclub into an $8 million home
Who is Navneet Alag? Meet husband of newly elected Indian-American congresswoman Pia Dandiya
Idaho Supreme Court overturns ruling granting ex-partner 50% property ownership
Jewel-backed youth foundation reaches 1.6 million with mental health tools
How Abdullahs managed the rebellion: Farooq calls MLAs’ demands genuine, Omar offers to resign
Meryl Streep backs women's history education as two teachers earn award for AP course campaign
stories.summary: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

stories.title: India’s only floating post office gets longer working hours
Will you comply with Japanese laws? Japan plans new question for foreign visitors on entry form
US mother transfers property to son in 2003; court cancels deed after he refuses to return it
stories.summary: A New York mother who transferred her property to her son and daughter-in-law in 2003 after he promised to return it whenever asked has won a legal battle 23 years later. When the couple refused to return the property, she approached the court. A New York appeals court has now upheld the cancellation of the deed, ruling in her favour.

stories.title: London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
stories.summary: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.

stories.title: 7-year-old sells lemonade for school shoes; officer returns with Adidas surprise
John Wick star Keanu Reeves offered a 15-minute Zoom date for charity
Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.

stories.title: 'Convince Modi ji for SIR debate': Rahul Gandhi tells Amit Shah to stop confusing PM, shares video of remarks
PM Modi's Sule message to Sharad Pawar; 'internal tussle' in NCP: Is Maharashtra politics heading for another churn?
stories.summary: Internal conflicts within the Pawar clan has once again put the party at a crossroads. A meeting of senior NCP leaders with Union home minister Amit Shah amid reports of discontent within the party has fuelled speculations. NCP chief Sunetra Pawar has convened meetings to address unity concerns after Ajit Pawar's death. Rohit Pawar has issued a caution to the family regaridng possible BJP manoeuvres.

stories.title: 16 Canadians moved to Florida in 2022 on instruction of cult leader Liana Shanti. After years of legal battle, 3 get $56 million in defamation case
3M agrees to pay up to $7.35 billion in PFAS water contamination settlement involving 120,000 people
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, 3M has agreed to a $7.35 billion resolution for personal injury claims linked to PFAS exposure. This crucial settlement is designed to aid individuals asserting health damages from polluted water and products. The claims process is set up to fairly assess and settle cases expeditiously, with around 120,000 potential beneficiaries meeting defined eligibility criteria. This agreement marks a pivotal move toward tackling PFAS-related health problems.

stories.title: 'Directed at Delhi govt officials': Court dismisses plea seeking FIR against CM Rekha Gupta over Lord Hanuman remark
1983 Air Canada jet runs out of fuel mid-air, but pilots land safely with all 69 aboard
stories.summary: On July 23, 1983, an Air Canada Boeing 767 experienced a loss of engine power while traversing over Manitoba. With 61 passengers and 8 crew aboard, a serious fuel miscalculation by ground staff resulted in a 45 percent shortage. Remarkably, the pilots managed to glide the aircraft and executed an emergency landing on an old military track. Thankfully, everyone onboard suffered only minor injuries, and the plane was later restored.

stories.title: Michael Jordans's Wings initiative supports 4,000 scholars, awards 350 in 2025
Florida Burmese python lays 96 eggs in abandoned concrete pipe nest
Man Sues OpenAI Over Poison Plot: lawsuit says ChatGPT aided alleged plan; adds to AI legal scrutiny
Notary rewrites 88-year-old woman’s will to inherit her fortune
stories.summary: In a shocking case from Braunfels, an 88-year-old woman’s intention to leave her estate to charities was thwarted by a corrupt former notary who forged her will. The Limburg Regional Court imposed a two-year suspended sentence on the notary, who attributed his actions to financial stress but was ultimately deemed to have acted out of greed. His courtroom apology raises questions about the potential repercussions for the woman’s family.

stories.title: Living near a highway toll plaza? New FASTag rule offers annual pass of up to Rs 3,000, but there's a catch
stories.summary: Residents living within 20 km of National Highway toll plazas can apply for a Concessional Local Pass. The pass costs Rs 1,500 or Rs 3,000 annually, depending on the plaza's location. To qualify, motorists must have a functional FASTag, and their vehicle must be non-commercial. The scheme aims to reduce toll expenses for eligible residents but has specific restrictions.

stories.title: Trump had demanded that Harmeet K Dhillon be fired after he watched her on 60 Minutes on October 18: Report
North Carolina court revives roofing firm's lawsuits against insurers over unpaid storm repairs
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court has reinstated lawsuits from Piedmont Roofing Services against various major insurance companies. Overturning an earlier trial judge's dismissal of breach of contract claims, the court concluded that sufficient grounds exist for the roofing company to pursue its claims. This ruling sheds light on the intricate legal issues related to the transfer of insurance rights in property damage situations.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: Panic as Karmabhoomi Express catches fire in Punjab; bomb threats to Bombay HC, BSE and Amitabh Bachchan’s residence, and more
'Your tacit approval?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin questions Rahul Gandhi over Jharkhand Congress leader's 'Nepal-Bangladesh' remark
Eva Longoria-backed charity supports 100+ children at Vietnam orphanage, expands plans to Spain therapy centre
stories.summary: Since 2018, the Global Gift Foundation has championed the Quang Chau Orphanage, now known as Casa Ángeles, providing care to over 100 needy children. This initiative, bolstered by funds from the Global Gift Gala in Paris, also supports the Casa Ángeles therapy centre in Spain. Through engaging performances and a vibrant auction, the event helps sustain vital projects aimed at uplifting vulnerable communities.

stories.title: At 9, she started feeding hungry children; now her nonprofit has reached over 110,000 people
stories.summary: New Jersey teenager Anakh Sawhney started Rice Kids in 2018, aged nine, to provide meals to hungry children. Her nonprofit has since supported more than 110,000 people across five US states and parts of India through food, education, healthcare and other essential resources. More than half of the students supported by the organisation in India have returned to mainstream education.

stories.title: The watchman and the log scale
Democrats win Congress but Trump's final 2 years could be the most explosive yet
Michigan brother ploughs landscaped strip beside sibling's home, triggering bitter land dispute
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court revived a couple's claim over a 0.13-acre strip allegedly landscaped by their family for years. The dispute began after the husband's brother ploughed the land in 2022. The court ruled that a 1991 foreclosure judgment did not prevent the boundary claim, while leaving the $5,364.44 award for trespass and waste undisturbed.

stories.title: New York buyer loses $1 million lawsuit after demanding $270,000 cut on $550,000 Bronx home deal
stories.summary: A man from New York made a cash offer for a dilapidated home in the Bronx, agreeing to accept it in its current state. After finding additional issues just days before the closing, he sought a considerable price decrease. The seller declined, referring to the contract terms and previous property condition disclosures.

stories.title: US start-up plans to sell sunlight at night with India's Skyroot Aerospace
'1,800 fake AI books, inflated prices': Periyar library pits CM Vijay against DMK
stories.summary: In a heated exchange, Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay pointed fingers at the former DMK administration for alleged corruption linked to library book purchases. It has come to light that almost 1,800 artificially generated books were bought at excessive prices. Author Perumal Murugan raised concerns, leading Congress's Manickam Tagore to insist on a full inquiry.

stories.title: Milo Ventimiglia says family is settled in new home after losing two houses in LA fires
stories.summary: Milo Ventimiglia and wife Jarah Mariano lost their home and another house under construction in the January 2025 Los Angeles fires, when she was 38 weeks pregnant. Nearly two years later, the actor says the family has settled into a new home with their two children, while reflecting on the loss, memories and rebuilding their lives.

stories.title: Laura Loomer announces 'break' after GOP's midterm rout; but not from supporting Trump
Republicans turn against Vivek Ramaswamy: 'He's a tech guy, Ohio is blue collar'
'Inviting death': Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after emotional Facebook Live post
stories.summary: Nisha Kumari Bhagat, a prominent tribal leader in Jharkhand, was tragically found dead at her home in Ranchi. Just hours prior, she had gone live on Facebook, voicing concerns about threats from governmental bodies and land brokers. While police have indicated a possible suicide, they are actively probing the details surrounding her untimely death.

stories.title: Boy who started food bank with £40 at age 9 now helps 5,000 people annually across six sites
stories.summary: After witnessing local families struggle with food insecurity, Isaac Winfield initiated a pop-up food bank in Redditch. This effort has grown into a well-established community service that supports thousands annually. The organization operates six sites and encourages donations without stigma or barriers. Isaac's mother highlights the positive community response and the inspiration his actions have sparked in others.

stories.title: Painting bought for $3,800 in 1963 hidden under fur coats for 40 years, now valued at $3 million
stories.summary: In an astonishing find, a Georgia O’Keeffe painting that lay hidden for almost four decades in an East Village closet has come to light. Originally bought for $3,800 in 1963, it's now valued between $2 million and $3 million. With its auction set for November 18, a public exhibition will showcase the artwork at Rockefeller Center in early November.

stories.title: CBI books Future Retail Ltd, key promoters in Rs 904-crore bank fraud case
stories.summary: CBI has registered a major bank fraud concerning Future Retail Ltd. and its top executives for bank fraud. This case, involving Rs 904 crore, follows a complaint from State Bank of India regarding fund misappropriation. Search operations were conducted at various locations linked to the firm's promoters, leading to the recovery of important documents. The company reportedly diverted bank funds through associated entities without using them for the intended purposes.

stories.title: You can own the world and still feel poor: Aruna Lohia Goenka on the magic of abundance
EC gives voters excluded from draft electoral rolls in 7 states another chance to apply
SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has clarified that its March ruling will not impact completed appointments or promotions. Cases still pending will be examined individually by the courts based on merit and eligibility. The government expressed concerns that retrospective application could unsettle established positions and admissions. It sought two years to establish a uniform creamy layer mechanism across various sectors.

stories.title: Karmabhoomi Express passengers panic as moving train catches fire in Punjab
'Will be dealt with iron hand': SC issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over controversial CJI post
2013 Tehelka rape case: SC refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal's 10-year jail term
IMA asks CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, flags glorification of violence against doctors
stories.summary: The Indian Medical Association has raised concerns about the film Suryaa, which they claim glorifies violence against healthcare workers. They argue that certain scenes depict a father taking revenge on doctors, raising ethical issues. The IMA provided data on increased workplace violence against healthcare professionals in recent years. They have requested that the Central Board of Film Certification deny certification based on these representations.

stories.title: 'It was an imposter': X tells HC takedown notices for IFF, SFLC not sent by Delhi Police
‘AQI data fraud can cost lives’: Saurabh Bharadwaj accuses Delhi government of misleading people
'NC has never been broken, will never be broken': Farooq Abdullah after meeting disgruntled MLAs
Bob Dylan donated all royalties from his 2009 Christmas album to fight hunger
Jharkhand High Court quashes state government's decision to cancel JSSC CGL exam
stories.summary: The Jharkhand High Court has set aside the government's cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination. This ruling comes after candidates protested against the decision and alleged irregularities. The government had previously cancelled multiple recruitment examinations amidst public outcry over these allegations. Additionally, two individuals were arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department related to examination irregularities. Ongoing legal proceedings continue as candidates seek justice and reform in recruitment processes.

stories.title: ‘Hope you are enjoying Delhi weather’: CJI blames vehicles as SC takes up air pollution case
North Dakota ranchers take $383,375 legal fee fight against pipeline firm to US Supreme Court
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court will hear a dispute involving North Dakota ranchers and WBI Energy Transmission over $383,375.76 in legal fees. The justices will decide whether state or federal law governs compensation when private natural gas companies acquire land through eminent domain.

stories.title: Shaquille O’Neal-backed youth centre attracts 400+ children after $1.1 million makeover
stories.summary: Shaquille O’Neal’s foundation has successfully transformed a dilapidated middle school in Henry County into a vibrant Boys and Girls Club. With a renovation budget of $1.1 million, the facility now features improved educational and recreational spaces. Within its first year, it welcomed over 400 children, providing essential youth programs designed to foster safe, nurturing environments for the community’s young people.

stories.title: Judge Halts Arch Construction: US court blocks Trump monument for 14 days; veterans’ suits proceed
stories.summary: A federal judge has placed a temporary hold on the construction of a proposed triumphal arch meant to celebrate American independence. Approved by the National Capital Planning Commission, the monument faced opposition from Vietnam War veterans and local entities, who argued it lacked necessary permissions. As legal disputes unfold, the project’s momentum is halted for two weeks, raising alarms over potential environmental impacts and increased traffic in the area.

stories.title: 1 officer killed, 3 injured as gunman opens fire on police in Colorado
North Carolina farm builds 7 tiny homes inspired by a woman who spent 27 years in prison
'Jantar Mantar in Kochi': Actor Prakash Raj calls for anti-SIR protest on Saturday
Ranjeev Puri makes history as first Indian-American elected Michigan House Speaker
stories.summary: Ranjeev Puri's election as Speaker of the Michigan House of Representatives for the 2027-28 term signifies a historic milestone, marking the first instance of Indian origin in such a prominent role. Expressing gratitude to his peers, Puri highlighted the achievement's significance for his family. His background in Barack Obama's campaigns and the automotive sector fuels his commitment to lowering household expenses and uplifting South Asian communities.

stories.title: Wendy’s rejects billionaire Nelson Peltz’s $1.4 billion takeover bid, adopts ‘poison pill’ defence as burger chain shuts hundreds of US outlets
stories.summary: Wendy's has rejected a takeover proposal valued at $1.4 billion from billionaire investor Nelson Peltz. The fast-food chain argued that the offer undervalues its long-term growth potential, prompting the adoption of a shareholder rights plan. This defensive strategy is designed to protect the company from unwanted acquisition attempts. Wendy's has been facing declining sales and rising operational costs in the competitive fast-food market.

stories.title: After years of flooding, Philippine village turns to bamboo, oyster shells and coconut waste to keep rising waters at bay
stories.summary: Pamarawan village in the Philippines has embraced an innovative coastal defense system to tackle flooding challenges. This initiative incorporates natural materials such as bamboo poles, oyster shells, and coconut husks to fortify against powerful waves and prevent sediment displacement. Remarkably, there have been no flooding incidents reported for almost two years since the project's inception, prompting officials to explore similar setups for other flood-threatened areas.

stories.title: Trump-Kim reset after midterm blow? Why North Korea may hold the cards
Two Iowa families donate 21 acres for wildlife and public recreation
Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals
Denzel Washington helped save August Wilson's childhood home, now an arts centre

Scientists examining dinosaur fossils report evidence of preserved red blood cells and collagen amino acids, a finding led by Curtin University that could change how researchers investigate ancient biological material
stories.summary: Palaeontologists found fossilised signs of dinosaur blood and collagen in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone. These structures were discovered in a theropod dinosaur known as Aratasaurus museunacionali. Advanced techniques identified iron-containing heme and collagen, suggesting biological materials survived long periods. Researchers believe rapid burial in low-oxygen conditions contributed to preservation. This discovery opens new avenues for understanding dinosaur biology beyond skeletal remains.

stories.title: Archaeologists studying an ancient Spanish copper mine uncovered stone tools and new evidence of Bronze Age production; the findings suggest metal from Iberia may have travelled as far north as Scandinavia
stories.summary: Archaeologists conducted a thorough investigation of Las Minillas, an ancient copper mine in southern Spain, revealing its historical impact. Over 700 stone tools and pottery shards were found, pinpointing extensive activity from 1300 to 700 BC. This research indicates that the copper mined here likely reached Scandinavia through trade networks, showcasing the interconnectedness of Bronze Age communities across Europe.

stories.title: Another attack on Iran soon? Trump meets top security advisers after midterm elections
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump held meetings to evaluate potential military operations against Iran's nuclear program. While considering various options, Trump indicated that decisions would be made soon regarding escalating military action. The US Central Command is preparing for possible renewed combat operations in the region, coinciding with the new moon conditions. Iranian officials have communicated their conditions for negotiations to international partners, seeking confidence-building measures.

stories.title: 'Long road ahead': Eisenkot beats Netanyahu 67-46 in backing but govt test looms
NCP's Praful Patel visits Sharad Pawar in hospital amid reported discontent with Sunetra
'No impact on India-US ties': Tharoor says Trump retains power on tariffs, Iran war
Trump team stands firm: Rubio rules out exit, Hegseth gets president's backing
stories.summary: Marco Rubio has dismissed rumors about potentially leaving his position in the Trump administration. He asserts that completing Trump's second term has always been his plan. While he supports Vice President JD Vance for a future presidential run, Rubio avoids discussing his ambitions. Reports regarding a possible exit have been rejected by the White House and the State Department.

stories.title: 'Vote red today!' Elon Musk deletes pro-Republican posts after spending $458 million
stories.summary: Elon Musk removed social media posts encouraging support for Republican candidates after Democrats achieved significant victories. His pinned message included a call to vote Republican on Election Day. Musk’s financial backing totaled around $458 million, making him a significant donor during the election cycle. The election results also caused a decline in Musk's personal wealth and the stock values of his companies.

stories.title: 'Rahul's offer to debate still stands': Tharoor challenges BJP amid SIR, vote theft row
'You'll know soon enough': Trump's warning on 'destroying' rest of Iran
stories.summary: During a press conference at the Oval Office, Donald Trump cautioned Iran regarding its nuclear ambitions, hinting at possible future actions while preferring to avoid escalation. He asserted that Iran must seek US approval for any developments in its nuclear program, showcasing America's ongoing influence. These statements highlight the escalating tensions and complex dynamics between the two nations.

stories.title: It's all about the Raman effect: From Transparent Chennai to City of Angels
Centre takes over 39.5 acres of land housing IAF’s sports complex at Race Course
Oregon court now upholds $810,000 award over 2018 tree clearing beyond a neighbour's property line
stories.summary: In an Oregon land dispute, a property owner accused their neighbor of intentionally clearing land past established boundaries. A jury sided with the plaintiff, awarding them $810,000 in damages. The court upheld this decision, indicating that the defendants failed to provide valid evidence to counter their liability, while also noting that Bosma was aware of the boundary issues before the clearing took place.

stories.title: Julia Child Home Sells: former Cambridge house fetches $6.525 million; kitchen lives on at Smithsonian
stories.summary: Julia Child’s iconic home in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has found a new owner for $6.525 million. This historic residence, adored for its connection to Child's culinary shows, has seen extensive renovations. The original kitchen, however, remains untouched and is now a cherished exhibit at the Smithsonian Museum. To honor her legacy, a commemorative plaque is set to be installed at the site, ensuring that Child's influence on cooking continues.

stories.title: US wildlife teams surveyed six offshore islands for invasive species, finding rats on five and iguanas on one; the results will guide future work to protect nesting seabirds
stories.summary: Recent surveys in the U.S. Virgin Islands have identified invasive species on several offshore cays. Black rats and green iguanas pose significant threats to local seabird populations, such as the red-billed tropicbird. Conservationists are now evaluating strategies to eradicate these non-native animals from the islands. Removal efforts could lead to improved nesting conditions for seabirds in the future. Successful initiatives may help restore these vital habitats for future generations.

stories.title: Day after militants killing, Manipur launches search and cordon operations
Opposition planning unrest, says BJP after TV channel sting
Youth Cong suspends 300 for no-show at Rahul's Delhi rally
Georgia court upholds waste facility permit as 97 planned townhomes still unbuilt at permit filing
stories.summary: A developer in Bartow County, Georgia challenged a permit for a nearby waste processing facility. The county approved the permit despite concerns that it violated zoning restrictions. The developer argued that their planned townhomes should receive protection under existing zoning laws. However, the court found that the definitions of residential dwellings applied only to already constructed buildings. Ultimately, the appeals court upheld the permit, allowing the waste facility to operate.

stories.title: Special summary roll revision in 6 states, UTs; draft on Nov 30
Luke Bryan's Farm Tour awards 97 college scholarships and helps provide 11 million meals since 2009
stories.summary: Since its inception in 2009, Luke Bryan's Farm Tour has championed educational opportunities by awarding 97 scholarships and supplying over 11 million meals for needy families. Partnering with Bayer’s #HerestotheFarmer campaign, the initiative bridges support between farming families and communities. Attendees also donated nearly 20,000 pounds of food to hunger-relief efforts, underscoring a commitment to enhancing education and food accessibility in agricultural areas nationwide.

stories.title: She runs a Caribbean takeaway in England and gives free meals to people who cannot afford them; 71-year-old Florence ‘Mama Flo’ Coke has become a local hero.
stories.summary: Florence Coke runs a Caribbean takeaway in Stockport, where she offers free meals for the needy. She has been inspired by her parents' tradition of helping the poor in Jamaica. During the COVID-19 crisis, she continued to feed struggling families with free meals and food parcels. Recently, she was recognized with a Local Hero award for her community service efforts.

stories.title: EC rejigs work, new officer to oversee ECINet functioning
Party after gun buy ends in a death
Firecrackers stored in house explode, kill 1
Mulling panel to review UGC equity norms: Government
Government buys time on UGC rules without committing to withdrawal or retention
Umar, Sharjeel move SC for bail
Bodies of 5 missing fishermen wash ashore
4 die as car plunges into Bhagirathi
24-hour deadline starts with detention: SC
Washington court upholds deal after couple split again, leaving wife without bank and stock assets
stories.summary: A couple from Washington navigated a messy divorce settlement only to remarry, before the cycle of separation began once more. The court upheld an arbitration ruling that favored William Gibbs, denying Joy the assets previously awarded. Although Joy retained some funds from her BNY Mellon 401(k), she forfeited half of the USAA accounts and restricted stock units.

stories.title: Texas Farm Funds Scholarships: Donated land backs Gruver High students; many are first-generation grads
stories.summary: In Gruver, Texas, a remarkable farming initiative has turned inherited land into a thriving source of scholarship funds for local students. By pooling their resources, farmers and community members cultivate crops that have raised around $3 million for education since 2012, benefitting nearly 300 students, including first-generation college graduates like Sydney Ortiz and Rhett Sparks.

stories.title: ‘I guess I’m dead’: Tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson's chilling post resurfaces
stories.summary: In a heartbreaking incident, tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson and his family lost their lives in a Florida plane crash on November 1, 2026. The tragedy claimed all nine individuals aboard the private jet. Robinson, known for his sarcastic social media presence, previously founded notable marketing technology companies. The National Transportation Safety Board has initiated an investigation into the cause of the fatal accident.

stories.title: Former Maoist-controlled forest area turns into cockfight gambling den
Minister alleges foreign funding, CJP counters
‘Speedy trial is a fundamental right’: SC says Constitution has primacy over special laws
Cops to give 7-day notice to Akoijam before action
Pennsylvania court upholds borough's duty to maintain steps after 130 years of public use
stories.summary: A couple from Jim Thorpe filed a lawsuit against their borough regarding the maintenance of public steps. They argued that the borough had historically maintained the steps, which had been used for over 130 years. The Commonwealth Court upheld the lower court's ruling that affirmed the borough's maintenance obligation. Evidence included historical records showing the borough's involvement in repairs and maintenance over the years.

stories.title: A British family doctor was convicted of murdering 15 patients
stories.summary: Harold Shipman, a general practitioner in England, was infamously convicted for the murder of numerous patients. His reputation as a trusted doctor gave him unfettered access to the homes of vulnerable elderly individuals, leading to a devastating series of crimes. An extensive investigation later uncovered that Shipman was linked to the deaths of at least 215 people over many years.

stories.title: Christopher Plummer's widow donates land for 750-acre nature preserve
California court allows grandfather five-minute monthly calls, rejects mother's $17,193 fee bid
stories.summary: Timothy S sought court-ordered visitation with his granddaughter after Sarah H regained custody of the children. He had raised the older child for nearly two years prior to this change in custody. The trial court allowed only a brief monthly telephone call while denying Sarah's request for legal fees tied to the case. California's Court of Appeal upheld this decision, affirming the lower court's interpretation of the law.

stories.title: Jen Lilley revives Christmas Is Not Cancelled toy drive for kids
stories.summary: Jen Lilley, the acclaimed actress, has relaunched her Christmas Is Not Cancelled campaign to aid children in need, setting a goal of delivering 20,000 gifts to underprivileged youth this Christmas. By letting parents select the gifts, the initiative preserves their dignity. Furthermore, podcaster Shawn Ryan's generous $30,000 donation will provide bikes and scooters. The campaign is now a nonprofit, making financial contributions tax-deductible.

stories.title: NASA's Hubble studied dwarf galaxies and found they kept just 11% of the oxygen made by their stars
stories.summary: A recent investigation revealed that dwarf galaxies only retain an average of 11% of the oxygen generated by their stars. The remaining oxygen likely escapes into space during powerful supernova explosions. This finding indicates that smaller galaxies have greater difficulty retaining their materials than previously believed. Researchers plan to conduct further studies to examine where this missing oxygen ultimately ends up.

Kashmir has 1 active local terrorist, says IG
Iraq airspace available again, Air India flights between Delhi, Mumbai and New York become nonstop; shave 4 hours off from Rome one-stops
Lee Miller’s son gifted her former home to charity to preserve her legacy
Hadid sisters' childhood Malibu mansion land sells for $6.5 million
Arizona appeals court upholds divorce asset division
stories.summary: An Arizona couple, married in 2016, built three businesses before filing for divorce in 2023. During the divorce, the husband disputed a business valuation and claimed loans as marital debt. The court found his loan documentation lacking credibility and upheld a valuation of $305,800. After a trial, the court awarded businesses to the wife and denied the husband's claims about wasted funds.

stories.title: Two brothers find ultra-rare Tom Brady card in $30 box
stories.summary: Lucas and Trevor Martell bought three boxes of sports cards and discovered a rare one-of-one card. The card features Tom Brady and could be worth over $150,000. This unexpected find has significantly impacted their financial situation and future plans. Lucas intends to pay off medical bills and help his grandmother using the potential earnings. The brothers also plan to start their own trading card business together for the future.

stories.title: US study finds eating one avocado & mango every day improves blood vessel function in prediabetic adults
stories.summary: A new research study indicates that integrating mango and avocado into your daily diet may significantly improve heart health. Focused on adults with prediabetes, this study monitored the effects of these fruits over eight weeks with controlled calorie intake. Results showed enhanced blood vessel performance and lowered blood pressure in male participants, highlighting the cardiovascular advantages of incorporating these nutritious fruits into your meals.

stories.title: Drummer Lars Ulrich sells San Francisco mansions for nearly $68 million
Lady Gaga’s foundation gives $100,000 to Atlanta youth organisation
Florida's giant Burmese pythons may be spreading seeds, reshaping the Everglades
Up to 10-fold statutory costs, month-long delays: Report flags hurdles in used vehicle transfers
Montana Supreme Court awards husband $955,000 home despite property being in wife's name
stories.summary: In a contentious property dispute in Montana, a couple found themselves at odds after their marriage dissolved. The husband poured approximately $955,000 into their shared home, though it was registered solely in the wife's name. Ultimately, the Montana Supreme Court favored the husband, underscoring the significance of financial contributions over title ownership in divorce settlements.

stories.title: Backyard Railway Village: Chicago family turns garden into miniature town; hobby draws visitors
stories.summary: Over two decades, a Chicago family's backyard has transformed into a vibrant miniature railway town. What began as a modest garden endeavor blossomed into a captivating landscape filled with elaborate buildings and model trains. Despite initial worries about sacrificing garden space, family members embraced the hobby, turning their yard into a destination for train enthusiasts, while inspiring younger generations to explore the joys of model railroading.

stories.title: ‘Expect new dynamics’: Ukraine hopes for more support after Democrats sweep midterms
stories.summary: Ukraine anticipates enhanced military and financial assistance from the United States after the midterm elections. Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha expressed hope for new dynamics and support from the incoming Democratic majority. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy acknowledged the Democrats' vocal backing of Ukraine since their election success. This shift in power could enable legislation favoring aid to Ukraine despite previous limitations.

stories.title: Wife smears faeces in husband's mouth after threatening to make him eat it; gets suspended jail term
stories.summary: A 63-year-old woman in the UK has received a suspended prison sentence after smearing faeces into her husband's mouth during an argument at their £1 million farmhouse. Alison Moore had threatened to make him eat it before carrying out the attack. The judge described the act as a 'gratuitous degradation' of the victim.

stories.title: Louisiana court upholds a trust protector's powers to change beneficiaries and approve early closure
stories.summary: A Louisiana appeals court upheld a trust protector's authority to change future beneficiaries and require approval before a trust could be ended early. The case involved a trust created by a stepfather for his stepson in 2004. The stepson challenged the powers given to his stepbrother, but the court upheld the lower court's decision.

stories.title: Temporary move: No slots next summer for 12 int’l carriers at CSMIA; can operate from Navi Mumbai
Vance lances Trump as MAGA enters week of the long knives
3 injured in shooting at US post office in Iowa, suspect detained
Arkansas man loses challenge to sale of ex-wife's share of their jointly owned land
stories.summary: A couple bought land together in Arkansas in 2021 but divorced within a year, retaining equal ownership. After the woman filed for bankruptcy in 2023, a trustee sold her share to an investment company. Her former husband challenged the sale, but the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit dismissed his appeal because he had not challenged the buyer's good faith before the bankruptcy court.

stories.title: Kim Kardashian’s former mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed, listed for $8.5 million after makeover
stories.summary: Kim Kardashian’s former Beverly Hills mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed to her on camera in 2011, is heading to the market for nearly $8.5 million after an extensive makeover. Kim bought the property for $3.4 million in 2010 and sold it for $3.6 million in 2013. The five-bedroom estate now boasts luxurious modern interiors.

stories.title: Washington court broadens rules on divorce legal fees
stories.summary: Washington's Court of Appeals ruled that trial courts can award legal fees despite prenuptial agreements. This decision allows judges to consider broader divorce aspects for fee awards. In the case reviewed, a wealthy husband was ordered to pay his wife's legal costs. The trial court is to reassess the specific fee awards granted to the wife.

stories.title: Once homeless himself, he is on a mission to end food insecurity
stories.summary: Dion Dawson founded Dion's Chicago Dream in 2020 to provide fresh produce to families facing food insecurity. After experiencing homelessness and food scarcity, he aimed to improve food distribution methods. The non-profit now delivers 80,000 pounds of fresh produce weekly to over 5,400 households. Paid staff members maintain a steady workforce while providing dignity to recipients through efficient service.

stories.title: He survived Hiroshima, returned home to Nagasaki and was hit by a second atomic bomb three days later: The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi
stories.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a survivor of both atomic bombings, faced immense physical and emotional trauma from his experiences. Initially reluctant to share his story, he eventually became an advocate for a world free of nuclear weapons. His journey from hibakusha to spokesperson illustrates the lasting impact of nuclear warfare on individuals and communities.

stories.title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition
stories.summary: Three significant works from India's literary heritage have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register. Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata', and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' received this recognition recently. These inscriptions reflect various aspects of India's intellectual traditions, including historical writing and governance. This announcement follows India's previous regional register recognitions in 2024 for other literary works. The initiative aims to preserve and digitise India's manuscript heritage for future generations.

stories.title: Student union representatives from 7 states join ABVP rally at Delhi University
Cabinet approves Rs 14,500 crore VGF scheme for energy storage
Mizoram: CRPF constable shoots self dead while on duty at governor's residence
Aadhaar verification goes paperless as UIDAI brings 300 entities on board
Oversight layer intact, says EC official after poll panel tweaks work order for IT chief Seema Khanna
'Sitting in palace, watching soldiers fight': Chirag Paswan's dig at Akhilesh Yadav over UP polls remark
Evening newswrap: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement; Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to face-off in Parliament over SIR, and more
Delhi riots case: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam challenge Delhi HC's bail refusal in Supreme Court
stories.summary: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have filed for bail in the Supreme Court concerning the Delhi riots case. They contend that the prosecution has failed to call any witnesses during their extensive period of detention. The activists pointed out the looming deadline for submitting new bail applications as established by the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Centre amends Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order: What Indians travelling to or returning from Nepal or Bhutan need to know
Eight Lakshmis, 1.4 billion oceans: Aruna Lohia Goenka's vision of an awakened Bharat
Indian Medical Association wants CBFC to refuse certification to Sunny Deol film ‘Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak’
stories.summary: The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.

stories.title: Hardeep Singh Puri elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Hardeep Singh Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh after other candidates failed to qualify. The nominations of Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected for not meeting necessary requirements. Puri's election follows the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan in mid-October. Hemant Khandelwal, among other officials, was present when Puri collected his election certificate.

stories.title: Toronto woman turns 2013 meal project into food charity 5N2
Rahul Gandhi gets relief as Allahabad HC rejects plea seeking FIR over remarks on Sikh community
Mid-air chaos: Multiple flights in Europe diverted due to bomb threats
Scottish rescuer fights to keep badger cub he says cannot survive in the wild
‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
stories.summary: Sheikh Hasina has confirmed her intention to return to Bangladesh, despite facing a death sentence. The former Prime Minister is aware of the risks associated with her return, including potential arrest or worse. Hasina's Awami League party has been banned, resulting in widespread political repression and violence against its members. She expressed concerns over the rising influence of extremist groups in the current political climate.

stories.title: US midterm fallout: Trump's India envoy Sergio Gor may replace Marco Rubio - report
Classroom to billion-dollar fortune: How Chinese siblings struck gold in the stock market
stories.summary: Michael Mai and his sister, Mai Huixia, reached billionaire status following the public debut of Crown New Materials Technology on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, where shares surged nearly eightfold in just one day. This company, known for producing adhesives for major clients like Tesla and Apple, prompted a call for rational investment behavior amidst recent challenges and government interventions in China's stock market.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar violence: SC gives panel 1 month to file report, flags lack of complaints
US woman says co-op staff took her pets, hid dog's whereabouts; court allows lawsuit
stories.summary: A New York woman who accused co-op employees of entering her apartment without permission, removing her dog and cat, and concealing her dog's whereabouts can continue pursuing two legal claims. Nearly three years after the incident, an appeals court allowed her trespass and emotional distress claims to proceed. Court records indicated that her dog was euthanised after spending nearly two months at a shelter.

stories.title: Small Listing Spurs Protection: Indiana saves 3,950 acres; new wildlife area opens
stories.summary: An effort to save a 191-acre parcel in Indiana led to the protection of nearly 4,000 acres. The land was acquired to prevent fragmentation and protect wildlife habitats in the area. Various organizations and public agencies collaborated to complete the acquisition. The Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area opened to the public in April 2025 for outdoor recreation.

stories.title: Titanic's owners received $5 million within 30 days of the sinking; 114 years later, original insurance certificate resurfaces and could sell for $67,000
stories.summary: An authentic insurance document related to the Titanic's last journey is slated for auction in Britain. This significant paperwork details the insurance sought mere weeks before the 1912 sinking. The owners received their payout shortly after the tragedy, contrasting sharply with the delays faced by bereaved families. The piece also underscores the important insurance arrangements for the Titanic, along with a selection of other artifacts that commemorate its storied past.

stories.title: Youth Congress suspends 200 office-bearers across 7 states for skipping INDIA bloc anti-CEC rally
'Contemplating to appoint a committee': Centre to SC on UGC's equity rules
Russell Brand Trial: Jury weighs seven sexual offence charges; deliberations to resume Wednesday
stories.summary: Jury discussions are now underway regarding comedian Russell Brand's sexual offences trial at Southwark Crown Court. Faced with multiple charges from six women about occurrences between 1999 and 2009, the prosecution argues that Brand leveraged his celebrity status for sexual manipulation. In his defense, Brand asserts that all encounters were consensual and refutes the allegations.

stories.title: David Bowie performed here, Carlos Sainz raced go-karts: Madrid's iconic La Ermita mall demolished for 529 homes in €77 million makeover
stories.summary: The once-thriving La Ermita shopping centre in Madrid has met its end as plans to demolish it progress. In its place, a new development will rise, offering 529 homes, a blend of accessible and protected housing. This initiative aims to enhance local infrastructure, incorporating public spaces and green zones for the community.

stories.title: EC announces electoral roll revision in 6 states, UTs; final rolls on Jan 21
Australia launches A$28 million project to stop invasive cane toads from reaching Pilbara after 1935 introduction
stories.summary: A new project involving Curtin University and Rio Tinto seeks to establish a waterless barrier for cane toads. The initiative intends to protect Western Australia's Pilbara area from the ecologically damaging species. Researchers plan to modify water sources over a significant area to prevent the toads' survival. Traditional Owners have been engaged throughout the project to ensure cultural significance is respected.

stories.title: Jimmy Buffett's $275 million family trust becomes a legal battleground
Did Russia rehearse satellite attack? Expert on close encounter with western spacecraft
stories.summary: A Russian military satellite's recent close encounter with a commercial satellite has sparked serious concerns about security in space. Experts are alarmed, suggesting this action may signal an escalation towards targeting satellites linked to military operations. US officials have warned that these provocative moves could jeopardize commercial satellite networks, further fueling the existing geopolitical tensions and prompting analysts to rigorously track Russian movements in the sky.

stories.summary: A High Court judge ruled that specific assets of the deceased were legitimate gifts received by Masudur Rahman before death, dating back to October 2020. stories.summary: A couple from Tennessee faced a setback as their claim over a strip of land beside their house was overturned by the court. stories.summary: Olivia Newton-John owned a country estate in Australia that she transformed over nearly four decades. This property included natural features and a significant amount of wildlife habitat that she developed. After battling cancer, the estate was sold in 2019 for $4.6 million, reflecting changes in her priorities. Newton-John's connection to the area continued through her involvement with a wellness retreat she co-founded.

stories.title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
Stephen Curry-backed golf teams make history with women's first NEC title and men's third win
stories.summary: Howard University's golf program reached new heights when both men's and women's teams won their conference championships. The women's team claimed its first-ever Northeast Conference title in April 2026. Just days later, the men's team secured its third consecutive NEC championship victory. The successes highlighted the growth of the program, supported by NBA star Stephen Curry's funding.

stories.title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Nebraska court rejects handwritten will signed by man but written largely by his longtime partner
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, Nebraska's Supreme Court declared a handwritten will invalid, stating that the primary handwriting was not that of the testator. The court reaffirmed the original 1984 will, which allocated assets to the deceased's sons. This decision underlined the necessity for a holographic will to be solely in the writer's hand to clarify testamentary intent, especially amid disputes from a long-term partner after Douglas G. Todd's death.

stories.title: Maryland court orders new trial over $3.2 million trust after sisters challenge inheritance
stories.summary: A Maryland appeals court has mandated a new trial concerning a $3.2 million trust fund held by three sisters. The court identified procedural errors that prevented two sisters from presenting crucial handwriting evidence regarding the trust. Their claims included accusations of undue influence exerted by their sister, the main beneficiary. The appeals court emphasized issues with the previous trial's allowed testimonies and evidence exclusions.

Paul McCartney-backed Liverpool arts institute celebrates 400+ graduates 30 years on
stories.summary: The LIPA held its 2026 graduation ceremony celebrating its 30th anniversary by awarding degrees to its very first graduates. With over 400 students from 28 different countries in attendance, this event marked a monumental occasion. Sir Paul McCartney was on hand to honor five notable figures for their artistry and impact on the cultural landscape, showcasing LIPA's commitment to nurturing creative talent across various fields, including music, theatre, and film.

First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
stories.summary: CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. The milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide.

stories.title: 'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
stories.summary: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

stories.title: 'Surge in popularity after reality show': Tej Pratap Yadav asks for enhanced security from Centre
stories.summary: In a post on X, Yadav said his recent appearance on a reality show had increased his popularity, with large numbers of people approaching him in public places to take photographs. He said the crowds posed a risk not only to him but also to the lone security personnel currently assigned to him.
